Managing Conformance Packs for AWS Config Across all Accounts in Your Organization

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage its AWS accounts. The company recently acquired another company with standalone AWS accounts. The acquiring company's DevOps team must consolidate administration of the AWS accounts for both companies while retaining full administrative control of the accounts. The DevOps team must also collect and group findings across every account to implement and maintain a security posture. Which combination of steps should the DevOps team take to meet these requirements?
options: A. Invite the acquired company's AWS accounts to join the organization. Create an SCP that has full administrative privileges. Attach the SCP to the management account.

B. Invite the acquired company's AWS accounts to join the organization. Create the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the invited accounts. Grant permission to the management account to assume the role.
C. Use AWS Security Hub to collect and group findings across all accounts. Use Security Hub to automatically detect new accounts as the accounts are added to the organization.

D. Use AWS Firewall Manager to collect and group findings across all accounts. Enable all features for the organization. Designate an account in the organization as the delegated administrator account for Firewall Manager.
E. Use Amazon Inspector to collect and group findings across all accounts. Designate an account in the organization as the delegated administrator account for Amazon Inspector.
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations does not automatically create OrganizationAccountAccessRole for an existing account that is invited into an organization. Creating that role in each invited account, granting it administrative permissions, and permitting principals in the management account to assume it provides centralized administrative access. AWS Security Hub aggregates and normalizes security findings across member accounts; its organization integration can automatically add and enable accounts as they join the organization. LEARN MORE Creating OrganizationAccountAccessRole for an invited account with AWS Organizations Automatically enabling Security Hub CSPM in new organization accounts

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization managed jointly by a security team and a DevOps team. Both teams access the accounts through AWS IAM Identity Center. A separate group exists for each team. The DevOps team's group is assigned a permission set named DevOps. The permission set has the AdministratorAccess managed IAM policy attached and is applied to every account in the organization. The security team needs to ensure that the DevOps team cannot access IAM Identity Center in the organization's management account. The security team attached the following SCP to the organization root: After the policy is implemented, the security team finds that the DevOps team can still access IAM Identity Center. Which solution fixes the problem?
options: A. In the organization's management account, create a new OU. Move the organization's management account to the new OU. Detach the SCP from the organization root. Attach the SCP to the new OU.
B. In the organization's management account, update the SCP condition reference to the ARN of the DevOps team's group role to include the AWS account ID of the organization's management account.

C. In IAM Identity Center, create a new permission set. Ensure that the assigned policy has full access but explicitly denies permission for the sso:* action and the sso-directory:* action. Update the assigned permission set for the DevOps team's group role in the organization's management account. Delete the SCP.

D. In IAM Identity Center, update the DevOps permission set. Ensure that the assigned policy has full access but explicitly denies permission for the sso:* action and the sso-directory:* action. In the Deny statement, add a StringEquals condition that compares the aws:SourceAccount global condition context key with the organization's management account IDelete the SCP.
questions.explanation: Service control policies affect only member accounts and do not restrict IAM users or roles in an AWS Organizations management account. An explicit Deny for sso:* and sso-directory:* in the IAM Identity Center permission set policy is attached to the IAM role provisioned in the management account and overrides the AdministratorAccess allow, preventing the DevOps role from accessing IAM Identity Center there. LEARN MORE Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations Create a permission set - AWS IAM Identity Center

Create a permission set - AWS IAM Identity Center

questions.questionText: A company uses an Amazon Aurora cluster as its application's data store. The Aurora cluster has a single DB instance configured. The application uses the cluster's instance endpoint to perform database read and write operations. The company has planned an update for the cluster during an upcoming maintenance window. The cluster must stay available with the minimum possible interruption during that maintenance window. What should a DevOps engineer do to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Add a reader instance to the Aurora cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster endpoint for write operations. Update the Aurora cluster's reader endpoint for reads.
B. Add a reader instance to the Aurora cluster. Create a custom ANY endpoint for the cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster's custom ANY endpoint for read and write operations.
C. Turn on the Multi-AZ option on the Aurora cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster endpoint for write operations. Update the Aurora cluster’s reader endpoint for reads.

D. Turn on the Multi-AZ option on the Aurora cluster. Create a custom ANY endpoint for the cluster. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster's custom ANY endpoint for read and write operations
questions.explanation: Adding an Aurora reader instance gives the cluster an available replica that Aurora can promote to the primary instance during a failover. The Aurora cluster endpoint is the writer endpoint and automatically directs read/write connections to the current primary after promotion, minimizing interruption. The reader endpoint load-balances read-only connections across Aurora Replicas, so reads should use that endpoint. An ANY custom endpoint can route connections to reader instances and therefore cannot safely serve mixed write traffic. LEARN MORE Cluster endpoints for Amazon Aurora Reader endpoints for Amazon Aurora
learnMore: Cluster endpoints for Amazon Aurora
Reader endpoints for Amazon Aurora

questions.questionText: A highly regulated company has a policy that DevOps engineers must not log in to its Amazon EC2 instances except during emergencies. If a DevOps engineer does log in, the security team must receive notification within 15 minutes of the event. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Install the Amazon Inspector agent on each EC2 instance. Subscribe to Amazon EventBridge notifications. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to check if a message is about user logins. If it is, send a notification to the security team using Amazon SNS.

B. Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on each EC2 instance. Configure the agent to push all logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs and set up a CloudWatch metric filter that searches for user logins. If a login is found, send a notification to the security team using Amazon SNS.

C. Set up AWS CloudTrail with Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Subscribe CloudWatch Logs to Amazon Kinesis. Attach AWS Lambda to Kinesis to parse and determine if a log contains a user login. If it does, send a notification to the security team using Amazon SNS.

D. Set up a script on each Amazon EC2 instance to push all logs to Amazon S3. Set up an S3 event to invoke an AWS Lambda function, which invokes an Amazon Athena query to run. The Athena query checks for logins and sends the output to the security team using Amazon SNS.
questions.explanation: The CloudWatch agent can collect operating-system authentication logs from EC2 instances and publish them to CloudWatch Logs. A CloudWatch Logs metric filter can detect login entries and produce a metric; a CloudWatch alarm on that metric can notify the security team through Amazon SNS within the required period. LEARN MORE Collect metrics, logs, and traces using the CloudWatch agent Creating metrics from log events using filters

questions.questionText: A company plans to create a pipeline that updates its standard AMI every month. The AMI must use the latest patches so that newly launched Amazon EC2 instances remain current. Each new AMI must be available to every AWS account in the company’s AWS Organizations organization. The company must configure an automated pipeline to build the AMI. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses AWS CodeBuild. Create an AWS Lambda function to run the pipeline every month. Create an AWS CloudFormation template. Share the template with all AWS accounts in the organization.
B. Create an AMI pipeline by using EC2 Image Builder. Configure the pipeline to distribute the AMI to the AWS accounts in the organization. Configure the pipeline to run monthly.

C. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that runs an AWS Lambda function to build the AMI. Configure the pipeline to share the AMI with the AWS accounts in the organization. Configure Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to invoke the pipeline every month.
D. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Configure the automation to run in all AWS accounts in the organization. Create an AWS Lambda function to run the automation every month.
questions.explanation: EC2 Image Builder provides managed AMI build pipelines with scheduled execution, enabling a monthly build that incorporates current patches. Its distribution settings can automatically share each output AMI with specified AWS accounts, AWS Organizations, or organizational units. This directly satisfies the recurring build and organization-wide availability requirements without maintaining custom orchestration components. LEARN MORE Manage Image Builder distribution settings Configure pipeline execution settings for image pipelines

Configure pipeline execution settings for image pipelines

questions.questionText: A company operates a web application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company uses Amazon CloudFront to distribute the application and recently enabled AWS WAF. The company configured Amazon CloudWatch Logs to send logs to an aws-waf-logs log group. The company needs a DevOps engineer to receive alerts when blocked traffic changes suddenly. The company does not want alerts for other changes in AWS WAF log behavior. The company will tune AWS WAF rules over time. The DevOps engineer is already subscribed to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in the environment. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a CloudWatch Logs metrics filter for blocked requests on the AWS WAF log group to create a custom metric. Create a CloudWatch alarm by using CloudWatch anomaly detection and the published custom metric. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.

B. Create a CloudWatch anomaly detector for the log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm by using metrics that the CloudWatch anomaly detector publishes. Use the high setting for the LogAnomalyPriority metric. Configure the alarm to go into alarm state if a static threshold of one anomaly is detected. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.

C. Create a CloudWatch metrics filter for counted requests on the AWS WAF log group to create a custom metric. Create a CloudWatch alarm that activates when the sum of blocked requests in the custom metric during a period of 1 hour is greater than a static estimate for the acceptable number of blocked requests in 1 hour. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.

D. Create a CloudWatch anomaly detector for the log group. Create a CloudWatch alarm by using metrics that the CloudWatch anomaly detector publishes. Use the medium setting for the LogAnomalyPriority metric. Configure the alarm to go into alarm state if a sum of anomalies over 1 hour is greater than an expected value. Configure the alarm to notify the SNS topic to alert the DevOps engineer.
questions.explanation: A metric filter that matches only blocked AWS WAF requests produces a metric limited to blocked-traffic volume. A CloudWatch anomaly-detection alarm learns the normal range of that metric and alerts when its value deviates unexpectedly, while adapting as normal blocked-request levels change due to WAF rule tuning. It avoids monitoring unrelated patterns or anomalies elsewhere in the WAF logs. LEARN MORE Creating metrics from log events using filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs Alarming on logs - Amazon CloudWatch
learnMore: Creating metrics from log events using filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
Alarming on logs - Amazon CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A company grants its employees limited AWS permissions. DevOps engineers can assume an administrator role. For auditing purposes, the security team needs a near-real-time notification whenever the administrator role is assumed. How should this be implemented?
options: A. Configure AWS Config to publish logs to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs and send a notification to the security team when the administrator role is assumed.
B. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor when the administrator role is assumed and send a notification to the security team.
C. Create an Amazon EventBridge event rule using an AWS Management Console sign-in events event pattern that publishes a message to an Amazon SNS topic if the administrator role is assumed.

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge events rule using an AWS API call that uses an AWS CloudTrail event pattern to invoke an AWS Lambda function that publishes a message to an Amazon SNS topic if the administrator role is assumed.
questions.explanation: AWS STS records a role assumption as an AssumeRole API event in AWS CloudTrail. An Amazon EventBridge rule can match AWS API Call via CloudTrail events, including the STS AssumeRole event and the administrator role ARN, then invoke a Lambda function to publish an Amazon SNS notification. This provides event-driven, near-real-time notification. Logging IAM and AWS STS API calls with AWS CloudTrail LEARN MORE Logging IAM and AWS STS API calls with AWS CloudTrail AWS CloudTrail events - Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A company has deployed a critical application across two AWS Regions. The application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in each Region. The company has Amazon Route 53 alias DNS records for both ALBs. The company uses Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to make sure that the application can fail over between the two Regions. The Route 53 ARC configuration contains a routing control for each Region. The company uses Route 53 ARC to conduct quarterly disaster recovery (DR) tests. During the latest DR test, a DevOps engineer inadvertently turned off both routing controls. The company must ensure that at least one routing control remains turned on at all times. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. In Route 53 ARC, create a new assertion safety rule. Apply the assertion safety rule to the two routing controls. Configure the rule with the ATLEAST type with a threshold of 1.
B. In Route 53 ARC, create a new gating safety rule. Apply the assertion safety rule to the two routing controls. Configure the rule with the OR type with a threshold of 1.

C. In Route 53 ARC, create a new resource set. Configure the resource set with an AWS::Route53::HealthCheck resource type. Specify the ARNs of the two routing controls as the target resource. Create a new readiness check for the resource set.

D. In Route 53 ARC, create a new resource set. Configure the resource set with an AWS::Route53RecoveryReadiness::DNSTargetResource resource type. Add the domain names of the two Route 53 alias DNS records as the target resource. Create a new readiness check for the resource set.
questions.explanation: A Route 53 ARC assertion safety rule prevents routing-control state updates unless its configured criterion is satisfied. Applying an ATLEAST assertion rule with a threshold of 1 to the two Regional routing controls prevents a transaction from leaving both controls Off, thereby ensuring that traffic can continue to be routed to at least one Region. LEARN MORE Creating safety rules for routing control — Amazon Route 53 ARC Set up routing control components — Amazon Route 53 ARC

questions.questionText: A company has an AWS CodePipeline pipeline configured with an Amazon S3 bucket in the eu-west-1 Region. The pipeline deploys an AWS Lambda application to that same Region. It includes an AWS CodeBuild project build action and an AWS CloudFormation deploy action. The CodeBuild project uses the aws cloudformation package AWS CLI command to create an artifact containing the Lambda function code .zip file and the CloudFormation template. The CloudFormation deploy action refers to the CloudFormation template in the output artifact from the CodeBuild project’s build action. The company wants to deploy the Lambda application to the us-east-1 Region as well, using the pipeline in eu-west-1. A DevOps engineer has already updated the CodeBuild project to use the aws cloudformation package command to generate an additional output artifact for us-east-1. Which combination of additional steps should the DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements?
options: A. Modify the CloudFormation template to include a parameter for the Lambda function code’s zip file location. Create a new CloudFormation deploy action for us-east-1 in the pipeline. Configure the new deploy action to pass in the us-east-1 artifact location as a parameter override.
B. Create a new CloudFormation deploy action for us-east-1 in the pipeline. Configure the new deploy action to use the CloudFormation template from the us-east-1 output artifact.
C. Create an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure the S3 bucket policy to allow CodePipeline to have read and write access.
D. Create an S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the S3 bucket in eu-west-1 to the S3 bucket in us-east-1.

E. Modify the pipeline to include the S3 bucket for us-east-1 as an artifact store. Create a new CloudFormation deploy action for us-east-1 in the pipeline. Configure the new deploy action to use the CloudFormation template from the us-east-1 output artifact.
questions.explanation: CodePipeline requires an S3 artifact store in the pipeline Region and in each Region where it executes a cross-Region action. A us-east-1 bucket must therefore be created and configured for CodePipeline access, and the pipeline must include it as the us-east-1 artifact store. The CloudFormation deploy action in us-east-1 should use the us-east-1 packaged output artifact. CodePipeline handles copying artifacts between its configured regional artifact stores, so S3 Cross-Region Replication is not required. LEARN MORE Add a cross-Region action in CodePipeline AWS::CodePipeline::Pipeline ArtifactStoreMap

questions.questionText: A company is testing a web application that runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones. The company uses a blue/green deployment process with immutable instances to deploy new software. During testing, users are automatically logged out of the application at random times. Testers also report that all users are logged out when a new application version is deployed. The development team needs a solution that ensures users stay logged in through scaling events and application deployments. What is the MOST operationally efficient way to ensure users remain logged in?
options: A. Enable smart sessions on the load balancer and modify the application to check for an existing session.
B. Enable session sharing on the load balancer and modify the application to read from the session store.
C. Store user session information in an Amazon S3 bucket and modify the application to read session information from the bucket.
D. Modify the application to store user session information in an Amazon ElastiCache cluster.
questions.explanation: Application session state must be stored outside the ephemeral EC2 instances so that every instance, including instances introduced during Auto Scaling or immutable blue/green deployments, can retrieve the same session. An Amazon ElastiCache cluster provides a shared, low-latency session store. Application Load Balancer stickiness only maintains affinity to a specific target and cannot preserve a session after that target is replaced. LEARN MORE Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute incoming application traffic in your Auto Scaling group

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer operates a web application running on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are in an EC2 Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones. The engineer must implement a deployment strategy that: Launches a second instance fleet with the same capacity as the original fleet. Leaves the original fleet unchanged while the second fleet launches. Shifts traffic to the second fleet after it is fully deployed. Automatically terminates the original fleet 1 hour after the transition. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use an AWS CloudFormation template with a retention policy for the ALB set to 1 hour. Update the Amazon Route 53 record to reflect the new ALB.

B. Use two AWS Elastic Beanstalk environments to perform a blue/green deployment from the original environment to the new one. Create an application version lifecycle policy to terminate the original environment in 1 hour.

C. Use AWS CodeDeploy with a deployment group configured with a blue/green deployment configuration Select the option Terminate the original instances in the deployment group with a waiting period of 1 hour.
D. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk with the configuration set to Immutable. Create an .ebextension using the Resources key that sets the deletion policy of the ALB to 1 hour, and deploy the application.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployments for EC2 can automatically copy an EC2 Auto Scaling group to provision a replacement fleet. After the replacement instances are deployed, CodeDeploy reroutes load-balancer traffic to them and can terminate the original instances after a configured waiting period of 1 hour. LEARN MORE Create an application for a blue/green deployment (console) - AWS CodeDeploy
learnMore: Create an application for a blue/green deployment (console) - AWS CodeDeploy

questions.questionText: A company operates a web application across multiple Availability Zones. The company uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) for routing, AWS Fargate for the application, and Amazon Aurora for the application data. The company uses AWS CloudFormation templates to deploy the application. All Docker images are stored in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository in the same AWS account and AWS Region. A DevOps engineer must establish a disaster recovery (DR) process in another Region. The solution must meet an RPO of 8 hours and an RTO of 2 hours. The company occasionally requires more than 2 hours to build the Docker images from the Dockerfile. Which solution will meet the RTO and RPO requirements MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Copy the CloudFormation templates and the Dockerfile to an Amazon S3 bucket in the DR Region. Use AWS Backup to configure automated Aurora cross-Region hourly snapshots. In case of DR, build the most recent Docker image and upload the Docker image to an ECR repository in the DR Region. Use the CloudFormation template that has the most recent Aurora snapshot and the Docker image from the ECR repository to launch a new CloudFormation stack in the DR Region. Update the application DNS records to point to the new ALB.

B. Copy the CloudFormation templates to an Amazon S3 bucket in the DR Region. Configure Aurora automated backup Cross-Region Replication. Configure ECR Cross-Region Replication. In case of DR, use the CloudFormation template with the most recent Aurora snapshot and the Docker image from the local ECR repository to launch a new CloudFormation stack in the DR Region. Update the application DNS records to point to the new ALB.

C. Copy the CloudFormation templates to an Amazon S3 bucket in the DR Region. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an AWS Lambda function to take an hourly snapshot of the Aurora database and of the most recent Docker image in the ECR repository. Copy the snapshot and the Docker image to the DR Region. In case of DR, use the CloudFormation template with the most recent Aurora snapshot and the Docker image from the local ECR repository to launch a new CloudFormation stack in the DR Region.

D. Copy the CloudFormation templates to an Amazon S3 bucket in the DR Region. Deploy a second application CloudFormation stack in the DR Region. Reconfigure Aurora to be a global database. Update both CloudFormation stacks when a new application release in the current Region is needed. In case of DR, update the application DNS records to point to the new ALB.
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora Global Database provides cross-Region replication to a secondary Region, and a predeployed application stack avoids both an infrastructure deployment delay and a Docker-image build during recovery. DNS can therefore be redirected to the already-running secondary ALB within the 2-hour RTO while the replicated database meets the 8-hour RPO. Aurora does not support cross-Region automated backup replication, and Amazon ECR replicates container images through cross-Region replication rather than ECR image snapshots. LEARN MORE Replication with Amazon Aurora Retaining automated backups for Aurora DB clusters

Retaining automated backups for Aurora DB clusters

questions.questionText: A security team plans to use AWS CloudTrail to monitor every action and API call in multiple accounts within the same AWS Organizations organization. The security team must ensure that users in those accounts cannot disable CloudTrail. Which solution satisfies this requirement?
options: A. Apply an SCP to all OUs to deny the cloudtrail:StopLogging action and the cloudtrail:DeleteTrail action.
B. Create IAM policies in each account to deny the cloudtrail:StopLogging action and the cloudtrail:DeleteTrail action.
C. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to notify the security team when a user disables CloudTrail in an account.
D. Use AWS Config to automatically re-enable CloudTrail if a user disables CloudTrail in an account.
questions.explanation: A service control policy (SCP) applied to the organization’s OUs can explicitly deny cloudtrail:StopLogging and cloudtrail:DeleteTrail for member accounts. SCP explicit denies limit the maximum permissions available in those accounts and override IAM allows, preventing account users from stopping or deleting CloudTrail. StopLogging stops the recording of AWS API calls and log-file delivery for a trail. LEARN MORE Application logging and monitoring using AWS CloudTrail StopLogging - AWS CloudTrail API Reference

StopLogging - AWS CloudTrail API Reference

questions.questionText: A company runs microservices in AWS Lambda that read data from Amazon DynamoDB. Developers manually deploy the Lambda code after it has been successfully tested. The company now requires tests and deployments to be automated and executed in the cloud. In addition, traffic to each microservice's new versions must be shifted incrementally over time after deployment. Which solution satisfies all requirements while providing the MOST developer velocity?
options: A. Create an AWS CodePipeline configuration and set up a post-commit hook to trigger the pipeline after tests have passed. Use AWS CodeDeploy and create a Canary deployment configuration that specifies the percentage of traffic and interval.

B. Create an AWS CodeBuild configuration that triggers when the test code is pushed. Use AWS CloudFormation to trigger an AWS CodePipeline configuration that deploys the new Lambda versions and specifies the traffic shift percentage and interval.

C. Create an AWS CodePipeline configuration and set up the source code step to trigger when code is pushed. Set up the build step to use AWS CodeBuild to run the tests. Set up an AWS CodeDeploy configuration to deploy, then select the CodeDeployDefault.LambdaLinear10PercentEvery3Minutes option.

D. Use the AWS CLI to set up a post-commit hook that uploads the code to an Amazon S3 bucket after tests have passed Set up an S3 event trigger that runs a Lambda function that deploys the new version. Use an interval in the Lambda function to deploy the code over time at the required percentage.
questions.explanation: AWS CodePipeline can automatically start from a source-code push and orchestrate the delivery workflow, while AWS CodeBuild runs the tests in a managed cloud build stage. AWS CodeDeploy supports Lambda linear deployments; CodeDeployDefault.LambdaLinear10PercentEvery3Minutes shifts 10% of traffic to the new Lambda version every three minutes until all traffic is shifted, satisfying the incremental rollout requirement with managed AWS services. LEARN MORE Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy Add a CodeBuild build action to a pipeline

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodePipeline pipelines to automate releases of its application. A typical pipeline has three stages: build, test, and deployment. The company has been using a separate AWS CodeBuild project to run scripts for each stage. However, the company now wants to use AWS CodeDeploy for the deployment stage of the pipelines. The company has packaged the application as an RPM package and must deploy it to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are in an EC2 Auto Scaling group and launch from a common AMI. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a new version of the common AMI with the CodeDeploy agent installed. Update the IAM role of the EC2 instances to allow access to CodeDeploy.
B. Create a new version of the common AMI with the CodeDeploy agent installed. Create an AppSpec file that contains application deployment scripts and grants access to CodeDeploy.

C. Create an application in CodeDeploy. Configure an in-place deployment type. Specify the Auto Scaling group as the deployment target. Add a step to the CodePipeline pipeline to use EC2 Image Builder to create a new AMI. Configure CodeDeploy to deploy the newly created AMI.

D. Create an application in CodeDeploy. Configure an in-place deployment type. Specify the Auto Scaling group as the deployment target. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to use the CodeDeploy action to deploy the application.

E. Create an application in CodeDeploy. Configure an in-place deployment type. Specify the EC2 instances that are launched from the common AMI as the deployment target. Update the CodePipeline pipeline to use the CodeDeploy action to deploy the application.
questions.explanation: For CodeDeploy deployments to Amazon EC2 instances, the CodeDeploy agent must be installed and running, and the instances require an IAM instance profile. A CodeDeploy in-place deployment group can target an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group, and the CodeDeploy action in CodePipeline deploys the application revision to that fleet. LEARN MORE Deployments on an EC2/On-Premises Compute Platform Integrating CodeDeploy with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
learnMore: Deployments on an EC2/On-Premises Compute Platform
Integrating CodeDeploy with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled. The company uses AWS Backup in a primary account and uses an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key to encrypt its backups. The company must automate cross-account backups of the resources that AWS Backup protects in the primary account. The company configures cross-account backup in the Organizations management account. It creates a new AWS account in the organization and configures an AWS Backup backup vault in that account. The company creates a KMS key in the new account to encrypt the backups. Finally, the company configures a new backup plan in the primary account, with the backup vault in the new account as the destination. When the AWS Backup job in the primary account runs, it creates backups in the primary account. However, the backups are not copied to the backup vault in the new account. Which combination of steps must the company take to copy the backups to the backup vault in the new account?
options: A. Edit the backup vault access policy in the new account to allow access to the primary account.
B. Edit the backup vault access policy in the primary account to allow access to the new account.
C. Edit the backup vault access policy in the primary account to allow access to the KMS key in the new account.
D. Edit the key policy of the KMS key in the primary account to share the key with the new account.
E. Edit the key policy of the KMS key in the new account to share the key with the primary account.
questions.explanation: The destination backup vault must have a resource-based access policy that allows the primary (source) account to perform backup:CopyIntoBackupVault. Also, when the source resources are encrypted with a customer-managed KMS key, the source key’s policy must grant the destination account access so AWS Backup can perform the cross-account copy. AWS Backup re-encrypts the copied recovery point with the destination vault’s KMS key. LEARN MORE Creating backup copies across AWS accounts - AWS Backup Encryption for backups in AWS Backup
learnMore: Creating backup copies across AWS accounts - AWS Backup
Encryption for backups in AWS Backup

questions.questionText: A company's web application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to route traffic to Amazon EC2 instances in three Availability Zones. The company deployed a newer application version to one Availability Zone for testing. If an application issue is detected, the company needs to route traffic away from the affected Availability Zone until the deployment is rolled back. The application must stay available and maintain static stability throughout the rollback. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Disable cross-zone load balancing on the ALB's target group. Initiate a zonal shift on the ALB to direct traffic away from the affected Availability Zone.
B. Disable cross-zone load balancing on the ALB's target group. Manually remove instances in the target group that belong to the affected Availability Zone.
C. Configure cross-zone load balancing on the ALB's target group to inherit settings from the ALB. Initiate a zonal shift on the ALB to direct traffic away from the affected Availability Zone.
D. Configure cross-zone load balancing on the ALB's target group to inherit settings from the ALB. Remove the subnet that is associated with the affected Availability Zone.
questions.explanation: Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC) zonal shift lets an Application Load Balancer move traffic away from a single affected Availability Zone with one action. With cross-zone load balancing enabled, the ALB blocks traffic to targets in the impacted zone and removes that zone’s load-balancer IP address from DNS. Configuring the target group to inherit the ALB setting retains this behavior while avoiding manual target deregistration or subnet removal, which supports static stability during rollback. LEARN MORE Zonal shift for your Application Load Balancer Application Load Balancers - Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)
learnMore: Zonal shift for your Application Load Balancer
Application Load Balancers - Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)

questions.questionText: A DevOps team runs an integration service on an Amazon EC2 instance. The team manages the integration service’s domain name with Amazon Route 53 by using a simple routing record. The integration service is stateful and uses Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for both data and state storage. The integration service does not support load balancing across multiple nodes. The DevOps team deploys the integration service to a new EC2 instance as a warm standby to decrease mean time to recovery. The team wants the integration service to fail over automatically to the standby EC2 instance. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Update the existing Route 53 DNS record's routing policy to weighted. Set the existing DNS record's weighting to 100. For the same domain, add a new DNS record that points to the standby EC2 instance. Set the new DNS record's weighting to 0. Associate an application health check with each record.

B. Update the existing Route 53 DNS record's routing policy to weighted. Set the existing DNS record's weighting to 99. For the same domain, add a new DNS record that points to the standby EC2 instance. Set the new DNS record's weighting to 1. Associate an application health check with each record.

C. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Update the existing Route 53 record to point to the ALB. Create a target group for each EC2 instance. Configure an application health check on each target group. Associate both target groups with the same ALB listener. Set the primary target group's weighting to 100. Set the standby target group's weighting to 0.

D. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Update the existing Route 53 record to point to the ALB. Create a target group for each EC2 instance. Configure an application health check on each target group. Associate both target groups with the same ALB listener. Set the primary target group's weighting to 99. Set the standby target group's weighting to 1.
questions.explanation: Route 53 weighted records that each have health checks provide active-passive DNS failover when the primary record has a nonzero weight and the standby record has weight 0. Route 53 returns healthy nonzero-weight records while they exist; if all such records are unhealthy, it considers the zero-weight standby record. This preserves a single active node and avoids load balancing the stateful service. LEARN MORE Active-active and active-passive failover - Amazon Route 53 How Amazon Route 53 chooses records when health checking is configured
learnMore: Active-active and active-passive failover - Amazon Route 53
How Amazon Route 53 chooses records when health checking is configured

questions.questionText: A company delivers an application to its customers. The application includes an Amazon API Gateway REST API that invokes an AWS Lambda function. During initialization, the Lambda function loads a large volume of data from an Amazon DynamoDB table. This data-loading process causes long cold-start times of 8–10 seconds. DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is configured for the DynamoDB table. Customers say that the application intermittently takes a long time to respond to requests. The application receives thousands of requests during the day. In the middle of the day, the application receives 10 times more requests than at any other time of day. Near the end of the day, the application's request volume drops to 10% of its normal total. A DevOps engineer must reduce Lambda function latency at all times of day. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure provisioned concurrency on the Lambda function with a concurrency value of 1. Delete the DAX cluster for the DynamoDB table.
B. Configure reserved concurrency on the Lambda function with a concurrency value of 0.

C. Configure provisioned concurrency on the Lambda function. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the Lambda function with provisioned concurrency values set to a minimum of 1 and a maximum of 100.
D. Configure reserved concurrency on the Lambda function. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the API Gateway API with a reserved concurrency maximum value of 100.
questions.explanation: Provisioned concurrency keeps pre-initialized Lambda execution environments ready for requests, moving initialization work such as loading data outside request-time cold starts. AWS Application Auto Scaling can automatically scale Lambda provisioned concurrency based on utilization or a schedule; a minimum of 1 preserves a warm environment during low traffic, while a maximum of 100 accommodates higher demand. Reserved concurrency only reserves and caps capacity; it does not pre-initialize execution environments. LEARN MORE Configuring provisioned concurrency for a function AWS Lambda and Application Auto Scaling
learnMore: Configuring provisioned concurrency for a function

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is designing a continuous development strategy for a company’s software-as-a-service (SaaS) web application that runs on AWS. For application and security reasons, users who subscribe to the application are distributed across multiple Application Load Balancers (ALBs), each with its own dedicated Auto Scaling group and fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The application does not need a build stage and, when committed to AWS CodeCommit, must initiate a simultaneous deployment to all ALBs, Auto Scaling groups, and EC2 fleets. Which architecture meets these requirements with the least configuration?
options: A. Create a single AWS CodePipeline pipeline that deploys the application in parallel using unique AWS CodeDeploy applications and deployment groups created for each ALB-Auto Scaling group pair.
B. Create a single AWS CodePipeline pipeline that deploys the application using a single AWS CodeDeploy application and single deployment group.
C. Create a single AWS CodePipeline pipeline that deploys the application in parallel using a single AWS CodeDeploy application and unique deployment group for each ALB-Auto Scaling group pair.

D. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline for each ALB-Auto Scaling group pair that deploys the application using an AWS CodeDeploy application and deployment group created for the same ALB-Auto Scaling group pair.
questions.explanation: For an Amazon EC2/On-Premises CodeDeploy deployment, one deployment group can target multiple Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups and can be associated with multiple Application Load Balancer target groups. A single CodePipeline deployment action can deploy the same revision through that deployment group to all of its included instance fleets, avoiding separate applications, deployment groups, and pipelines. LEARN MORE Working with deployment groups in CodeDeploy Create a deployment group for an in-place deployment
learnMore: Working with deployment groups in CodeDeploy
Create a deployment group for an in-place deployment

questions.questionText: A company hosts a development-environment website and database on an Amazon EC2 instance that uses Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) storage. The company wants to make the instance more resilient to underlying hardware issues. It wants to automatically recover the EC2 instance if AWS determines that the instance has lost network connectivity. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Add the EC2 instance to an Auto Scaling group. Set the minimum, maximum, and desired capacity to 1.
B. Add the EC2 instance to an Auto Scaling group. Configure a lifecycle hook to detach the EBS volume if the EC2 instance shuts down or terminates
C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed_System metric. Add an EC2 action to recover the instance when the alarm state is in ALARM
D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the NetworkOut metric. Add an EC2 action to recover the instance when the alarm state is in INSUFFICIENT_DATA.
questions.explanation: A failed EC2 system status check indicates an underlying AWS host hardware or software problem; examples include lost network connectivity. A CloudWatch alarm that monitors StatusCheckFailed_System and performs the EC2 recover action automatically recovers the instance onto different hardware. The recovery process preserves the instance identity and attached EBS volumes. LEARN MORE Configure CloudWatch action-based recovery on an EC2 instance Automatic instance recovery
learnMore: Configure CloudWatch action-based recovery on an EC2 instance
Automatic instance recovery

questions.questionText: An organization in AWS Organizations has one OU. The company operates Amazon EC2 instances in the accounts within that OU. It must restrict use of each EC2 instance’s credentials to the particular EC2 instance to which the credentials are assigned. A DevOps engineer must configure security for these EC2 instances. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an SCP that specifies the VPC CIDR block. Configure the SCP to check whether the value of the aws:VpcSourcelp condition key is in the specified block. In the same SCP check, check whether the values of the aws:EC2InstanceSourcePrivatelPv4 and aws:SourceVpc condition keys are the same. Deny access if either condition is false. Apply the SCP to the OU.

B. Create an SCP that checks whether the values of the aws:EC2InstanceSourceVPC and aws:SourceVpc condition keys are the same. Deny access if the values are not the same. In the same SCP check, check whether the values of the aws:EC2InstanceSourcePrivateIPv4 and aws:VpcSourceIp condition keys are the same. Deny access if the values are not the same. Apply the SCP to the OU.

C. Create an SCP that includes a list of acceptable VPC values and checks whether the value of the aws:SourceVpc condition key is in the list. In the same SCP check, define a list of acceptable IP address values and check whether the value of the aws:VpcSourceIp condition key is in the list. Deny access if either condition is false. Apply the SCP to each account in the organization.

D. Create an SCP that checks whether the values of the aws:EC2InstanceSourceVPC and aws:VpcSourceIp condition keys are the same. Deny access if the values are not the same. In the same SCP check, check whether the values of the aws:EC2InstanceSourcePrivateIPv4 and aws:SourceVpc condition keys are the same. Deny access if the values are not the same. Apply the SCP to each account in the organization.
questions.explanation: An SCP can bind Amazon EC2 role credentials to their originating instance by denying requests unless the request comes through a VPC endpoint in the same VPC where the credentials were delivered (aws:Ec2InstanceSourceVPC equals aws:SourceVpc) and from the same private IP address (aws:EC2InstanceSourcePrivateIPv4 equals aws:VpcSourceIp). Together, the VPC ID and private IP identify the specific instance; attaching this SCP to the OU enforces it for all accounts in that OU. LEARN MORE AWS global condition context keys

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS CodeCommit repository to store its source code and related unit tests. The company has configured an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that includes an AWS CodeBuild project, which runs when code is merged into the repository’s main branch. The company wants the CodeBuild project to execute the unit tests. If the tests pass, the CodeBuild project must tag the latest commit. How should the company configure the CodeBuild project to meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure the CodeBuild project to use native Git to done the CodeCommit repository. Configure the project to run the unit tests. Configure the project to use native Git to create a tag and to push the Git tag to the repository if the code passes the unit tests.

B. Configure the CodeBuild projed to use native Git to done the CodeCommit repository. Configure the project to run the unit tests. Configure the project to use AWS CLI commands to create a new repository tag in the repository if the code passes the unit tests.

C. Configure the CodeBuild project to use AWS CLI commands to copy the code from the CodeCommit repository. Configure the project to run the unit tests. Configure the project to use AWS CLI commands to create a new Git tag in the repository if the code passes the unit tests.

D. Configure the CodeBuild project to use AWS CLI commands to copy the code from the CodeCommit repository. Configure the project to run the unit tests. Configure the project to use AWS CLI commands to create a new repository tag in the repository if the code passes the unit tests.
questions.explanation: A Git tag labels a specific commit and must be created in a Git repository and pushed to CodeCommit with Git. AWS documents creating a tag with git tag and publishing it with git push; AWS CLI CodeCommit tagging instead adds AWS resource tags to the repository, not Git tags. A full Git clone also provides the Git metadata required for CodeBuild to perform Git operations. LEARN MORE Create a Git tag in AWS CodeCommit Use full clone with a CodeCommit pipeline source
learnMore: Create a Git tag in AWS CodeCommit
Use full clone with a CodeCommit pipeline source

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations, AWS Control Tower, AWS Config, and Terraform to manage its AWS accounts and resources. The company needs to ensure that users deploy only AWS Lambda functions that are connected to a VPC in member AWS accounts. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Configure AWS Control Tower to use proactive controls (guardrails). Enable the optional controls (guardrails) implemented with AWS CloudFormation hooks for Lambda on all OUs.

B. Create a new SCP. Include a conditional statement that uses a StringEquals condition operator to check the lambd:Vpclds condition key against a list of VPC IDs. Configure the SCP to allow the lambda CreateFunction action and the lambda UpdateFunctionConfiguration action if the value of the condition key matches one of the VPC IDs.
C. Create a custom rule in AWS Config to detect Lambda functions that are not connected to a VPC when any Lambda function is created or updated.

D. Create a new SCP. Include a conditional statement that uses a Null condition operator to determine whether the lambda Vpclds condition key is absent. Configure the SCP to deny the lambda CreateFunction action and the lambda UpdateFunctionConfiguration action if the condition key is absent.
questions.explanation: An SCP with an explicit Deny for lambda:CreateFunction and lambda:UpdateFunctionConfiguration when the lambda:VpcIds condition key is absent prevents Lambda functions from being created or updated without VPC configuration in member accounts. The Lambda VPC condition keys are supported by both actions, and the IAM Null operator tests whether a condition key is absent. This applies to direct API and Terraform operations, unlike CloudFormation-hook proactive controls, and prevents noncompliance rather than merely detecting it. LEARN MORE Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC IAM JSON policy elements: Condition operators
learnMore: Giving Lambda functions access to resources in an Amazon VPC
IAM JSON policy elements: Condition operators

questions.questionText: A company manages several AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations. Its security policy requires that member-account AWS root user credentials must not be used, and the company monitors access to those credentials. A recent alert indicates that a member account’s root user launched an Amazon EC2 instance. A DevOps engineer must create an SCP at the organization root level to prevent root users in member accounts from making any AWS service API calls. Which SCP satisfies these requirements?
options: A.
B.
C.
D.
questions.explanation: An SCP attached at the organization root can explicitly deny permissions for all member accounts, including each member account’s root user. A Deny for Action: "*" and Resource: "*", conditioned with StringLike on aws:PrincipalArn: "arn:aws:iam::*:root", matches only account root-user principals and prevents their AWS service API calls. AWS documents this deny-all-root-actions SCP pattern. LEARN MORE Best practices for member accounts - AWS Organizations Curated SCPs and Config Rules - AMS Advanced User Guide
learnMore: Best practices for member accounts - AWS Organizations
Curated SCPs and Config Rules - AMS Advanced User Guide

questions.questionText: A company’s application teams use AWS CodeCommit repositories for their applications. The application teams maintain repositories in multiple AWS accounts. All accounts belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. Each application team uses AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On), configured with an external IdP, to assume a developer IAM role. The developer role permits the application teams to use Git to work with code in the repositories. A security audit finds that the application teams can modify the main branch in any repository. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that lets the application teams modify the main branch only in the repositories they manage. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Update the SAML assertion to pass the user's team name. Update the IAM role's trust policy to add an access-team session tag that has the team name.
B. Create an approval rule template for each team in the Organizations management account. Associate the template with all the repositories. Add the developer role ARN as an approver.

C. Create an approval rule template for each account. Associate the template with all repositories. Add the "aws:ResourceTag/access-team": "$ ;{aws:PrincipalTag/access-team}" condition to the approval rule template.
D. For each CodeCommit repository, add an access-team tag that has the value set to the name of the associated team.
E.
F.
questions.explanation: A SAML-provided access-team session tag makes the team identity available as aws:PrincipalTag/access-team, while an access-team tag on each CodeCommit repository identifies its managing team. An SCP can apply an organization-wide explicit deny to main-branch write operations when the principal tag and repository tag do not match, overriding the broad existing developer-role permissions. CodeCommit supports tag-based authorization and its GitPush action supports the codecommit:References condition key for branch-specific restrictions. LEARN MORE Attributes for access control — AWS IAM Identity Center Identity and Access Management for AWS CodeCommit
learnMore: Attributes for access control — AWS IAM Identity Center
Identity and Access Management for AWS CodeCommit

questions.questionText: A company has several member accounts that belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. The security team must review every Amazon EC2 security group, including its inbound and outbound rules. The team wants to retrieve this information programmatically from the member accounts by using an AWS Lambda function in the organization's management account. Which combination of access changes satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Create a trust relationship that allows users in the member accounts to assume the management account IAM role.
B. Create a trust relationship that allows users in the management account to assume the IAM roles of the member accounts.
C. Create an IAM role in each member account that has access to the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess managed policy.
D. Create an I AM role in each member account to allow the sts:AssumeRole action against the management account IAM role's ARN.
E. Create an I AM role in the management account that allows the sts:AssumeRole action against the member account IAM role's ARN.
F. Create an IAM role in the management account that has access to the AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess managed policy.
questions.explanation: Cross-account role access requires a role in each member account whose trust policy allows the management-account principal to assume it, and whose permissions allow read-only EC2 inspection. The Lambda execution role in the management account must also be allowed to perform sts:AssumeRole on those member-account roles. AmazonEC2ReadOnlyAccess supplies the needed EC2 read permissions. LEARN MORE Cross-account resource access in IAM Update a role trust policy

Update a role trust policy

questions.questionText: A company’s DevOps engineer works in a multi-account environment. The company uses AWS Transit Gateway to route all outbound traffic through a network operations account. In that account, traffic from every account passes through a firewall appliance for inspection before proceeding to an internet gateway. The firewall appliance sends logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, with event severities of CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM, LOW, and INFO. The security team needs an alert whenever any CRITICAL events occur. What should the DevOps engineer do to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Synthetics canary to monitor the firewall state. If the firewall reaches a CRITICAL state or logs a CRITICAL event, use a CloudWatch alarm to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.

B. Create an Amazon CloudWatch metric filter by using a search for CRITICAL events. Publish a custom metric for the finding. Use a CloudWatch alarm based on the custom metric to publish a notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.

C. Enable Amazon GuardDuty in the network operations account. Configure GuardDuty to monitor flow logs. Create an Amazon EventBridge event rule that is invoked by GuardDuty events that are CRITICAL. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.

D. Use AWS Firewall Manager to apply consistent policies across all accounts. Create an Amazon EventBridge event rule that is invoked by Firewall Manager events that are CRITICAL. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target. Subscribe the security team’s email address to the topic.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs metric filters can match a term or pattern in incoming log events and convert matches into a custom CloudWatch metric. An alarm on that metric can enter the ALARM state when a CRITICAL event is logged and publish a notification to an Amazon SNS topic, which can deliver email to the security team. LEARN MORE Creating metrics from log events using filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs Alarming on logs - Amazon CloudWatch
learnMore: Creating metrics from log events using filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
Alarming on logs - Amazon CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are in an OU with a policy attached that allows all actions. The company is migrating several Git repositories to a specified AWS CodeConnections-supported Git provider. The Git repositories manage AWS CloudFormation stacks for application infrastructure that the company deploys across multiple AWS Regions. The company wants a DevOps team to integrate CodeConnections into the CloudFormation stacks. The DevOps team must ensure that company staff members can integrate only with the specified Git provider. The deployment process must be highly available across Regions. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Add a new SCP statement to the OU that denies the CodeConnections CreatingConnections action where the provider type is not the specified Git provider.
B. Add a new SCP statement to the OU that allows the CodeConnections CreatingConnections action where the provider type is the specified Git provider.
C. Use CodeConnectlons to configure a single CodeConnections connection to each Git repository.
D. Use CodeConnections to create a CodeConnections connection from each Region where the company operates to each Git repository.
E. Use CodeConnections to create a CodeConnections repository link. Update each CfoudFormation stack to sync from the Git repository.
F. For each Git repository, create a pipeline in AWS CodePipefine that has the Git repository set as the source and a CloudFormation deployment stage.
questions.explanation: An explicit SCP deny for codeconnections:CreateConnection when codeconnections:ProviderType is not the approved provider overrides the OU’s broad allow and prevents connections to unapproved Git providers. AWS CodeConnections connections are global resources: a connection created once can be used in any AWS Region, supporting multi-Region operation without separately creating connections per Region. A repository link associates that connection with the external repository, and Git sync uses the link to monitor repository content and synchronize CloudFormation stack updates. LEARN MORE Actions, resources, and condition keys for AWS CodeConnections Global resources in AWS CodeConnections
learnMore: Actions, resources, and condition keys for AWS CodeConnections
Global resources in AWS CodeConnections

questions.questionText: A company plans to migrate its content-sharing web application, currently hosted on Amazon EC2, to a serverless architecture. The company currently deploys application changes by creating a new Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances and a new Elastic Load Balancer, then shifting traffic away by using an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy. For the new serverless application, the company plans to use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. It must update its deployment processes to support the new application. It must also preserve the ability to test new features with a small number of users before releasing those features to the entire user base. Which deployment strategy meets these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CDK to deploy API Gateway and Lambda functions. When code needs to be changed, update the AWS CloudFormation stack and deploy the new version of the APIs and Lambda functions. Use a Route 53 failover routing policy for the canary release strategy.

B. Use AWS CloudFormation to deploy API Gateway and Lambda functions using Lambda function versions. When code needs to be changed, update the CloudFormation stack with the new Lambda code and update the API versions using a canary release strategy. Promote the new version when testing is complete.

C. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy API Gateway and Lambda functions. When code needs to be changed, deploy a new version of the API and Lambda functions. Shift traffic gradually using an Elastic Beanstalk blue/green deployment.

D. Use AWS OpsWorks to deploy API Gateway in the service layer and Lambda functions in a custom layer. When code needs to be changed, use OpsWorks to perform a blue/green deployment and shift traffic gradually.
questions.explanation: Amazon API Gateway canary releases split a configured percentage of requests between the production deployment and a new deployment, allowing new API and Lambda-backed functionality to be tested with a small subset of users. After successful testing, the canary deployment can be promoted to the production release. AWS CloudFormation can manage the API Gateway and Lambda resources, while Lambda versions support versioned function code. LEARN MORE Set up an API Gateway canary release deployment Promote a canary release
learnMore: Set up an API Gateway canary release deployment
Promote a canary release

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer operates a large commercial website running on Amazon EC2. The website uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to collect and process web logs. The DevOps engineer manages the Kinesis consumer application, which also runs on Amazon EC2. Sudden data increases cause the Kinesis consumer application to lag behind, and the Kinesis data streams discard records before they can be processed. The DevOps engineer must implement a solution that improves stream handling. Which solution satisfies these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Modify the Kinesis consumer application to store the logs durably in Amazon S3. Use Amazon EMR to process the data directly on Amazon S3 to derive customer insights. Store the results in Amazon S3.

B. Horizontally scale the Kinesis consumer application by adding more EC2 instances based on the Amazon CloudWatch GetRecords.IteratorAgeMilliseconds metric. Increase the retention period of the Kinesis data streams.
C. Convert the Kinesis consumer application to run as an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Kinesis data streams as the event source for the Lambda function to process the data streams.
D. Increase the number of shards in the Kinesis data streams to increase the overall throughput so that the consumer application processes the data faster.
questions.explanation: AWS Lambda can consume Amazon Kinesis Data Streams through an event source mapping, which polls stream shards, batches records, and invokes the function without managing EC2 consumer instances. This serverless design reduces operational work while accommodating variable stream-processing demand; Lambda also supports concurrent batch processing per shard when additional throughput is needed. LEARN MORE Using Lambda to process records from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams Process Amazon Kinesis Data Streams records with Lambda
learnMore: Using Lambda to process records from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams
Process Amazon Kinesis Data Streams records with Lambda

questions.questionText: A large enterprise is deploying a web application in AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances operate in an Auto Scaling group spanning multiple Availability Zones. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for Oracle DB instance and Amazon DynamoDB. Separate environments exist for development, testing, and production. What is the MOST secure and flexible method for obtaining password credentials during deployment?
options: A. Retrieve an access key from an AWS Systems Manager SecureString parameter to access AWS services. Retrieve the database credentials from a Systems Manager SecureString parameter.
B. Launch the EC2 instances with an EC2 IAM role to access AWS services. Retrieve the database credentials from AWS Secrets Manager.
C. Retrieve an access key from an AWS Systems Manager plaintext parameter to access AWS services. Retrieve the database credentials from a Systems Manager SecureString parameter.
D. Launch the EC2 instances with an EC2 IAM role to access AWS services. Store the database passwords in an encrypted config file with the application artifacts.
questions.explanation: An EC2 IAM role provides the application with temporary, automatically rotated AWS credentials, avoiding long-term access keys on instances. AWS Secrets Manager is designed to securely retrieve and rotate database credentials at runtime, keeping database passwords out of application artifacts and enabling credential lifecycle management. LEARN MORE IAM roles for Amazon EC2 What is AWS Secrets Manager?

questions.questionText: A company keeps its Python-based application code in AWS CodeCommit and uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy the application. The CodeCommit repository and the CodePipeline pipeline are deployed in the same AWS account. The company’s security team requires that all code undergo vulnerability scanning before deployment to production. If vulnerabilities are detected, the deployment must stop. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a new CodeBuild project. Configure the project to run a security scan on the code by using Amazon CodeGuru Security. Configure the CodeBuild project to raise an error if CodeGuru Security finds vulnerabilities. Create a new IAM role that has sufficient permissions to run CodeGuru Security scans. Assign the role to the CodeBuild project. In the CodePipeline pipeline, add a new stage before the deployment stage. Select AWS CodeBuild as the action provider for the new stage. Use the source artifact from the CodeCommit repository. Configure the action to use the CodeBuild project.

B. Create a new CodeBuild project. Configure the project to run a security scan on the code by using Amazon Inspector. Configure the CodeBuild project to raise an error if Amazon Inspector finds vulnerabilities. Create a new IAM role that has sufficient permissions to run Amazon Inspector scans. Assign the role to the CodeBuild project. In the CodePipeline pipeline, add a new stage before the deployment stage. Select AWS CodeBuild as the action provider for the new stage. Use the source artifact from the CodeCommit repository. Configure the action to use the CodeBuild project.

C. Update the IAM role that is attached to CodePipeline to include sufficient permissions to invoke Amazon DevOps Guru. In the CodePipeline pipeline, add a new stage before the deployment stage. Select DevOps Guru as the action provider for the new stage. Use the source artifact from the CodeCommit repository.

D. Update the IAM role that is attached to CodePipeline to include sufficient permissions to invoke Amazon DevOps Guru. In the CodePipeline pipeline, add a new stage before the deployment stage. Select CodeGuru Security as the action provider for the new stage. Use the source artifact from the CodeCommit repository.
questions.explanation: Amazon CodeGuru Security performs static analysis to detect vulnerabilities in application code. A CodeBuild project can run the scan against the pipeline’s source artifact and fail its build when findings are detected. Because CodePipeline stops when a required CodeBuild action fails, placing that action before deployment prevents vulnerable code from reaching production. Amazon Inspector assesses deployed workloads, while Amazon DevOps Guru provides operational insights rather than source-code vulnerability scanning. LEARN MORE AWS CodeBuild build and test action reference Amazon CodeGuru Security CLI reference

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The company must implement comprehensive logging for the control plane and the nodes. It must analyze API requests to the Kubernetes control plane and monitor container performance on the nodes. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Enable AWS CloudTrail for control plane logging. Deploy Logstash as a ReplicaSet on the nodes to collect logs from the nodes. Use Amazon OpenSearch Service to store and analyze the logs for the control plane and the nodes.

B. Enable control plane logging for the EKS cluster. Send the logs to Amazon CloudWatch. Use CloudWatch Container Insights to collect logs for the nodes and the containers. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query and analyze the logs for the control plane and the nodes.

C. Enable API server control plane logging for the EKS cluster. Send the logs to Amazon S3 Deploy Kubernetes Event Exporter to the nodes to collect logs from the nodes. Send the logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query logs for the control plane and the nodes. Use Amazon QuickSight for visualization.

D. Use AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry to collect logs for the control plane and the nodes. Stream all the logs to Amazon Data Firehose. Use Amazon Redshift to analyze the aggregated log data for the control plane and the nodes.
questions.explanation: Amazon EKS control plane logging delivers Kubernetes control-plane audit and diagnostic logs, including API server logs, directly to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. CloudWatch Container Insights collects and summarizes container and node metrics and logs for Amazon EKS, including performance data. CloudWatch Logs Insights can query the centralized CloudWatch log data, so this solution meets the logging, API-analysis, and node-performance requirements with managed services and minimal operational administration. questions.questionText: A company determines that its production environment and disaster recovery (DR) environment are deployed in the same AWS Region. All production applications run on Amazon EC2 instances and are deployed through AWS CloudFormation. The applications use an Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP volume for application storage. No application data is stored on the EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer copies the required AMIs to a new DR Region. The DevOps engineer also modifies the CloudFormation code to accept a Region as a parameter. Storage in the DR Region requires an RPO of 10 minutes. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 bucket in both Regions. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) for the S3 buckets. Create a scheduled AWS Lambda function to copy any new content from the FSx for ONTAP volume to the S3 bucket in the production Region.

B. Use AWS Backup to create a backup vault and a custom backup plan that has a 10-minute frequency. Specify the DR Region as the target Region. Assign the EC2 instances in the production Region to the backup plan.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function to create snapshots of the instance store volumes that are attached to the EC2 instances. Configure the Lambda function to copy the snapshots to the DR Region and to remove the previous copies. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule that invokes the Lambda function every 10 minutes.
D. Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the DR Region. Configure a 5-minute schedule for a volume-level NetApp SnapMirror to replicate the volume from the production Region to the DR Region.
questions.explanation: NetApp SnapMirror provides scheduled volume-level replication between Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP file systems, including cross-Region replication. It can run as often as every 5 minutes, so replicating the application-storage volume every 5 minutes keeps the recovery point within a 10-minute RPO. questions.questionText: A cloud team uses AWS Organizations and AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to administer a company’s AWS accounts. The company recently formed a research team. The research team needs the ability to fully manage resources in its account, but it must not be able to create IAM users. The cloud team creates a Research Administrator permission set in IAM Identity Center for the research team. The permission set has the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy attached. The cloud team must ensure that nobody on the research team can create IAM users. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM policy that denies the iam:CreateUser action. Attach the IAM policy to the Research Administrator permission set.
B. Create an IAM policy that allows all actions except the iam:CreateUser action. Use the IAM policy to set the permissions boundary for the Research Administrator permission set.
C. Create an SCP that denies the iam:CreateUser action. Attach the SCP to the research team's AWS account.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that deletes IAM users. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that detects the IAM CreateUser event. Configure the rule to invoke the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: An SCP with an explicit Deny for iam:CreateUser restricts every principal in the affected member account and overrides permissions granted by AdministratorAccess. It cannot be bypassed by creating and assuming another IAM role, unlike a deny policy or permissions boundary applied only to the IAM Identity Center permission-set role. questions.questionText: A company operates several applications in the same AWS account. The applications send logs to Amazon CloudWatch. A data analytics team must collect performance metrics and custom metrics from the applications. The team must transform the metrics data before storing it in an Amazon S3 bucket. The team must automatically collect any new metrics that are added to the CloudWatch namespace. Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Configure a CloudWatch metric stream to include metrics from the application and the CloudWatch namespace. Configure the metric stream to deliver the metrics to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the Firehose delivery stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform the data. Configure the delivery stream to send the transformed data to the S3 bucket.

B. Configure a CloudWatch metrics stream to include all the metrics and to deliver the metrics to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the Firehose delivery stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform the data. Configure the delivery stream to send the transformed data to the S3 bucket.
C. Configure metric filters for the CloudWatch logs to create custom metrics. Configure a CloudWatch metric stream to deliver the application metrics to the S3 bucket.

D. Configure subscription filters on the application log groups to target an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream. Configure the Firehose delivery stream to invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform the data. Configure the delivery stream to send the transformed data to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: A CloudWatch metric stream configured for all metrics automatically includes newly created metrics. It can send metrics to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream, where an AWS Lambda transformation is applied before Firehose delivers the transformed records to Amazon S3. This avoids maintaining filters or subscriptions as metrics are added. LEARN MORE Use metric streams - Amazon CloudWatch Custom setup with Firehose - Amazon CloudWatch
