questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must configure an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that publishes container images to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. The pipeline must wait for the preceding run to complete and must run when new Git tags are pushed to a Git repository connected to AWS CodeConnections. An existing deployment pipeline must run when new container images are published. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Configure a CodePipeline V2 type pipeline that uses QUEUED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all tags. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches container image pushes to start the existing deployment pipeline.

B. Configure a CodePipeline V2 type pipeline that uses SUPERSEDED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all branches. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches container image pushes to start the existing deployment pipeline.

C. Configure a CodePipeline V1 type pipeline that uses SUPERSEDED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all tags. Add a stage at the end of the pipeline to invoke the existing deployment pipeline.

D. Configure a CodePipeline V1 type pipeline that uses QUEUED mode. Add a trigger filter to the pipeline definition that includes all branches. Add a stage at the end of the pipeline to invoke the existing deployment pipeline.
questions.explanation: CodePipeline QUEUED mode processes executions in their queued order and requires a V2 pipeline. V2 pipelines support trigger filters for Git tags on CodeConnections source actions. Amazon ECR sends an EventBridge event after each completed image push, so an EventBridge rule matching successful image pushes can start the existing deployment pipeline. questions.questionText: An Amazon EC2 instance runs in a VPC and must download an object from a restricted Amazon S3 bucket. When the DevOps engineer attempts to download the object, an AccessDenied error occurs. What could cause this error?
options: A. The S3 bucket default encryption is enabled.
B. There is an error in the S3 bucket policy.
C. The object has been moved to S3 Glacier.
D. There is an error in the IAM role configuration.
E. S3 Versioning is enabled.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 returns AccessDenied when authorization is explicitly denied or when no applicable permission allows the action. A bucket policy can deny the request or fail to grant the instance role access, and the EC2 instance’s IAM role can be missing the required s3:GetObject permission or include a deny. Default encryption and versioning do not independently prevent object reads; an object in S3 Glacier must be restored and normally produces an object-state error rather than an authorization denial. questions.questionText: A company’s production environment uses an AWS CodeDeploy blue/green deployment to deploy an application. The deployment includes Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups that launch instances running Amazon Linux 2. A functional appspec.yml file is in the code repository and contains the following text: A DevOps engineer must ensure that a script downloads and installs a license file on the instances before the replacement instances begin handling request traffic. The DevOps engineer adds a hooks section to the appspec.yml file. Which hook should the DevOps engineer use to run the script that downloads and installs the license file?
options: A. AfterBlockTraffic
B. BeforeBlockTraffic
C. BeforeInstall
D. DownloadBundle
questions.explanation: BeforeInstall is a scriptable lifecycle event available for the replacement instances in an EC2/On-Premises blue/green deployment and is intended for preinstallation tasks. It therefore allows the license to be downloaded and installed before the replacement environment serves production traffic. DownloadBundle is reserved for the CodeDeploy agent and cannot be used to run scripts. LEARN MORE AppSpec 'hooks' section for an EC2/On-Premises deployment
learnMore: AppSpec 'hooks' section for an EC2/On-Premises deployment

questions.questionText: A company is implementing AWS CodePipeline to automate its testing process. The company wants notification when the execution state fails and has configured the following custom event pattern in Amazon EventBridge: Which type of events will this event pattern match?
options: A. Failed deploy and build actions across all the pipelines
B. All rejected or failed approval actions across all the pipelines
C. All the events across all pipelines
D. Approval actions across all the pipelines
questions.explanation: This EventBridge pattern matches CodePipeline action execution state-change events whose state is FAILED and whose action category is Approval, with no restriction to particular pipelines. A failed approval action represents either a reviewer rejection or a failure caused by an incorrect action configuration. LEARN MORE Monitoring CodePipeline events
learnMore: Monitoring CodePipeline events

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is developing an application that uses an AWS Lambda function to query an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The Lambda function executes read-only queries. Amazon EventBridge events invoke the Lambda function. As an increasing number of events invoke the Lambda function each second, database latency rises and database throughput falls. The DevOps engineer must improve the application's performance. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon RDS Proxy to create a proxy. Connect the proxy to the Aurora cluster reader endpoint. Set a maximum connections percentage on the proxy.
B. Implement database connection pooling inside the Lambda code. Set a maximum number of connections on the database connection pool.
C. Implement the database connection opening outside the Lambda event handler code.
D. Implement the database connection opening and closing inside the Lambda event handler code.
E. Connect to the proxy endpoint from the Lambda function.
F. Connect to the Aurora cluster endpoint from the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS Proxy provides connection pooling and can limit the database connections it establishes by using a maximum connections percentage, preventing highly concurrent Lambda invocations from exhausting Aurora connections. For a read-only workload, a proxy reader endpoint uses Aurora reader instances and supports read scalability. Lambda should establish the reusable database connection outside the event handler, and its connection string must use the proxy endpoint. Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora RDS Proxy endpoints for Aurora LEARN MORE Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora Working with Amazon RDS Proxy endpoints

questions.questionText: A company hosts a static website in an Amazon S3 bucket. Customers access the website at example.com. The company uses an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy with a TTL of 1 day. The company has chosen to replace the current static website with a dynamic web application. The dynamic web application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. On the day of the production launch for customers, the company creates an additional Route 53 weighted DNS record entry pointing to the ALB, with a weight of 255 and a TTL of 1 hour. Two days later, a DevOps engineer observes that the former static website is sometimes shown when customers go to example.com. How can the DevOps engineer ensure that the company serves only dynamic content for example.com?
options: A. Delete all objects, including previous versions, from the S3 bucket that contains the static website content.
B. Update the weighted DNS record entry that points to the S3 bucket. Apply a weight of 0. Specify the domain reset option to propagate changes immediately.
C. Configure webpage redirect requests on the S3 bucket with a hostname that redirects to the ALB.
D. Remove the weighted DNS record entry that points to the S3 bucket from the example.com hosted zone. Wait for DNS propagation to become complete.
questions.explanation: Weighted Route 53 records route DNS responses in proportion to their weights; adding an ALB record with weight 255 does not stop the existing S3 weighted record from being returned. Deleting the S3 record removes it from future Route 53 responses. DNS resolvers that previously cached the S3 answer must be allowed to expire that cached entry, so waiting for DNS propagation/cache expiry ensures only the ALB-backed dynamic application is served. AWS: Weighted routing AWS: Values specific for weighted records LEARN MORE AWS Route 53 weighted routing AWS Route 53 values specific for weighted records

questions.questionText: A software development team is building a CI/CD pipeline for its web application. The team uses AWS CodeBuild to compile Java-based source code and run unit tests. The team must store the artifacts produced by the CodeBuild project. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket as an artifact output location in the project. Add the artifact locations to the project's buildspec file. Configure an S3 bucket policy that allows the CodeBuild project's resource access role to access the S3 bucket.

B. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket as an artifact output location in the project's buildspec file. Add the artifact locations to the project's buildspec file.Configure an S3 bucket policy that allows the CodeBuild service role to access the S3 bucket.

C. Configure an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system as a file system location for the project. Configure the EFS file system as the artifact output location in the project's buildspec file. Configure a file system policy that allows CodeBuild to access the file system.

D. Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure the EBS volume as the artifact output location in the project's buildspec file. Configure an IAM role that allows CodeBuild to access the volume.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild stores build output artifacts in an Amazon S3 bucket when the project artifact type is S3. The project defines the output bucket, and the buildspec artifacts section identifies the generated files to collect. The CodeBuild project's role must be authorized to access the bucket. EFS and EBS are not supported output-artifact destinations for CodeBuild. LEARN MORE ProjectArtifacts - AWS CodeBuild API Reference Build specification reference for CodeBuild

questions.questionText: A company mandates an RPO of 2 hours and an RTO of 10 minutes for its data and application at all times. An application uses a MySQL database and Amazon EC2 web servers. The development team requires a failover and disaster-recovery strategy. Which combination of deployment strategies will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon Aurora cluster in one Availability Zone across multiple Regions as the data store. Use Aurora’s automatic recovery capabilities in the event of a disaster.
B. Create an Amazon Aurora global database in two Regions as the data store. In the event of a failure, promote the secondary Region as the primary for the application.
C. Create an Amazon Aurora multi-master cluster across multiple Regions as the data store. Use a Network Load Balancer to balance the database traffic in different Regions.

D. Set up the application in two Regions and use Amazon Route 53 failover-based routing that points to the Application Load Balancers in both Regions. Use health checks to determine the availability in a given Region. Use Auto Scaling groups in each Region to adjust capacity based on demand.

E. Set up the application in two Regions and use a multi-Region Auto Scaling group behind Application Load Balancers to manage the capacity based on demand. In the event of a disaster, adjust the Auto Scaling group’s desired instance count to increase baseline capacity in the failover Region.
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora Global Database replicates an Aurora MySQL database across Regions, typically with replication latency under a second, and supports cross-Region failover by promoting a secondary cluster. Route 53 failover routing uses health checks to send traffic to the healthy Regional Application Load Balancer, while Auto Scaling groups in each Region provide independent web-tier capacity. Together, these strategies provide a cross-Region database recovery path and a healthy application endpoint within the stated recovery objectives. LEARN MORE Using switchover or failover in Amazon Aurora Global Database Overview of Amazon Aurora Global Database

Overview of Amazon Aurora Global Database

questions.questionText: A company has multiple development teams in separate business units that work in one shared AWS account. Every Amazon EC2 resource created in the account must have tags identifying who created it. Tagging must take place within the first hour after resource creation. A DevOps engineer must add tags to the created resources that contain the user ID of the resource creator and the cost center ID. The DevOps engineer configures an AWS Lambda function with the cost center mappings to tag the resources. The DevOps engineer also configures AWS CloudTrail in the AWS account. An Amazon S3 bucket stores the CloudTrail event logs. Which solution meets the tagging requirements?
options: A. Create an S3 event notification on the S3 bucket to invoke the Lambda function for s3:ObjectTagging:Put events. Enable bucket versioning on the S3 bucket.
B. Enable server access logging on the S3 bucket. Create an S3 event notification on the S3 bucket for s3:ObjectTagging:* events.
C. Create a recurring hourly Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule that invokes the Lambda function. Modify the Lambda function to read the logs from the S3 bucket.
D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses Amazon EC2 as the event source. Configure the rule to match events delivered by CloudTrail. Configure the rule to target the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 API calls are recorded by AWS CloudTrail, including identity information about the principal that made the call. Amazon EventBridge rules can match Amazon EC2 events with the AWS API Call via CloudTrail detail type and invoke a Lambda function as the target. This provides the Lambda function the creation event and creator identity promptly, so it can apply the required creator and cost-center tags. AWS EventBridge documentation LEARN MORE Tutorial: Create an EventBridge rule that reacts to API calls via CloudTrail Log Amazon EC2 API calls using AWS CloudTrail

questions.questionText: A company runs several applications in an AWS account. Each application sends its logs to a separate Amazon CloudWatch log group. The company’s CloudWatch ingestion costs are rising. A DevOps engineer must determine which applications are responsible for the increased logging costs. Which solution satisfies this requirement in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Use CloudWatch metrics to create a custom expression that identifies the CloudWatch log groups that receive the most data.
B. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs Insights to create a query for the application log groups to identify the number of log groups that received data during a specific time period.
C. Use AWS Cost Explorer to generate a cost report that details costs for CloudWatch usage.
D. Use AWS CloudTrail to filter for CreateLogStream events for each application.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs publishes IncomingBytes for each LogGroupName. A CloudWatch metric query or expression can group and rank these metrics to reveal the log groups—and therefore applications—ingesting the most data, directly targeting the source of higher ingestion charges. questions.questionText: A company requires a failover and disaster-recovery strategy for its data and application. The application uses a MySQL database and Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires a maximum RPO of 2 hours and a maximum RTO of 10 minutes for its data and application at all times. Which combination of deployment strategies meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon Aurora Single-AZ cluster in multiple AWS Regions as the data store. Use Aurora's automatic recovery capabilities in the event of a disaster.

B. Create an Amazon Aurora global database in two AWS Regions as the data store. In the event of a failure, promote the secondary Region to the primary for the application. Update the application to use the Aurora cluster endpoint in the secondary Region.
C. Create an Amazon Aurora cluster in multiple AWS Regions as the data store. Use a Network Load Balancer to balance the database traffic in different Regions.
D. Set up the application in two AWS Regions. Use Amazon Route 53 failover routing that points to Application Load Balancers in both Regions. Use health checks and Auto Scaling groups in each Region.

E. Set up the application in two AWS Regions. Configure AWS Global Accelerator to point to Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in both Regions. Add both ALBs to a single endpoint group. Use health checks and Auto Scaling groups in each Region.
questions.explanation: Amazon Aurora Global Database replicates data across AWS Regions and supports cross-Region failover by promoting a secondary cluster. Its RPO is typically measured in seconds and its RTO can be on the order of minutes, meeting the specified recovery objectives. Deploying the application in both Regions with Route 53 failover routing, ALB health checks, and Auto Scaling groups provides regional application failover and capacity in the secondary Region. questions.questionText: A company uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to develop a microservices-based application. The company must create reusable infrastructure components for three environments: development, staging, and production. The components must include networking resources, database resources, and serverless compute resources. The company must implement a solution that delivers consistent infrastructure across environments while allowing environment-specific customizations. The solution must also minimize code duplication. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST development overhead?
options: A. Create custom Level 1 (L1) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create a single set of deployment stacks that takes the environment name as an argument upon instantiation. Deploy CDK applications for each environment.

B. Create custom Level 1 (L1) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create separate deployment stacks for each environment. Use the CDK context command to determine which stacks to run when deploying to each environment.

C. Create custom Level 3 (L3) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create a single set of deployment stacks that takes the environment name as an argument upon instantiation. Deploy CDK applications for each environment.

D. Create custom Level 3 (L3) constructs out of Level 2 (L2) constructs where repeatable patterns exist. Create separate deployment stacks for each environment. Use the CDK context command to determine which stacks to run when deploying to each environment.
questions.explanation: Custom L3 constructs are reusable patterns that compose multiple L2 constructs into higher-level application infrastructure. They encapsulate common networking, database, and serverless resources while exposing properties for environment-specific overrides. Instantiating one shared set of stacks with an environment argument maintains consistent deployments and eliminates the duplicated code required by separate stacks. L1 constructs are low-level CloudFormation resource representations and are not the appropriate abstraction for composing reusable patterns from L2 constructs. LEARN MORE AWS CDK constructs Layer 3 constructs
learnMore: Layer 3 constructs

questions.questionText: A company operates an application in a single AWS Region. The application runs on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster and connects to an Amazon Aurora MySQL cluster. The application is built in an AWS CodeBuild project. Its container images are published to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The company must replicate the application state for the container images and the database to a second Region. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Turn on Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) on the bucket that holds the ECR container images. Deploy the application to an EKS cluster in the second Region by referencing the new S3 bucket object URL for the container image in a Kubernetes deployment file. Configure a cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Configure the new application deployment to use the endpoints for the cross-Region Aurora Replica.

B. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to image pushes to the ECR repository. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to replicate the image to a new ECR repository in the second Region. Deploy the application to an EKS cluster in the second Region by referencing the new ECR repository in a Kubernetes deployment file. Configure a cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Configure the new application deployment to use the endpoints for the cross-Region Aurora Replica.

C. Turn on Cross-Region Replication to replicate the ECR repository to the second Region. Deploy the application to an EKS cluster in the second Region by referencing the new ECR repository in a Kubernetes deployment file. Configure an Aurora global database with clusters in the initial Region and the second Region. Configure the new application deployment to use the endpoints for the second Region's cluster in the Aurora global database.

D. Configure the CodeBuild project to also push the container image to an ECR repository in the second Region. Deploy the application to an EKS cluster in the second Region by referencing the new ECR repository in a Kubernetes deployment file. Configure an Aurora MySQL cluster in the second Region as the target for binary log replication from the Aurora MySQL cluster in the initial Region. Configure the new application deployment to use the endpoints for the second Region's cluster.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR Cross-Region Replication automatically copies container images to a repository in the destination Region. An Aurora Global Database provides managed replication from the primary Aurora cluster to a secondary cluster in another Region, using Aurora’s storage-layer replication with typically sub-second lag and without configuring or managing Aurora MySQL binary-log replication. This combination minimizes custom automation and database replication administration. LEARN MORE Private image replication in Amazon ECR Using Amazon Aurora Global Database
learnMore: Private image replication in Amazon ECR
Using Amazon Aurora Global Database

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to host containerized applications that are available in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The company currently creates EKS clusters in its development environment by using the AWS CLI aws eks create-cluster command. The company uses the aws eks create-addon command to install required add-ons. All installed add-ons are currently version-compatible with the Kubernetes version that the company uses. Every cluster uses managed node groups exclusively for compute capacity. Some EKS clusters require a version upgrade. A DevOps engineer must ensure that upgrades continue to occur within the AWS standard support schedule. Which solution meets this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Run the aws eks update-cluster-version command. Providing appropriate arguments such as cluster name and version number.
B. Enable EKS Auto Mode on all EKS clusters. Remove all existing managed node groups.
C. Run the eksctl command to upgrade the EKS clusters. Provide appropriate arguments such as cluster name and version number
D. Refactor the environment to create EKS clusters by using infrastructure as code (IaC). Upgrade the clusters by using code changes.
questions.explanation: EKS Auto Mode minimizes Kubernetes upgrade operations by managing compute and automatically maintaining nodes and related components. After a control-plane update, Auto Mode incrementally updates its nodes while respecting Pod Disruption Budgets, avoiding the separate managed-node-group upgrade work required by standard EKS clusters. EKS Auto Mode also automates key infrastructure capabilities that otherwise require add-on management. LEARN MORE Automate cluster infrastructure with EKS Auto Mode Update existing cluster to new Kubernetes version

questions.questionText: A company operates a workload on Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires a control that mandates Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) on every EC2 instance in the AWS account. If an EC2 instance does not block the use of Instance Metadata Service Version 1 (IMDSv1), that EC2 instance must be terminated. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Set up AWS Config in the account. Use a managed rule to check EC2 instances. Configure the rule to remediate the findings by using AWS Systems Manager Automation to terminate the instance.

B. Create a permissions boundary that prevents the ec2:RunInstance action if the ec2:MetadataHttpTokens condition key is not set to a value of required. Attach the permissions boundary to the IAM role that was used to launch the instance.

C. Set up Amazon Inspector in the account. Configure Amazon Inspector to activate deep inspection for EC2 instances. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for an Inspector2 finding. Set an AWS Lambda function as the target to terminate the instance.
D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for the EC2 instance launch successful event. Send the event to an AWS Lambda function to inspect the EC2 metadata and to terminate the instance.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule EC2_IMDSV2_CHECK evaluates EC2 instances and marks an instance as noncompliant when its HttpTokens setting is optional, which allows IMDSv1. AWS Config supports remediation through AWS Systems Manager Automation documents, enabling automatic termination of each noncompliant instance. LEARN MORE ec2-imdsv2-check - AWS Config Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config

questions.questionText: A company runs a globally deployed product from multiple AWS Regions. The company’s DevOps team must use Amazon API Gateway to deploy an API that supports the product. The API must be deployed redundantly. The deployment must deliver independent availability from each company location. It must also respond through a custom domain URL and optimize performance for API user requests. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Deploy an API Gateway edge-optimized API endpoint in the us-east-1 Region. Create an API Gateway custom domain for the API. Create an Amazon Route 53 record set with a geoproximity routing policy for the API's custom domain. Increase the geographic bias to the maximum allowed value.

B. Deploy an API Gateway regional API endpoint in the us-east-1 Region. Integrate the API Gateway API with a public Application Load Balancer (ALB). Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator. Associate the endpoint with the ALCreate an Amazon Route 53 alias record set that points the custom domain name to the DNS name that is assigned to the accelerator.

C. Deploy an API Gateway regional API endpoint in every AWS Region where the company's product is deployed. Create an API Gateway custom domain in each Region for the deployed API Gateway API. Create an Amazon Route 53 record set that has a latency routing policy for every deployed API Gateway custom domain.

D. Deploy an API Gateway edge-optimized API endpoint in the us-east-1 Region. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the CloudFront distribution with an alternate domain name. Specify the API Gateway Invoke URL as the origin domain. Create an Amazon Route 53 alias record set with a simple routing policy. Point the routing policy to the CloudFront distribution domain name.
questions.explanation: Deploying Regional API Gateway endpoints in every product Region provides independent, redundant API availability. Regional custom domain names are specific to their Regions, but the same custom domain can be used across multiple Regional deployments. Route 53 latency-based routing directs each user to the deployed Region with the lowest latency, optimizing request performance while retaining a single custom domain URL. questions.questionText: A company runs its applications in containers. The company discovers that some container images lack required security configurations. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that creates a standard base image. The solution must publish the base image weekly to the us-west-2, us-east-2, and eu-central-1 Regions. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an EC2 Image Builder pipeline that uses a container recipe to build the image. Configure the pipeline to distribute the image to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository in us-west-2. Configure ECR replication from us-west-2 to us-east-2 and from us-east-2 to eu-central-1. Configure the pipeline to run weekly.

B. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses an AWS CodeBuild project to build the image. Use AWS CodeDeploy to publish the image to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository in us-west-2. Configure ECR replication from us-west-2 to us-east-2 and from us-east-2 to eu-central-1. Configure the pipeline to run weekly.

C. Create an EC2 Image Builder pipeline that uses a container recipe to build the image. Configure the pipeline to distribute the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories in all three Regions. Configure the pipeline to run weekly.

D. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses an AWS CodeBuild project to build the image. Use AWS CodeDeploy to publish the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories in all three Regions. Configure the pipeline to run weekly.
questions.explanation: EC2 Image Builder can use a container recipe to create a standardized container image and can distribute that image directly to Amazon ECR repositories in each specified Region on a recurring schedule. Amazon ECR replication does not chain: an image replicated from one Region to another is not replicated again to a third Region. Direct distribution settings for all three target Regions therefore satisfy the publishing requirement. questions.questionText: A company sends AWS Network Firewall flow logs to an Amazon S3 bucket and analyzes the flow logs with Amazon Athena. The company must transform the flow logs and add extra data before the logs are delivered to the existing S3 bucket. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS Lambda function to transform the data and to write a new object to the existing S3 bucket. Configure the Lambda function with an S3 trigger for the existing S3 bucket. Specify all object create events for the event type. Acknowledge the recursive invocation.

B. Enable Amazon EventBridge notifications on the existing S3 bucket. Create a custom EventBridge event bus. Create an EventBridge rule that is associated with the custom event bus. Configure the rule to react to all object create events for the existing S3 bucket and to invoke an AWS Step Functions workflow. Configure a Step Functions task to transform the data and to write the data into a new S3 bucket.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is associated with the default EventBridge event bus. Configure the rule to react to all object create events for the existing S3 bucket. Define a new S3 bucket as the target for the rule. Create an EventBridge input transformation to customize the event before passing the event to the rule target.

D. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that is configured with an AWS Lambda transformer. Specify the existing S3 bucket as the destination. Change the Network Firewall logging destination from Amazon S3 to Kinesis Data Firehose.
questions.explanation: AWS Network Firewall can send logs to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream, with one firewall log delivered as one Firehose record. Firehose can invoke an AWS Lambda function to transform incoming records before it delivers the transformed data to its Amazon S3 destination, allowing the existing bucket to receive the enriched logs directly. questions.questionText: A company runs its staging website on an Amazon EC2 instance backed by Amazon EBS storage. The company needs rapid recovery with minimal data loss if the EC2 instance experiences network-connectivity problems or power failures. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Add the instance to an EC2 Auto Scaling group with the minimum, maximum, and desired capacity set to 1.
B. Add the instance to an EC2 Auto Scaling group with a lifecycle hook to detach the EBS volume when the EC2 instance shuts down or terminates.
C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed System metric and select the EC2 action to recover the instance.
D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed Instance metric and select the EC2 action to reboot the instance.
questions.explanation: Loss of network connectivity and loss of system power cause EC2 system status check failures. A CloudWatch alarm that monitors StatusCheckFailed_System and invokes the Recover action automatically recovers the instance from underlying host issues; attached EBS volumes are preserved during recovery. questions.questionText: A company is building an application that will generate log events. The log events include five distinct metrics every one-tenth of a second and create a large volume of data. The company must configure the application to write the logs to Amazon Timestream. The company will run a daily query against the Timestream table. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the FASTEST query performance?
options: A. Use batch writes to write multiple log events in a single write operation.
B. Write each log event as a single write operation.
C. Treat each log as a single-measure record.
D. Treat each log as a multi-measure record.
E. Configure the memory store retention period to be longer than the magnetic store retention period.
F. Configure the memory store retention period to be shorter than the magnetic store retention period.
questions.explanation: Batching multiple records per write operation improves Timestream ingestion performance. Multi-measure records store metrics emitted at the same time in one row, producing more compact storage and lower query latency for multi-metric queries. The memory store is optimized for fast point-in-time queries, while the magnetic store supports long-term storage and fast analytical queries; a daily analytical workload therefore uses a shorter memory-store retention period than magnetic-store retention. LEARN MORE Amazon Timestream data modeling Amazon Timestream write batching

questions.questionText: A company’s application development team uses Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances as bastion hosts. Inbound SSH access to the bastion hosts is limited to specific IP addresses, as specified in the associated security groups. The company’s security team wants to receive a notification if security group rules are changed to permit SSH access from any IP address. What should a DevOps engineer do to satisfy this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with a source of aws.cloudtrail and the event name AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target.

B. Enable Amazon GuardDuty and check the findings for security groups in AWS Security Hub. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule with a custom pattern that matches GuardDuty events with an output of NON_COMPLIANT. Define an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as the target.

C. Create an AWS Config rule by using the restricted-ssh managed rule to check whether security groups disallow unrestricted incoming SSH traffic. Configure automatic remediation to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

D. Enable Amazon Inspector. Include the Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures-1.1 rules package to check the security groups that are associated with the bastion hosts. Configure Amazon Inspector to publish a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule restricted-ssh evaluates EC2 security groups and is NON_COMPLIANT when incoming SSH is permitted from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0. AWS Config can send notifications to an Amazon SNS topic, and an automatic remediation action can use an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to publish the message. questions.questionText: A company performs vulnerability scans for all Amazon EC2 instances across multiple accounts. The accounts belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. Each account’s VPCs are connected to a shared transit gateway, and the VPCs route internet traffic through a central egress VPC. The company has enabled Amazon Inspector in a delegated administrator account and enabled scanning for every member account. A DevOps engineer finds that some EC2 instances appear in the Amazon Inspector not scanning tab. Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to fix this issue?
options: A. Verify that AWS Systems Manager Agent is installed and is running on the EC2 instances that Amazon Inspector is not scanning.
B. Associate the target EC2 instances with security groups that allow outbound communication on port 443 to the AWS Systems Manager service endpoint.
C. Grant inspector:StartAssessmentRun permissions to the IAM role that the DevOps engineer is using.
D. Configure EC2 Instance Connect for the EC2 instances that Amazon Inspector is not scanning.
E. Associate the target EC2 instances with instance profiles that grant permissions to communicate with AWS Systems Manager.
F. Create a managed-instance activation. Use the Activation Code and the Activation ID to register the EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: Amazon Inspector uses AWS Systems Manager and SSM Agent for agent-based EC2 vulnerability scanning. An instance must have SSM Agent installed and running, an IAM instance profile that permits Systems Manager to manage it (such as one with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy), and outbound HTTPS connectivity to Systems Manager endpoints. Allowing outbound port 443 through the central egress path enables that required SSM communication. LEARN MORE Scanning Amazon EC2 instances with Amazon Inspector Assessing Amazon Inspector coverage of your AWS environment

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory as its identity provider (IdP). The company requires that all infrastructure be defined and deployed through AWS CloudFormation. A DevOps engineer must create a fleet of Windows-based Amazon EC2 instances to host an application. The DevOps engineer has created a CloudFormation template containing an EC2 launch template, IAM role, EC2 security group, and EC2 Auto Scaling group. The DevOps engineer must implement a solution that joins every EC2 instance to the domain of the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. In the CloudFormation template, create an AWS::SSM::Document resource that joins the EC2 instance to the AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain by using the parameters for the existing directory. Update the launch template to include the SSMAssociation property to use the new SSM document. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.

B. In the CloudFormation template, update the launch template to include specific tags that propagate on launch. Create an AWS::SSM::Association resource to associate the AWS-JoinDirectoryServiceDomain Automation runbook with the EC2 instances that have the specified tags. Define the required parameters to join the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.

C. Store the existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain connection details in AWS Secrets Manager. In the CloudFormation template, create an AWS::SSM::Association resource to associate the AWS-CreateManagedWindowsInstanceWithApproval Automation runbook with the EC2 Auto Scaling group. Pass the ARNs for the parameters from Secrets Manager to join the domain. Attach the AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess and SecretsManagerReadWrite AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.

D. Store the existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain administrator credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. In the CloudFormation template, update the EC2 launch template to include user data. Configure the user data to pull the administrator credentials from Secrets Manager and to join the AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore and SecretsManagerReadWrite AWS managed policies to the IAM role that the EC2 instances use.
questions.explanation: An AWS Systems Manager State Manager association can target managed instances by tags, and dynamic targets are applied as new instances are added to an Auto Scaling group. Associating the AWS-JoinDirectoryServiceDomain document with launch-propagated tags therefore automatically joins each new Windows instance to the existing AWS Managed Microsoft AD domain. The instance role needs AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore for Systems Manager management and AmazonSSMDirectoryServiceAccess for the SSM agent to access Directory Service and create the domain computer account. LEARN MORE AWS::SSM::Association - AWS CloudFormation AWS::SSM::Association Target - AWS CloudFormation

questions.questionText: A company is adopting AWS CodeDeploy to automate application deployments for a Java-Apache Tomcat application that uses an Apache Webserver. The development team began with a proof of concept, created a deployment group for a developer environment, and completed functional tests in the application. Afterward, the team will create further deployment groups for staging and production. The current log level is configured in the Apache settings, but the team wants to modify this configuration dynamically during deployment so it can apply different log-level configurations by deployment group, without maintaining a separate application revision for each group. How can these requirements be fulfilled with the LEAST management overhead and without needing different script versions for each deployment group?
options: A. Tag the Amazon EC2 instances depending on the deployment group. Then place a script into the application revision that calls the metadata service and the EC2 API to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference the script as part of the AfterInstall lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.

B. Create a script that uses the CodeDeploy environment variable DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ NAME to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the BeforeInstall lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.

C. Create a CodeDeploy custom environment variable for each environment. Then place a script into the application revision that checks this environment variable to identify which deployment group the instance is part of. Use this information to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the ValidateService lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.

D. Create a script that uses the CodeDeploy environment variable DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_ID to identify which deployment group the instance is part of to configure the log level settings. Reference this script as part of the Install lifecycle hook in the appspec.yml file.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy makes the DEPLOYMENT_GROUP_NAME environment variable available to lifecycle hook scripts. A single script can branch on that deployment-group name and update the Apache LogLevel setting for the applicable environment. AWS documents this exact Apache log-level use case and specifies invoking the script in the BeforeInstall lifecycle event, so the same application revision and script can serve development, staging, and production. questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CloudFormation stacks to deploy updates to its application. The stacks contain different resources, including AWS Auto Scaling groups, Amazon EC2 instances, Application Load Balancers (ALBs), and other resources required to launch and maintain independent stacks. Changes to application resources outside CloudFormation stack updates are prohibited. The company recently tried to update the application stack by using the AWS CLI. The stack update failed and produced this error message: “ERROR: both the deployment and the CloudFormation stack rollback failed. The deployment failed because the following resource(s) failed to update: [AutoScalingGroup].” The stack remains in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED status. Which solution will resolve this issue?
options: A. Update the subnet mappings that are configured for the ALBs. Run the aws cloudformation update-stack-set AWS CLI command.
B. Update the IAM role by providing the necessary permissions to update the stack. Run the aws cloudformation continue-update-rollback AWS CLI command.
C. Submit a request for a quota increase for the number of EC2 instances for the account. Run the aws cloudformation cancel-update-stack AWS CLI command.
D. Delete the Auto Scaling group resource. Run the aws cloudformation rollback-stack AWS CLI command.
questions.explanation: For an UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED stack caused by insufficient permissions, the CloudFormation service role must be granted the permissions needed to modify the affected resources. The aws cloudformation continue-update-rollback command then resumes the failed rollback and returns the stack to a recoverable state. LEARN MORE Troubleshooting CloudFormation Continue rolling back an update

Continue rolling back an update

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodePipeline to deploy an application. Under a new guideline, a member of the company’s security team must approve all application changes before they are deployed to production. The approval must be logged and retained. Which combination of actions meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure CodePipeline to write actions to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
B. Configure CodePipeline to write actions to an Amazon S3 bucket at the end of each pipeline stage.
C. Create an AWS CloudTrail trail to deliver logs to Amazon S3.
D. Create a CodePipeline custom action to invoke an AWS Lambda function for approval. Create a policy that gives the security team access to manage CodePipeline custom actions.
E. Create a CodePipeline manual approval action before the deployment step. Create a policy that grants the security team access to approve manual approval stages.
questions.explanation: A CodePipeline manual approval action before the production deployment stops pipeline execution until an IAM-authorized security-team member approves or rejects it. AWS CloudTrail records CodePipeline API calls, including the approval response, and a trail can continuously deliver those audit events to an Amazon S3 bucket for retention. LEARN MORE Add a manual approval action to a stage Logging CodePipeline API calls with AWS CloudTrail

questions.questionText: A company modified the AWS CloudFormation template for a critical business application. The stack update failed because of an error in the modified template, and AWS CloudFormation automatically started rolling back the stack. Later, a DevOps engineer found that the application remained unavailable and that the stack was in the UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED state. Which combination of actions should the DevOps engineer take to allow the stack rollback to finish successfully?
options: A. Attach the AWSCloudFormationFullAccess IAM policy to the AWS CloudFormation role.
B. Automatically recover the stack resources by using AWS CloudFormation drift detection.
C. Issue a ContinueUpdateRollback command from the AWS CloudFormation console or the AWS CLI.
D. Manually adjust the resources to match the expectations of the stack.
E. Update the existing AWS CloudFormation stack by using the original template.
questions.explanation: For an UPDATE_ROLLBACK_FAILED stack, CloudFormation could not restore one or more resources to their prior state. The failed resource condition may need to be corrected manually, after which ContinueUpdateRollback resumes the rollback and can return the stack to UPDATE_ROLLBACK_COMPLETE. questions.questionText: A company develops a stateless application that uses an Application Load Balancer in front of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The Auto Scaling group uses a fully prebuilt custom AMI, and the EC2 instances have no custom bootstrapping process. The AMI used by the Auto Scaling group was recently deleted. The Auto Scaling group's scaling activities are failing because the AMI ID no longer exists. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create a new launch template that uses the new AMI.
B. Update the Auto Scaling group to use the new launch template.
C. Reduce the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity to 0.
D. Increase the Auto Scaling group's desired capacity by 1.
E. Create a new AMI from a running EC2 instance in the Auto Scaling group.
F. Create a new AMI by copying the most recent public AMI of the operating system that the EC2 instances use.
questions.explanation: A running instance launched from the fully prebuilt custom AMI retains the application configuration needed to create a replacement AMI. A launch template must specify an AMI ID, and associating the new launch template with the Auto Scaling group causes subsequent instance launches to use the valid replacement configuration. questions.questionText: A company that is growing rapidly needs to scale to meet developers’ demand for AWS development environments. Development environments are currently created manually through the AWS Management Console. The networking team manages networking infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation and exports stack output values for the Amazon VPC and every subnet. The development environments follow common standards, including Application Load Balancers, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups, security groups, and Amazon DynamoDB tables. To meet demand, the DevOps engineer wants to automate development-environment creation. Because the infrastructure needed to support the application is expected to expand, the deployed infrastructure must be easy to update. CloudFormation will be used to create a template for the development environments. Which approach will satisfy these requirements and rapidly deliver consistent AWS environments to developers?
options: A. Use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions in the Resources section of the template to retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values. Use CloudFormation StackSets for the development environments, using the Count input parameter to indicate the number of environments needed. Use the UpdateStackSet command to update existing development environments.

B. Use nested stacks to define common infrastructure components. To access the exported values, use TemplateURL to reference the networking team’s template. To retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values, use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions in the Parameters section of the root template. Use the CreateChangeSet and ExecuteChangeSet commands to update existing development environments.

C. Use nested stacks to define common infrastructure components. Use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions with the resources of the nested stack to retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values. Use the CreateChangeSet and ExecuteChangeSet commands to update existing development environments.

D. Use Fn::ImportValue intrinsic functions in the Parameters section of the root template to retrieve Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) and subnet values. Define the development resources in the order they need to be created in the CloudFormation nested stacks. Use the CreateChangeSet. and ExecuteChangeSet commands to update existing development environments.
questions.explanation: Nested stacks provide reusable common infrastructure components for each environment. Fn::ImportValue retrieves the VPC and subnet output values exported by the separate networking stack when used by the relevant nested-stack resources. CloudFormation change sets support reviewing and executing updates across the nested-stack hierarchy with CreateChangeSet and ExecuteChangeSet. LEARN MORE Fn::ImportValue - AWS CloudFormation Change sets for nested stacks - AWS CloudFormation

questions.questionText: A company is rolling out a standardized security baseline across its AWS accounts. The accounts belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to deploy consistent IAM roles and policies across every existing and future account in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Enable AWS Control Tower in the management account. Configure AWS Control Tower Account Factory customization to deploy the required IAM roles and policies to all accounts.

B. Activate trusted access for AWS CloudFormation StackSets in Organizations. In the management account, create a stack set that has service-managed permissions to deploy the required IAM roles and policies to all accounts. Enable automatic deployment for the stack set.

C. In each member account, create IAM roles that have permissions to create and manage resources. In the management account, create an AWS CloudFormation stack set that has self-managed permissions to deploy the required IAM roles and policies to all accounts. Enable automatic deployment for the stack set.

D. In the management account, create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline. Configure the pipeline to use AWS CloudFormation to automate the deployment of the required IAM roles and policies. Set up cross-account IAM roles to allow CodePipeline to deploy resources in the member accounts.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions use AWS Organizations integration and service-linked roles, so IAM roles do not need to be manually created and maintained in each member account. Enabling automatic deployment deploys the StackSet to accounts added to the targeted organization or organizational units in the future. questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer operates an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that builds and deploys a web application on AWS. The pipeline contains a source stage, a build stage, and a deploy stage. When correctly deployed, a request to the web application's home-page URL returns an HTTP 200 OK response code. Recently, after CodePipeline deployed the application, the home page returned an HTTP 503 response code. The DevOps engineer must add an automated test to the pipeline. The test must verify that the application returns an HTTP 200 OK response code after deployment, and the pipeline must fail if that response code is not returned during the test. The DevOps engineer has added a CheckURL stage after the deploy stage. What should the DevOps engineer do next to implement the automated test?
options: A. Configure the CheckURL stage to use an Amazon CloudWatch action. Configure the action to use a canary synthetic monitoring check on the application URL and to report a success or failure to CodePipeline.

B. Create an AWS Lambda function to check the response code status of the URL and to report a success or failure to CodePipeline. Configure an action in the CheckURL stage to invoke the Lambda function.
C. Configure the CheckURL stage to use an AWS CodeDeploy action. Configure the action with an input artifact that is the URL of the application and to report a success or failure to CodePipeline.

D. Deploy an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API that checks the response code status of the URL and that reports success or failure to CodePipeline. Configure the CheckURL stage to use the AWS Device Farm test action and to provide the API Gateway HTTP API as an input artifact.
questions.explanation: An AWS Lambda invoke action can run a function after deployment, pass it the application URL through user parameters, make the HTTP request, and test for status code 200. The function reports PutJobSuccessResult when the check passes and PutJobFailureResult when it fails, causing CodePipeline to continue or fail accordingly. AWS provides this exact URL health-check pattern for Lambda actions in CodePipeline. LEARN MORE Invoke an AWS Lambda function in a pipeline in CodePipeline AWS Lambda invoke action reference
learnMore: Invoke an AWS Lambda function in a pipeline in CodePipeline

questions.questionText: A company identifies unusual login attempts across many of its AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that notifies the company's security team when multiple failed login attempts happen. The DevOps engineer has already created an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic and subscribed the security team to that SNS topic. Which solution will deliver the notification with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send management events to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter to match failed ConsoleLogin events. Create a CloudWatch alarm that is based on the metric filter. Configure an alarm action to send messages to the SNS topic.

B. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send management events to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon Athena query that returns a failure if the query finds failed logins in the logs in the S3 bucket. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to periodically run the query. Create a second EventBridge rule to detect when the query fails and to send a message to the SNS topic.

C. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send data events to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Create a CloudWatch logs metric filter to match failed ConsoleLogin events. Create a CloudWatch alarm that is based on the metric filter. Configure an alarm action to send messages to the SNS topic.

D. Configure AWS CloudTrail to send data events to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure an Amazon S3 event notification for the s3:ObjectCreated event type. Filter the event type by ConsoleLogin failed events. Configure the event notification to forward to the SNS topic.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudTrail records ConsoleLogin activity as a management event. Sending those events to CloudWatch Logs enables a metric filter to match failed console logins, and a CloudWatch alarm can evaluate the count over a specified threshold and publish its alarm notification to Amazon SNS. AWS documents this as the standard alarm pattern for AWS Management Console sign-in failures. LEARN MORE Logging management events - AWS CloudTrail Creating CloudWatch alarms for CloudTrail events: examples

Creating CloudWatch alarms for CloudTrail events: examples

questions.questionText: A company has built a web application that runs seasonal sales on public holidays. The application is deployed on AWS and uses AWS services for storage, database, compute, and encryption. During seasonal sales, the company anticipates heavy network traffic from a large number of users. The company needs insights into any unexpected behavior during the sale. A DevOps team wants to review the insights when anomalous behavior is detected during the sale. The team also wants recommended actions to resolve the anomalous behavior. The recommendations must address the provisioned infrastructure and potential issues that could occur in the future. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Enable Amazon DevOps Guru in the AWS account. Determine the coverage for DevOps Guru for all supported AWS resources in the account. Use the DevOps Guru dashboard to find the analysis, recommendations, and related metrics.
B. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure Amazon DevOps Guru to send notifications about important events to the company when anomalies are identified.

C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Store Amazon CloudWatch logs, AWS CloudTrail data, and AWS Config data in the S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to generate insights on the data. Create a dashboard by using Amazon QuickSight.
D. Configure email message reports for an Amazon QuickSight dashboard. Schedule and send the email reports to the company.
E. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Configure Amazon Athena to send query results about important events to the company when anomalies are identified.
questions.explanation: Amazon DevOps Guru is a fully managed service that analyzes covered AWS resources for anomalous operational behavior and produces insights containing recommendations and related operational data. Its proactive insights recommend actions for issues predicted to occur in the future. Configuring Amazon SNS as the DevOps Guru notification target alerts the DevOps team when important events, including anomaly and insight updates, occur. This uses built-in managed analysis and notification capabilities without operating a custom log analytics and dashboard solution. High level DevOps Guru workflow

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. The organization root has a child OU named Department. The Department OU has a child OU named Engineering. The default FullAWSAccess policy is attached to the root, the Department OU, and the Engineering OU. The company has many AWS accounts in the Engineering OU. Each account has an administrative IAM role with the AdministratorAccess IAM policy attached. The default FullAWSAccessPolicy is also attached to every account. A DevOps engineer plans to remove the FullAWSAccess policy from the Department OU. The DevOps engineer will replace it with a policy that includes an Allow statement for every Amazon EC2 API operation. What will be the effect of this change on the permissions of the administrative 1AM roles?
options: A. All API actions on all resources will be allowed.
B. All API actions on EC2 resources will be allowed. All other API actions will be denied.
C. All API actions on all resources will be denied.
D. All API actions on EC2 resources will be denied. All other API actions will be allowed.
questions.explanation: SCPs act as a permissions boundary, and a requested action requires an explicit SCP Allow at every level from the organization root through each OU to the account. Replacing FullAWSAccess at the Department OU with an EC2-only Allow limits accounts below that OU to EC2 API operations. AdministratorAccess IAM policies cannot grant permissions that the applicable SCPs do not allow. AWS Organizations SCP evaluation LEARN MORE SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: An IT team created an AWS CloudFormation template so that others in the company can quickly and consistently deploy and terminate an application. The template provisions an Amazon EC2 instance with a user data script that installs the application, plus an Amazon S3 bucket the application uses to serve static webpages while it runs. All resources must be removed when the CloudFormation stack is deleted. However, CloudFormation reports an error during stack deletion, and the S3 bucket created by the stack remains. How can the team resolve the error in the MOST efficient way, ensuring that all resources are deleted without errors?
options: A. Add a DelelionPolicy attribute to the S3 bucket resource, with the value Delete forcing the bucket to be removed when the stack is deleted.

B. Add a custom resource with an AWS Lambda function with the DependsOn attribute specifying the S3 bucket, and an IAM role. Write the Lambda function to delete all objects from the bucket when RequestType is Delete.
C. Identify the resource that was not deleted. Manually empty the S3 bucket and then delete it.
D. Replace the EC2 and S3 bucket resources with a single AWS OpsWorks Stacks resource. Define a custom recipe for the stack to create and delete the EC2 instance and the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 buckets must be empty before CloudFormation can delete them. A Lambda-backed custom resource can handle CloudFormation's Delete request and remove the bucket objects. With a dependency on the bucket, the custom resource is deleted first, so the bucket is empty when CloudFormation deletes it. AWS::S3::Bucket documentation LEARN MORE AWS::S3::Bucket - AWS CloudFormation CloudFormation custom resource request and response reference
learnMore: CloudFormation custom resource request and response reference

questions.questionText: A company has one developer who writes code for an automated deployment pipeline. The developer stores the source code for each project in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company plans to add more developers, but is worried about code conflicts and lost work. The company also wants to create a test environment to deploy newer code versions for testing and enable developers to automatically deploy to both environments when code changes in the repository. What is the MOST efficient way to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Use feature branches to develop new features and pull requests to merge code to testing and main branches.

B. Create another S3 bucket for each project for testing code, and use an AWS Lambda function to promote code changes between testing and production buckets. Enable versioning on all buckets to prevent code conflicts.

C. Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each project, and use the main branch for production and test code with different deployment pipelines for each environment. Use feature branches to develop new features.

D. Enable versioning and branching on each S3 bucket, use the main branch for production code, and create a testing branch for code deployed to testing. Have developers use each branch for developing in each environment.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeCommit provides Git-based repositories with branches and pull requests, allowing developers to isolate feature work, review and merge changes, and manage merge conflicts rather than overwriting source files in S3. A testing branch can drive deployment to the test environment, while the main branch represents production-ready code and drives production deployment after approved merges. CodePipeline can automatically detect repository changes and start deployments. LEARN MORE Working with pull requests in AWS CodeCommit repositories Working with branches in AWS CodeCommit repositories

Working with branches in AWS CodeCommit repositories

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage several AWS accounts that its developers use. The company requires all data to be encrypted in transit. Several Amazon S3 buckets created in developer accounts permit unencrypted connections. A DevOps engineer must enforce encryption in transit for every existing S3 bucket created in accounts in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to each account. Route all outbound requests from the AWS environment through the firewall. Deploy a policy to block access to all outbound requests on port 80.

B. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy an AWS Network Firewall firewall to each account. Route all inbound requests to the AWS environment through the firewall. Deploy a policy to block access to all inbound requests on port 80.

C. Turn on AWS Config for the organization. Deploy a conformance pack that uses the s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only managed rule and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Use a runbook that adds a bucket policy statement to deny access to an S3 bucket when the value of the aws:SecureTransport condition key is false.

D. Turn on AWS Config for the organization. Deploy a conformance pack that uses the s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only managed rule and an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook. Use a runbook that adds a bucket policy statement to deny access to an S3 bucket when the value of the s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id condition key is null.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only evaluates whether S3 bucket policies require SSL/TLS and marks buckets that permit HTTP requests as noncompliant. A bucket-policy statement that explicitly denies requests when aws:SecureTransport is false blocks unencrypted HTTP access, thereby enforcing HTTPS/TLS for data in transit. The s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption-aws-kms-key-id condition instead relates to AWS KMS server-side encryption at rest. LEARN MORE s3-bucket-ssl-requests-only - AWS Config Managing access based on HTTP or HTTPS requests - Amazon S3

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations and AWS Control Tower to manage all of its AWS accounts. The company has the Enterprise Support plan. A DevOps engineer uses Account Factory for Terraform (AFT) to provision new accounts. When the new accounts are provisioned, the DevOps engineer observes that their support plan is set to the Basic Support plan. The DevOps engineer must implement a solution that provisions the new accounts with the Enterprise Support plan. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use an AWS Config conformance pack to deploy the account-part-of-organizations AWS Config rule and to automatically remediate any noncompliant accounts.
B. Create an AWS Lambda function to create a ticket for AWS Support to add the account to the Enterprise Support plan. Grant the Lambda function the support:ResolveCase permission.
C. Add an additional value to the control_tower_parameters input to set the AWSEnterpriseSupport parameter as the organization's management account number.
D. Set the aft_feature_enterprise_support feature flag to True in the AFT deployment input configuration. Redeploy AFT and apply the changes.
questions.explanation: AFT provides an Enterprise Support feature option that enrolls accounts provisioned by AFT in the AWS Enterprise Support plan. Enable that option by setting aft_feature_enterprise_support to true in the AFT deployment input configuration and redeploying AFT. questions.questionText: An ecommerce company operates a large number of Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS)-backed Amazon EC2 instances. To reduce manual effort across all instances, a DevOps engineer must automate restart actions when EC2 instance retirement events are scheduled. How can this be achieved?
options: A. Create a scheduled Amazon EventBridge rule to run an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that checks if any EC2 instances are scheduled for retirement once a week. If the instance is scheduled for retirement, the runbook will hibernate the instance.
B. Enable EC2 Auto Recovery on all of the instances. Create an AWS Config rule to limit the recovery to occur during a maintenance window only.

C. Reboot all EC2 instances during an approved maintenance window that is outside of standard business hours. Set up Amazon CloudWatch alarms to send a notification in case any instance is failing EC2 instance status checks.
D. Set up an AWS Health Amazon EventBridge rule to run AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks that stop and start the EC2 instance when a retirement scheduled event occurs.
questions.explanation: For an Amazon EBS-backed EC2 instance scheduled for retirement, an AWS Health retirement event can be matched by an Amazon EventBridge rule. The rule can invoke an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook, such as AWS-RestartEC2Instance, to stop and start the instance automatically, moving it to replacement hardware. questions.questionText: A company operates a legacy application. A DevOps engineer must automate building the deployable artifact for that legacy application. The solution must save the deployable artifact in an existing Amazon S3 bucket so future deployments can reference it. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Create a custom Docker image that contains all the dependencies for the legacy application. Store the custom Docker image in a new Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Configure a new AWS CodeBuild project to use the custom Docker image to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.

B. Launch a new Amazon EC2 instance. Install all the dependencies for the legacy application on the EC2 instance. Use the EC2 instance to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.

C. Create a custom EC2 Image Builder image. Install all the dependencies for the legacy application on the image. Launch a new Amazon EC2 instance from the image. Use the new EC2 instance to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.

D. Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster with an AWS Fargate profile that runs in multiple Availability Zones. Create a custom Docker image that contains all the dependencies for the legacy application. Store the custom Docker image in a new Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Use the custom Docker image inside the EKS cluster to build the deployable artifact and to save the artifact to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild provides managed build environments, supports custom Docker images from Amazon ECR for build dependencies, and can store build output artifacts in an Amazon S3 bucket. This provides repeatable artifact builds without the operational overhead of administering EC2 instances, AMIs, or an Amazon EKS cluster. questions.questionText: A company has an AWS Organizations organization that includes workload accounts containing enterprise applications. The company centrally manages users from an operations account, and no users can be created in the workload accounts. The company recently added an operations team and needs to give its members administrator access to every workload account. Which combination of actions will provide this access?
options: A. Create a SysAdmin role in the operations account. Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to the role. Modify the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action from the workload accounts.
B. Create a SysAdmin role in each workload account. Attach the AdministratorAccess policy to the role. Modify the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action from the operations account.
C. Create an Amazon Cognito identity pool in the operations account. Attach the SysAdmin role as an authenticated role.
D. In the operations account, create an IAM user for each operations team member.

E. In the operations account, create an IAM user group that is named SysAdmins. Add an IAM policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole action for the SysAdmin role in each workload account. Add all operations team members to the group.
F. Create an Amazon Cognito user pool in the operations account. Create an Amazon Cognito user for each operations team member.
questions.explanation: A cross-account IAM role must reside in each target workload account, have AdministratorAccess permissions, and trust principals from the operations account. Operations team members require IAM identities in the operations account, with a group policy granting sts:AssumeRole on each workload account’s SysAdmin role. This supplies temporary administrator credentials without creating users in workload accounts. questions.questionText: A company uses the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) to define its application. It uses a pipeline consisting of AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild to deploy the CDK application. The company wants to add unit tests to the pipeline to test various infrastructure components. It must ensure that deployment proceeds only when no unit test fails. Which combination of steps will enforce the testing requirement in the pipeline?
options: A. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Set the OnFailure phase property to ABORT.
B. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Add the --rollback true flag to the cdk deploy command.
C. Update the CodeBuild build phase commands to run the tests then to deploy the application. Add the --require-approval any-change flag to the cdk deploy command.
D. Create a test that uses the AWS CDK assertions module. Use the template.hasResourceProperties assertion to test that resources have the expected properties.
E. Create a test that uses the cdk diff command. Configure the test to fail if any resources have changed.
questions.explanation: AWS CDK’s assertions module supports unit testing of synthesized CloudFormation templates, and template.hasResourceProperties verifies that a resource of a specified type has the expected properties. CodeBuild’s on-failure: ABORT setting aborts the build phase when a test command fails, preventing the subsequent cdk deploy command from running.
