questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations and AWS Control Tower to manage its multi-account environment. The company needs to deploy standardized security controls and compliance policies throughout all of its AWS accounts and AWS Regions. Any modifications to these controls must automatically be applied to every account at the same time. The required security controls and compliance policies are defined in the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) as a security controls construct. Which solution will deploy these controls across every account and Region with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an AWS CDK app that includes an AWS CloudFormation StackSets construct. Configure the StackSets construct to use the security controls construct as its template. Specify the target accounts and Regions. Create automation to deploy the CDK app to create and manage the CloudFormation stack set.

B. Create an AWS CDK app that synthesizes an AWS CloudFormation template from the security controls construct. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update a CloudFormation stack set when changes are made to the security controls construct.

C. Convert the security controls construct to an AWS CloudFormation macro. Create a CloudFormation stack set that references the macro and deploys the macro to all target accounts. Use Organizations to automatically add new accounts to the stack set’s list of target accounts.

D. Use AWS Control Tower to create a customized landing zone that includes configurations from the security controls construct. Configure AWS Control Tower to automatically enroll new accounts and to apply the landing zone template.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation StackSets deploy the same CloudFormation template to specified AWS accounts and Regions, and an update to a StackSet updates its associated stack instances. When used with AWS Organizations service-managed permissions, StackSets can target organizational accounts or OUs without manually managing per-account deployment roles. A CDK app can define and manage the StackSet from the security-controls construct, allowing one managed deployment path to propagate control changes consistently. LEARN MORE AWS CloudFormation StackSets concepts Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions
learnMore: Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions

questions.questionText: A company has deployed a new REST API using Amazon API Gateway. The company uses the API to access confidential data. The API must be accessible only from specific VPCs within the company. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create and attach a resource policy to the API Gateway API. Configure the resource policy to allow only the specific VPC IDs.
B. Add a security group to the API Gateway API. Configure the inbound rules to allow only the specific VPC IP address ranges.
C. Create and attach an IAM role to the API Gateway API. Configure the IAM role to allow only the specific VPC IDs.
D. Add an ACL to the API Gateway API. Configure the outbound rules to allow only the specific VPC IP address ranges.
questions.explanation: An API Gateway resource policy can restrict REST API invocation to specified VPCs by using the aws:SourceVpc condition. API Gateway does not use directly attached security groups or network ACLs for this control, and IAM roles govern identities rather than limiting access by VPC ID. LEARN MORE Control access to a REST API with API Gateway resource policies API Gateway resource policy examples

API Gateway resource policy examples

questions.questionText: A company is developing a serverless application that uses AWS Lambda functions for data processing. A BeginResponse Lambda function initializes data in response to particular application events. The company must ensure that a large number of Lambda functions are invoked after the BeginResponse Lambda function executes. Each Lambda function must be invoked in parallel and depend only on the outputs of the BeginResponse Lambda function. Each Lambda function requires invocation retry logic and must be able to fine-tune concurrency without data loss. Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Modify the BeginResponse Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic before the BeginResponse Lambda function finishes running. Subscribe all Lambda functions that need to invoke after the BeginResponse Lambda function runs to the SNS topic. Subscribe any new Lambda functions to the SNS topic.

B. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for each Lambda function that needs to run after the BeginResponse Lambda function runs. Subscribe each Lambda function to its own SQS queue. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe each SQS queue to the SNS topic. Modify the BeginResponse function to publish to the SNS topic when it finishes running.

C. Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for each Lambda function that needs to run after the BeginResponse Lambda function runs. Subscribe the Lambda function to the SQS queue. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic for each SQS queue. Subscribe the SQS queues to the SNS topics. Modify the BeginResponse function to publish to the SNS topics when the function finishes running.

D. Create an AWS Step Functions Standard Workflow. Configure states in the workflow to invoke the Lambda functions sequentially. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Modify the BeginResponse Lambda function to publish to the SNS topic before the Lambda function finishes running. Create a new Lambda function that is subscribed to the SNS topic and that invokes the Step Functions workflow.
questions.explanation: An Amazon SNS topic provides publish/subscribe fan-out, sending the BeginResponse output to a dedicated Amazon SQS queue for each downstream Lambda function. SQS durably retains each consumer's message until successful processing, while Lambda SQS event source mappings provide retry handling and configurable maximum concurrency independently for each queue-triggered function. This allows all downstream functions to process in parallel without one consumer's throughput or failures affecting the others. Using Lambda with Amazon SQS Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings LEARN MORE Using Lambda with Amazon SQS Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings

Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings

questions.questionText: A company stores 100 GB of log data in .csv format in an Amazon S3 bucket. SQL developers need to query this data and create graphs to visualize it. The SQL developers also require an efficient, automated method to store metadata from the .csv file. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the LEAST effort?
options: A. Filter the data through AWS X-Ray to visualize the data.
B. Filter the data through Amazon QuickSight to visualize the data.
C. Query the data with Amazon Athena.
D. Query the data with Amazon Redshift.
E. Use the AWS Glue Data Catalog as the persistent metadata store.
F. Use Amazon DynamoDB as the persistent metadata store.
questions.explanation: Amazon Athena runs standard SQL queries directly against data in Amazon S3 without infrastructure to manage. Amazon QuickSight creates graphical data visualizations. The AWS Glue Data Catalog is the persistent metadata store, and AWS Glue crawlers can automatically infer CSV schemas and populate it with table metadata. LEARN MORE Amazon Athena Documentation Adding visuals to QuickSight analyses

questions.questionText: A company operates a fleet of Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS account. The company uses an AWS Systems Manager Automation task across those EC2 instances. In the latest patch cycle, several EC2 instances entered an error state because they did not have enough available disk space. A DevOps engineer must ensure that the EC2 instances have sufficient free disk space during future patching operations. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Ensure that the Amazon CloudWatch agent is installed on all EC2 instances.
B. Create a cron job that is installed on each EC2 instance to periodically delete temporary files.

C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch log group for the EC2 instances. Configure a cron job that is installed on each EC2 instance to write the available disk space to a CloudWatch log stream for the relevant EC2 instance.
D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to monitor available disk space on all EC2 instances. Add the alarm as a safety control to the Systems Manager Automation task.
E. Create an AWS Lambda function to periodically check for sufficient available disk space on all EC2 instances by evaluating each EC2 instance's respective Amazon CloudWatch log stream.
questions.explanation: The Amazon CloudWatch agent collects Linux disk metrics, including disk_free and disk_used_percent, which make available disk capacity observable for each instance. A CloudWatch alarm can evaluate those metrics and be applied to a Systems Manager Automation execution as an alarm control; if the alarm enters the ALARM state, Systems Manager cancels the automation. This prevents the patch process from continuing when the configured disk-space threshold is not met. LEARN MORE Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent Run an automated operation powered by Systems Manager Automation
learnMore: Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent
Run an automated operation powered by Systems Manager Automation

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer must configure a blue/green deployment for an existing three-tier application. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon RDS database. The EC2 instances run behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and are in an Auto Scaling group. The DevOps engineer has created a launch template and an Auto Scaling group for the blue environment. The DevOps engineer has also created a launch template and an Auto Scaling group for the green environment. Each Auto Scaling group deploys to its corresponding blue or green target group. The target group also determines which software—blue or green—is loaded onto the EC2 instances. The ALB can be configured to direct traffic to either the blue environment’s target group or the green environment’s target group. An Amazon Route 53 record for www.example.com points to the ALB. The deployment must shift all traffic at once from the software on the blue environment’s EC2 instances to the newly deployed software on the green environment’s EC2 instances. What should the DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Start a rolling restart of the Auto Scaling group for the green environment to deploy the new software on the green environment’s EC2 instances. When the rolling restart is complete, use an AWS CLI command to update the ALB to send traffic to the green environment’s target group.

B. Use an AWS CLI command to update the ALB to send traffic to the green environment’s target group. Then start a rolling restart of the Auto Scaling group for the green environment to deploy the new software on the green environment’s EC2 instances.

C. Update the launch template to deploy the green environment’s software on the blue environment’s EC2 instances. Keep the target groups and Auto Scaling groups unchanged in both environments. Perform a rolling restart of the blue environment’s EC2 instances.

D. Start a rolling restart of the Auto Scaling group for the green environment to deploy the new software on the green environment’s EC2 instances. When the rolling restart is complete, update the Route 53 DNS to point to the green environment’s endpoint on the ALB.
questions.explanation: The green instances must be updated before they receive production requests. After the rolling restart completes, updating the ALB listener’s forward action to the green target group performs the blue/green cutover at the traffic-routing layer. The Route 53 record should remain pointed at the existing ALB; the listener selects the target group that receives requests. AWS documents that an ALB listener’s default forward action can be changed to a different target group by using the modify-listener CLI command. LEARN MORE Edit a listener rule for your Application Load Balancer modify-listener — AWS CLI Command Reference

modify-listener — AWS CLI Command Reference

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is working on a data-archival project that requires migrating on-premises data to an Amazon S3 bucket. The DevOps engineer creates a script that incrementally archives on-premises data older than 1 month to Amazon S3. Data transferred to Amazon S3 is removed from the on-premises location. The script uses the S3 PutObject operation. During a code review, the DevOps engineer realizes that the script does not confirm whether the data was copied successfully to Amazon S3. The DevOps engineer must modify the script to ensure that data is not corrupted in transit. The script must use MD5 checksums to validate data integrity before deleting the on-premises data. Which solutions for the script meet these requirements?
options: A. Check the returned response for the VersionId. Compare the returned VersionId against the MD5 checksum.
B. Include the MD5 checksum within the Content-MD5 parameter. Check the operation call’s return status to find out if an error was returned.
C. Include the checksum digest within the tagging parameter as a URL query parameter.
D. Check the returned response for the ETag. Compare the returned ETag against the MD5 checksum.
E. Include the checksum digest within the Metadata parameter as a name-value pair. After upload, use the S3 HeadObject operation to retrieve metadata from the object.
questions.explanation: The Content-MD5 parameter supplies a Base64-encoded MD5 digest that Amazon S3 uses as an end-to-end integrity check; S3 rejects the upload if the received payload does not match. For applicable single-part PutObject uploads, the returned ETag is the MD5 digest of the object data, so it can be compared with the locally calculated MD5 checksum. LEARN MORE PutObject - Amazon S3 API Reference Checking object integrity for data uploads in Amazon S3
learnMore: PutObject - Amazon S3 API Reference
Checking object integrity for data uploads in Amazon S3

questions.questionText: A company deploys an application to Amazon EC2 instances. The application runs Amazon Linux 2 and uses AWS CodeDeploy. The application has the following code-repository file structure: The files section of the appspec.yml file contains the following: What will be the deployment result for the config.txt file?
options: A. The config.txt file will be deployed to only /var/www/html/config/config.txt.
B. The config.txt file will be deployed to /usr/local/src/config.txt and to /var/www/html/config/config.txt.
C. The config.txt file will be deployed to only /usr/local/src/config.txt.
D. The config.txt file will be deployed to /usr/local/src/config.txt and to /var/www/html/application/web/config.txt.
questions.explanation: The explicit file mapping deploys config/config.txt to /usr/local/src/config.txt. The source: / mapping copies the complete CodeDeploy revision bundle to /var/www/html while preserving its relative directory structure, which also deploys the file to /var/www/html/config/config.txt. questions.questionText: A company runs an application in two AWS Regions. The application currently uses an Amazon S3 bucket in the primary Region for data storage. A DevOps engineer must ensure that the application is highly available across both Regions. The engineer has created a new S3 bucket in the secondary Region. Both S3 buckets must contain all existing and future objects. The application must be able to fail over between the Regions without data loss. Which combination of steps satisfies these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create a new IAM role that allows the Amazon S3 and S3 Batch Operations service principals to assume the role that has the necessary permissions for S3 replication.
B. Create a new IAM role that allows the AWS Batch service principal to assume the role that has the necessary permissions for S3 replication.
C. Create an S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) rule on the source S3 bucket. Configure the rule to use the IAM role for Amazon S3 to replicate to the target S3 bucket.
D. Create a two-way replication rule on the source S3 bucket. Configure the rule to use the IAM role for Amazon S3 to replicate to the target S3 bucket.

E. Create an AWS Batch job that has an AWS Fargate orchestration type. Configure the job to use the IAM role for AWS Batch. Specify a Bash command to use the AWS CLI to synchronize the contents of the source S3 bucket and the target S3 bucket
F. Create an operation in S3 Batch Operations to replicate the contents of the source S3 bucket to the target S3 bucket. Configure the operation to use the IAM role for Amazon S3.
questions.explanation: S3 Batch Replication performs the on-demand backfill of objects that existed before replication was configured, while two-way S3 replication keeps objects synchronized when writes occur in either Regional bucket during failover. The IAM role must trust Amazon S3 for live replication and S3 Batch Operations for the Batch Replication job, and must grant the required permissions on both buckets. questions.questionText: A company regularly creates Docker images for an application and stores them in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). The company creates both tagged and untagged images. The company needs a solution that automatically deletes images that have not been updated for a long time and are not used frequently. The solution must retain at least a specified number of images. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Use Amazon S3 Lifecycle policies on the ECR repository to automatically delete images based on image age or the absence of tags on the image.
B. Use Amazon ECR lifecycle policies to delete images based on age or the number of images that need to be to retained in the repository.
C. Configure an AWS Lambda function to run a schedule to delete images based on age or the number of images that need to be retained in the repository.
D. Use AWS Systems Manager to run a script by using the aws:executeScript action to automatically delete images based on image age or the absence of tags on the image.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR lifecycle policies natively automate image expiration for tagged, untagged, or all images. Policy rules can expire images by age and can use an image-count threshold that retains the configured number of images, avoiding custom scheduled code or scripts. LEARN MORE Automate the cleanup of images by using lifecycle policies in Amazon ECR Lifecycle policy properties in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A company stores sensitive API keys in AWS Secrets Manager for use by an AWS Lambda function. Each time the Lambda function is invoked, it retrieves the API keys and calls an external service. The Secrets Manager secret is encrypted with the default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. A DevOps engineer must update the infrastructure so that only the Lambda function’s execution role can access the values in Secrets Manager. The solution must follow the principle of least privilege. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Update the default KMS key for Secrets Manager to allow only the Lambda function’s execution role to decrypt
B. Create a KMS customer managed key that trusts Secrets Manager and allows the Lambda function's execution role to decrypt. Update Secrets Manager to use the new customer managed key
C. Create a KMS customer managed key that trusts Secrets Manager and allows the account's root principal to decrypt. Update Secrets Manager to use the new customer managed key
D. Ensure that the Lambda function’s execution role has the KMS permissions scoped on the resource level. Configure the permissions so that the KMS key can encrypt the Secrets Manager secret
E. Remove all KMS permissions from the Lambda function’s execution role
questions.explanation: The AWS managed key aws/secretsmanager has a service-defined key policy that cannot be changed. A customer managed KMS key permits a restrictive key policy that authorizes Secrets Manager and grants kms:Decrypt only to the Lambda execution role. Removing separate KMS permissions from the Lambda role prevents broader or redundant IAM grants while the narrowly scoped customer-managed-key policy supplies the required decrypt authorization. LEARN MORE Secret encryption and decryption in AWS Secrets Manager Change a key policy - AWS Key Management Service
learnMore: Secret encryption and decryption in AWS Secrets Manager

questions.questionText: A company intends to use AWS Systems Manager documents to bootstrap physical laptops for developers. The bootstrap code is stored in GitHub. A DevOps engineer has already created a Systems Manager activation, installed the Systems Manager agent using the registration code, and installed an activation ID on all the laptops. Which set of steps should be performed next?
options: A. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the AWS-RunShellScript command to copy the files from GitHub to Amazon S3, then use the aws-downloadContent plugin with a sourceType of S3.
B. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the aws-configurePackage plugin with an install action and point to the Git repository.
C. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the aws-downloadContent plugin with a sourceType of GitHub and sourceInfo with the repository details.
D. Configure the Systems Manager document to use the aws:softwareInventory plugin and run the script from the Git repository.
questions.explanation: The aws:downloadContent Systems Manager document plugin downloads scripts and SSM documents from remote locations, including GitHub. With sourceType set to GitHub, sourceInfo supplies the GitHub repository details needed to retrieve the bootstrap content. LEARN MORE Command document plugin reference - AWS Systems Manager
learnMore: Command document plugin reference - AWS Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A company has several AWS accounts in an AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled. The company’s DevOps administrator must improve security throughout all of the company’s AWS accounts. The administrator must identify the most frequently used users and roles across every account. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create a new organization trail in AWS CloudTrail. Configure the trail to send log events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule for the userIdentity.arn log field. View the results in CloudWatch Contributor Insights.

B. Create an unused access analysis for the organization by using AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer. Review the analyzer results and determine if each finding has the intended level of permissions required for the workload.

C. Create a new organization trail in AWS CloudTrail. Create a table in Amazon Athena that uses partition projection. Load the Athena table with CloudTrail data. Query the Athena table to find the top users and roles.
D. Generate a Service access report for each account by using Organizations. From the results, pull the last accessed date and last accessed by account fields to find the top users and roles.
questions.explanation: An AWS CloudTrail organization trail centralizes events from the organization’s management and member accounts and can deliver them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. A CloudWatch Contributor Insights rule can analyze CloudTrail JSON logs by the high-cardinality userIdentity.arn field and rank the identities generating the most activity, which identifies the top users and roles without maintaining an Athena data-query workflow. LEARN MORE CloudTrail concepts — Organization trails Create a Contributor Insights rule in CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A healthcare services company is worried about increasing software-licensing costs for an application that monitors patient wellness. The company wants to establish an audit process to ensure that the application runs only on Amazon EC2 Dedicated Hosts. A DevOps engineer must create a workflow that audits the application for compliance. Which steps should the engineer take to satisfy this requirement with the LEAST administrative overhead?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager Configuration Compliance. Use calls to the put-compliance-items API action to scan and build a database of noncompliant EC2 instances based on their host placement configuration. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store these instance IDs for fast access. Generate a report through Systems Manager by calling the list-compliance-summaries API action.

B. Use custom Java code running on an EC2 instance. Set up EC2 Auto Scaling for the instance depending on the number of instances to be checked. Send the list of noncompliant EC2 instance IDs to an Amazon SQS queue. Set up another worker instance to process instance IDs from the SQS queue and write them to Amazon DynamoDUse an AWS Lambda function to terminate noncompliant instance IDs obtained from the queue, and send them to an Amazon SNS email topic for distribution.

C. Use AWS Config. Identify all EC2 instances to be audited by enabling Config Recording on all Amazon EC2 resources for the region. Create a custom AWS Config rule that triggers an AWS Lambda function by using the "config-rule-change -triggered" blueprint. Modify the Lambda evaluateCompliance() function to verify host placement to return a NON_COMPLIANT result if the instance is not running on an EC2 Dedicated Host. Use the AWS Config report to address noncompliant instances.

D. Use AWS CloudTrail. Identify all EC2 instances to be audited by analyzing all calls to the EC2 RunCommand API action. Invoke an AWS Lambda function that analyzes the host placement of the instance. Store the EC2 instance ID of noncompliant resources in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. Generate a report by querying the RDS instance and exporting the query results to a CSV text file.
questions.explanation: AWS Config records EC2 resource configuration and supports change-triggered custom rules that invoke AWS Lambda to evaluate AWS::EC2::Instance resources. The rule can evaluate the instance’s host placement and report any instance not running on an EC2 Dedicated Host as NON_COMPLIANT; AWS Config retains and reports the resulting compliance status. This avoids operating custom polling infrastructure, databases, queues, and report-generation workflows. AWS also documents AWS Config as a source for Dedicated Host and instance configuration data used for license reporting. LEARN MORE Track Amazon EC2 Dedicated Host configuration changes using AWS Config Creating AWS Config Custom Lambda Rules

Creating AWS Config Custom Lambda Rules

questions.questionText: A company’s DevOps engineer is developing an AWS Lambda function to handle notifications from an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. The Lambda function will process the notification messages and write their contents to an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance. During testing, a database administrator accidentally shut down the DB instance. While the database was unavailable, the company lost several SNS notification messages delivered during that period. The DevOps engineer must prevent notification-message loss in the future. Which solutions meet this requirement?
options: A. Replace the RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with an Amazon DynamoDB table.
B. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as a destination of the Lambda function.
C. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue for the SNS topic.
D. Subscribe an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue to the SNS topic. Configure the Lambda function to process messages from the SQS queue.
E. Replace the SNS topic with an Amazon EventBridge event bus. Configure an EventBridge rule on the new event bus to invoke the Lambda function for each event.
questions.explanation: For asynchronous Lambda invocations, a function error such as a failed database write is retried and, after all processing attempts fail, an Amazon SQS on-failure destination can retain the failed invocation record. Subscribing an SQS queue to the SNS topic also durably buffers each notification so that Lambda can retrieve and retry processing when the database becomes available. An SNS dead-letter queue addresses failed delivery to an SNS subscription, not a database-write failure after Lambda has accepted the notification. LEARN MORE Capturing records of Lambda asynchronous invocations Subscribing an Amazon SQS queue to an Amazon SNS topic
learnMore: Capturing records of Lambda asynchronous invocations
Subscribing an Amazon SQS queue to an Amazon SNS topic

questions.questionText: A company has an AWS account named PipelineAccount. This account manages a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. It uses an IAM role named CodePipeline_Service_Role and creates an artifact that is stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uses a customer managed AWS KMS key to encrypt objects in the S3 bucket. A DevOps engineer wants to configure the pipeline to use an AWS CodeDeploy application in an AWS account named CodeDeployAccount to deploy the produced artifact. The DevOps engineer updates the KMS key policy to give the CodeDeployAccount account permission to use the key. The DevOps engineer configures an IAM role named DevOps_Role in the CodeDeployAccount account that can access the CodeDeploy resources required by the pipeline. The DevOps engineer updates an Amazon EC2 instance role operating in the CodeDeployAccount account to allow access to the S3 bucket and the KMS key in the PipelineAccount account. Which additional steps will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the CodeDeployAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the PipelineAccount account to assume the role. Update the CodePipeline_Service_Role IAM role to grant permission to assume the DevOps_Role role.

B. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the CodeDeployAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the PipelineAccount account to assume the role. Update the DevOps_Role IAM role to grant permission to assume CodePipelfne_Service_Role role.

C. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the PipelineAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the PipelineAccount account to assume the role. Update the CodePipeline_Service_Role IAM to grant permission to assume the DevOps_Role role.

D. Update the S3 bucket policy to grant the CodeDeployAccount account access to the S3 bucket. Configure the DevOps_Role IAM role to have an IAM trust policy that allows the CodeDeployAccount account to assume the role. Update the CodePipeline_Service_Role IAM role to grant permission to assume the DevOps_Role role.
questions.explanation: For a pipeline in one account to use CodeDeploy resources in another account, the artifact bucket policy must allow the target account to access the artifacts. The cross-account role in the CodeDeploy account must trust the CodePipeline service role in the pipeline account, and that service role needs sts:AssumeRole permission on the cross-account role. This gives the assumed DevOps_Role access to the CodeDeploy resources and artifact bucket while the EC2 instance role retrieves and decrypts the deployment artifact. LEARN MORE Create a pipeline in CodePipeline that uses resources from another AWS account

questions.questionText: A company is organized into teams. Every team has an AWS account, and all accounts belong to one AWS Organizations organization. Each team must retain complete administrative permissions in its AWS account. Each team must also be able to use only AWS services that the company has approved. AWS services receive approval through a request-and-approval process. How should a DevOps engineer configure the accounts to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to provision IAM policies in each account to deny access to restricted AWS services. In each account, configure AWS Config rules that ensure that the policies are attached to IAM principals in the account.

B. Use AWS Control Tower to provision the accounts into OUs within the organization. Configure AWS Control Tower to enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure IAM Identity Center to provide administrative access. Include deny policies on user roles for restricted AWS services.
C. Place all the accounts under a new top-level OU within the organization. Create an SCP that denies access to restricted AWS services. Attach the SCP to the OU.
D. Create an SCP that allows access to only approved AWS services. Attach the SCP to the root OU of the organization. Remove the FullAWSAccess SCP from the root OU of the organization.
questions.explanation: Service control policies (SCPs) define the maximum permissions available to identities in affected AWS accounts, including administrators. Replacing the default FullAWSAccess SCP at the organization root with an SCP that explicitly allows only approved services implements an organization-wide allow list; services not explicitly allowed are unavailable until the policy is updated after approval. LEARN MORE SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations
learnMore: SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations
Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: A company needs to proactively monitor and respond to AWS service issues that could affect an application. The company must correlate AWS Health events with application performance metrics and configure automated alerts. The solution must enable the company to archive events, test the application's latency under different scenarios, and create custom metrics. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CloudTrail to log all AWS Health events. Use Amazon Athena to query the logs and to correlate the logs with application metrics stored in Amazon Timestream for LiveAnalytics. Set up AWS Chatbot for real-time notifications.

B. Use Amazon EventBridge to route AWS Health events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a metric filter for AWS Health events. Create custom metrics in CloudWatch that are based on application performance data. Set up CloudWatch alarms that correlate AWS Health events with the custom metrics.

C. Configure the AWS Health Dashboard to send notifications to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Use AWS Lambda to correlate the notifications with metrics and to update custom metrics in Amazon CloudWatch. Set up CloudWatch alarms for the custom metrics. Use AWS Systems Manager for automated remediation.

D. Configure AWS X-Ray to trace AWS Health events and application performance. Use Amazon QuickSight to visualize the correlations between events and metrics. Use Amazon GuardDuty to detect anomalies in the application's behavior and to provide alerts.
questions.explanation: Amazon EventBridge can receive AWS Health events and route them to CloudWatch Logs for retention. CloudWatch Logs metric filters turn matching Health log events into CloudWatch metrics, while CloudWatch custom metrics represent application performance data. CloudWatch alarms can evaluate the resulting metrics, including metric-math expressions, to alert on the relationship between AWS Health events and application performance. CloudWatch also supports Synthetics canaries for scheduled endpoint and latency testing. LEARN MORE Monitoring events in AWS Health with Amazon EventBridge Creating metrics from log events using filters

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage 10 AWS accounts. All features are enabled, and trusted access for AWS CloudFormation is enabled. A DevOps engineer must use CloudFormation to deploy an IAM role to the Organizations management account and to every member account in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has service-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target.
B. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has service-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target. Deploy a separate CloudFormation stack in the Organizations management account.
C. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has self-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target.
D. Create a CloudFormation StackSet that has self-managed permissions. Set the root OU as a deployment target. Deploy a separate CloudFormation stack in the Organizations management account.
questions.explanation: CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions use AWS Organizations integration and avoid manually creating and managing cross-account IAM roles. Targeting the root organizational unit deploys to all member accounts, but service-managed StackSets do not deploy stacks to the Organizations management account. A separate CloudFormation stack in that account is required. LEARN MORE Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions Prerequisites for using CloudFormation StackSets
learnMore: Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions
Prerequisites for using CloudFormation StackSets

questions.questionText: A company operates an application that streams logs to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. The logs must remain available for the team to search in CloudWatch for at least 30 days. Logs must be retrievable with low latency for at least 90 days. After 180 days, retrieving logs is uncommon and latency does not matter. A DevOps engineer creates an Amazon S3 bucket to store the logs. Log-availability metrics and data protection are important to the company. Which solution satisfies these requirements in the MOST cost-effective manner?
options: A. Configure the log group to have a retention period of 30 days and to use the infrequent access log class. Create a CloudWatch metric stream that uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to send log events to the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move objects to Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days and to Amazon Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 180 days.

B. Configure the log group to have a retention period of 30 days and to use the infrequent access log class. Create a CloudWatch metric stream that uses Amazon Data Firehose to send log events to the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move objects to Amazon S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 90 days and to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 180 days.

C. Configure the log groups to have a retention period of 30 days. Create a CloudWatch subscription filter that uses Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to send log events to the S3 bucket by writing files. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move objects to Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days and to Amazon S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 180 days.

D. Configure the log groups to have a retention period of 30 days. Create a CloudWatch subscription filter that uses Amazon Data Firehose to send log events to the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move objects to Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 90 days and to Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 180 days.
questions.explanation: A CloudWatch Logs subscription filter can stream log events to Amazon Data Firehose, which delivers them to Amazon S3. Subscription filters are supported only for CloudWatch Logs Standard log groups. S3 Standard-IA provides millisecond access and resiliency across multiple Availability Zones, fitting the low-latency retention period. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is the lowest-cost S3 archival storage class and is designed for data accessed less than once a year with retrieval times of hours, fitting rarely retrieved logs after 180 days. CloudWatch Logs subscriptions Amazon S3 storage classes LEARN MORE Real-time processing of log data with subscriptions Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes

questions.questionText: A company has recently migrated its application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that uses Amazon EC2 instances. The company configured the application for automatic scaling based on CPU utilization. The application generates memory errors during heavy loads. It also does not scale out sufficiently to accommodate the increased load. The company must collect and analyze application memory metrics over time. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Attach the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy managed IAM policy to the IAM instance profile that the cluster uses.
B. Attach the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy managed IAM policy to a service account role for the cluster.

C. Collect performance metrics by deploying the unified Amazon CloudWatch agent to the existing EC2 instances in the cluster. Add the agent to the AMI for any new EC2 instances that are added to the cluster.
D. Collect performance logs by deploying the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry collector as a DaemonSet.
E. Analyze the pod_memory_utilization Amazon CloudWatch metric in the ContainerInsights namespace by using the Service dimension.
F. Analyze the node_memory_utilization Amazon CloudWatch metric in the ContainerInsights namespace by using the ClusterName dimension.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Container Insights collects EKS workload metrics through the CloudWatch agent. For EC2 worker nodes, the agent requires CloudWatch permissions from the worker-node IAM instance profile, and the agent must be deployed on both current and subsequently added EC2 instances. The pod_memory_utilization metric supports a Service dimension, enabling memory analysis for the application service over time; node_memory_utilization instead measures worker-node memory usage. LEARN MORE Amazon EKS and Kubernetes Container Insights metrics Container Insights
learnMore: Container Insights

questions.questionText: A company has configured AWS CodeArtifact repositories with public upstream repositories. The company’s development team uses open-source dependencies from these repositories on the internal network. The security team recently identified a critical vulnerability in the latest version of a package consumed by the development team. The security team has created a patched version to remediate the vulnerability. The company must stop the vulnerable version from being downloaded. The company must also permit the security team to publish the patched version. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Update the status of the affected CodeArtifact package version to unlisted.
B. Update the status of the affected CodeArtifact package version to deleted.
C. Update the status of the affected CodeArtifact package version to archived.
D. Update the CodeArtifact package origin control settings to allow direct publishing and to block upstream operations.
E. Update the CodeArtifact package origin control settings to block direct publishing and to allow upstream operations.
questions.explanation: Deleting the affected package version removes it from the repository, prevents downloads, and allows that version to be republished. CodeArtifact package origin controls must allow direct publishing so the security team can publish the patched package, and must block upstream operations so the vulnerable version cannot be retained again from a public upstream repository. An Unlisted version can still be downloaded, while an Archived version cannot be republished through a package manager because it remains in the repository. LEARN MORE Packages overview - CodeArtifact Editing package origin controls - CodeArtifact
learnMore: Packages overview - CodeArtifact
Editing package origin controls - CodeArtifact

questions.questionText: A company's video-streaming platform usage has grown from 10,000 users per day to 50,000 users per day across multiple countries. The company deploys the streaming platform on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). The EKS workload scales to thousands of nodes during peak viewing periods. The company's users report instances of unauthorized logins. Users also report unexpected interruptions and logouts from the platform. The company wants extra security measures for the entire platform. The company also requires a summarized view of resource behaviors and interactions across the company's full AWS environment. The summarized view must display login attempts, API calls, and network traffic. The solution must allow network-traffic analysis while minimizing log-management overhead. The solution must also rapidly investigate any potential malicious behavior associated with the EKS workload. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Enable Amazon GuardDuty for EKS Audit Log Monitoring. Enable AWS CloudTrail logs. Store the EKS audit logs and CloudTrail log files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to create an external table. Use Amazon QuickSight to create a dashboard.
B. Enable Amazon GuardDuty for EKS Audit Log Monitoring. Enable Amazon Detective in the company's AWS account. Enable EKS audit logs from optional source packages in Detective.

C. Enable Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights. Enable AWS CloudTrail logs. Store the EKS audit logs and CloudTrail log files in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to create an external table. Use Amazon QuickSight to create a dashboard.
D. Enable Amazon GuardDuty for EKS Audit Log Monitoring. Enable Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights and VPC Flow Logs. Enable AWS CloudTrail logs.
questions.explanation: Amazon Detective automatically aggregates and visualizes login attempts, AWS API calls, VPC network traffic, and GuardDuty findings as a unified behavior graph, avoiding the need to manually enable or store the underlying CloudTrail and VPC Flow Logs for this analysis. Its optional EKS audit log data source adds EKS-cluster detail and correlates it with CloudTrail management events and VPC Flow Logs. GuardDuty EKS Audit Log Monitoring analyzes EKS audit activity and produces findings for potential threats, enabling rapid investigation in Detective. LEARN MORE What is Amazon Detective? Source data used in a Detective behavior graph

questions.questionText: An ecommerce company has selected AWS to host its new platform. The company’s DevOps team has begun creating an AWS Control Tower landing zone. The DevOps team has configured the identity store in AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to use an external identity provider (IdP) and configured SAML 2.0. The DevOps team needs a robust permissions model that follows the principle of least privilege. The model must let the team build and manage only its own resources. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Create IAM policies that include the required permissions. Include the aws:PrincipalTag condition key.
B. Create permission sets. Attach an inline policy that includes the required permissions and uses the aws:PrincipalTag condition key to scope the permissions.
C. Create a group in the IdP. Place users in the group. Assign the group to accounts and the permission sets in IAM Identity Center.
D. Create a group in the IdP. Place users in the group. Assign the group to OUs and IAM policies.
E. Enable attributes for access control in IAM Identity Center. Apply tags to users. Map the tags as key-value pairs.
F. Enable attributes for access control in IAM Identity Center. Map attributes from the IdP as key-value pairs.
questions.explanation: IAM Identity Center attribute-based access control can pass external IdP attributes as session tags. A custom policy in a permission set can use the aws:PrincipalTag condition key to allow actions only on resources whose tags match the user’s team attribute. Assigning the IdP group to the relevant AWS accounts and permission set grants those scoped permissions to the team members. LEARN MORE Checklist: Configuring ABAC in AWS using IAM Identity Center Create permission policies for ABAC in IAM Identity Center

questions.questionText: A company has a 24-hour RPO and a 10-minute RTO for a critical web application running on Amazon EC2 instances. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS account and wants to configure AWS Backup for its AWS environment. A DevOps engineer configures AWS Organizations for AWS Backup and creates a new centralized AWS account to hold the backups. Each EC2 instance has four attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. Which solution meets this requirement MOST securely?
options: A. Create encrypted backup vaults and customer managed AWS KMS keys in both accounts. Configure AWS Backup to create full EC2 backups as AMIs. Copy the backups to the centralized vault.
B. Create encrypted vaults in both accounts by using the source account's AWS KMS key. Configure AWS Backup to create EC2 AMIs. Copy the AMIs to the centralized vault.
C. Create backup vaults in both accounts. Use AWS managed keys for encryption. Configure AWS Backup to create EC2 AMIs. Copy the AMIs to the centralized vault.

D. Create encrypted vaults in both accounts. Use a customer managed KMS key in the source account. Use an AWS managed key in the centralized account. Configure AWS Backup to create EC2 AMIs. Copy the AMIs to the centralized vault.
questions.explanation: AWS Backup uses the encryption of the underlying EBS volumes for Amazon EC2 backups. EC2 is not fully managed by AWS Backup for this purpose, so cross-account backup copies cannot use AWS managed KMS keys: their key policies cannot be modified to authorize cross-account access. Customer managed KMS keys in both accounts allow the required key-policy permissions while encrypting the source and centralized backup vaults. An EC2 AMI backup captures the instance and its attached EBS volumes. LEARN MORE Encryption for backups in AWS Backup Creating backup copies across AWS accounts

Creating backup copies across AWS accounts

questions.questionText: A company operates a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. The company’s employees access the EC2 instances remotely by using the Remote Desktop Protocol (RDP). The company needs to collect metrics for the number of RDP sessions that employees initiate each day. Which combination of steps satisfies this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to EC2 Instance State-change Notification events.
B. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Specify the log group as a target for the EventBridge rule.
C. Create a flow log in VPC Flow Logs.
D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Specify the log group as a destination for the flow log.
E. Create a log group metric filter.
F. Create a log group subscription filter. Use EventBridge as the destination.
questions.explanation: VPC Flow Logs capture IP traffic to and from VPC network interfaces, including RDP traffic on TCP destination port 3389. Publishing the flow log to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group makes the records available to a CloudWatch Logs metric filter, which can match the RDP traffic pattern and increment a metric for daily session counts. questions.questionText: A company builds a container image in an AWS CodeBuild project by executing Docker commands. After building the container image, the CodeBuild project uploads it to an Amazon S3 bucket. The CodeBuild project has an IAM service role with permissions to access the S3 bucket. A DevOps engineer must replace the S3 bucket with an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository for storing the container images. The DevOps engineer creates an ECR private image repository in the same AWS Region as the CodeBuild project. The DevOps engineer updates the IAM service role with the permissions required to work with the new ECR repository. The DevOps engineer also adds new repository information to the docker build command and the docker push command used in the buildspec.yml file. When the CodeBuild project runs a build job, the job fails while trying to access the ECR repository. Which solution will resolve the failed access to the ECR repository?
options: A. Update the buildspec.yml file to log in to the ECR repository by using the aws ecr get-login-password AWS CLI command to obtain an authentication token. Update the docker login command to use the authentication token to access the ECR repository.

B. Add an environment variable of type SECRETS_MANAGER to the CodeBuild project. In the environment variable, include the ARN of the CodeBuild project's IAM service role. Update the buildspec.yml file to use the new environment variable to log in with the docker login command to access the ECR repository.
C. Update the ECR repository to be a public image repository. Add an ECR repository policy that allows the IAM service role to have access.
D. Update the buildspec.yml file to use the AWS CLI to assume the IAM service role for ECR operations. Add an ECR repository policy that allows the IAM service role to have access.
questions.explanation: Docker does not use IAM credentials directly to authenticate to an Amazon ECR private registry. The build must obtain an ECR authorization password with aws ecr get-login-password for the repository Region and provide it to docker login before pushing the image. AWS's CodeBuild ECR publishing example uses this exact authentication step. LEARN MORE Private registry authentication in Amazon ECR Publish Docker image to an Amazon ECR image repository

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances span multiple Availability Zones. The application was incorrectly configured in one Availability Zone, causing a partial application outage. A DevOps engineer changed the configuration so that unhealthy EC2 instances in one Availability Zone do not affect healthy EC2 instances in the other Availability Zones. The DevOps engineer must test the application's failover and change where the ALB directs traffic. During failover, the ALB must not send traffic to the Availability Zone in which the failure occurred. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Turn off cross-zone load balancing on the ALB. Use Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to start a zonal shift away from the Availability Zone.
B. Turn off cross-zone load balancing on the ALB’s target group. Use Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to start a zonal shift away from the Availability Zone.
C. Create an Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller resource set that uses the DNS hostname of the ALB. Start a zonal shift for the resource set away from the Availability Zone.
D. Create an Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller resource set that uses the ARN of the ALB’s target group. Create a readiness check that uses the ElbV2TargetGroupsCanServeTraffic rule.
questions.explanation: For an Application Load Balancer, cross-zone load balancing cannot be disabled at the load-balancer level, but it can be explicitly disabled at the target-group level. With cross-zone load balancing off for the target group, each load balancer node routes only to targets in its own Availability Zone. An ARC zonal shift for the ALB shifts traffic away from the impaired Availability Zone, preventing new traffic from being directed there. LEARN MORE Edit target group attributes for your Application Load Balancer Application Load Balancers - Amazon Application Recovery Controller (ARC)

questions.questionText: A company operates an application across multiple environments in one AWS account. An AWS CodePipeline pipeline uses a development Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster to test an application image from an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. The pipeline then promotes the image to a production ECS cluster. The company must move the production cluster to a separate AWS account in the same AWS Region. The production cluster must be able to download the images through a private connection. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon ECR VPC endpoints and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint. In the separate AWS account, create an ECR repository. Set the repository policy to allow the production ECS tasks to pull images from the main AWS account. Configure the production ECS task execution role to have permission to download the image from the ECR repository.

B. Set a repository policy on the production ECR repository in the main AWS account. Configure the repository policy to allow the production ECS tasks in the separate AWS account to pull images from the main account. Configure the production ECS task execution role to have permission to download the image from the ECR repository.
C. Configure ECR private image replication in the main AWS account. Activate cross-account replication. Define the destination account ID of the separate AWS account.

D. Use Amazon ECR VPC endpoints and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint. Set a repository policy on the production ECR repository in the main AWS account. Configure the repository policy to allow the production ECS tasks in the separate AWS account to pull images from the main account. Configure the production ECS task execution role to have permission to download the image from the ECR repository.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR repository policies can grant cross-account access to a source repository, while the ECS task execution role needs the relevant ECR permissions to authenticate and retrieve images. For private ECS image pulls, Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints provide private access to the ECR APIs and registry, and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint is required to retrieve the image layers that ECR stores in S3. questions.questionText: A company hosts an application on a single Amazon EC2 instance. The application's metadata is kept in Amazon S3 and must be retrieved whenever the instance is restarted. The instance must automatically restart or be relaunched if it becomes unresponsive. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for the StatusCheckFailed metric. Use the recover action to stop and start the instance. Use an S3 event notification to push the metadata to the instance when the instance is back up and running.
B. Configure AWS OpsWorks, and use the auto healing feature to stop and start the instance. Use a lifecycle event in OpsWorks to pull the metadata from Amazon S3 and update it on the instance.
C. Use EC2 Auto Recovery to automatically stop and start the instance in case of a failure. Use an S3 event notification to push the metadata to the instance when the instance is back up and running.
D. Use AWS CloudFormation to create an EC2 instance that includes the UserData property for the EC2 resource. Add a command in UserData to retrieve the application metadata from Amazon S3.
questions.explanation: AWS OpsWorks Stacks Auto Healing detects an unresponsive managed instance and automatically recovers it by stopping and starting an Amazon EBS-backed instance or replacing an instance-store-backed instance. OpsWorks lifecycle events run associated recipes during instance initialization and configuration, so a recipe can retrieve the required application metadata from Amazon S3 after recovery. questions.questionText: A company has an on-premises application written in Go. A DevOps engineer needs to migrate the application to AWS. The company's development team wants to support blue/green deployments and conduct A/B testing. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Deploy the application on an Amazon EC2 instance, and create an AMI of the instance. Use the AMI to create an automatic scaling launch configuration that is used in an Auto Scaling group. Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute traffic. When changes are made to the application, a new AMI will be created, which will initiate an EC2 instance refresh.

B. Use Amazon Lightsail to deploy the application. Store the application in a zipped format in an Amazon S3 bucket. Use this zipped version to deploy new versions of the application to Lightsail. Use Lightsail deployment options to manage the deployment.

C. Use AWS CodeArtifact to store the application code. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the application to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute the traffic to the EC2 instances. When making changes to the application, upload a new version to CodeArtifact and create a new CodeDeploy deployment.

D. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to host the application. Store a zipped version of the application in Amazon S3. Use that location to deploy new versions of the application. Use Elastic Beanstalk to manage the deployment options.
questions.explanation: AWS Elastic Beanstalk supports deployment of Go applications from application source bundles and provides managed deployment policies. Its traffic-splitting deployment policy launches new instances and sends a specified percentage of incoming traffic to the new application version during an evaluation period, while the remaining traffic continues to use the existing version. This supports controlled version testing and rollback, alongside blue/green-style deployment workflows. questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy applications to a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. In a recent deployment, several EC2 instances did not update successfully. A DevOps engineer needs to investigate the root cause of these failures and identify the specific deployment lifecycle events that had errors. What is the MOST operationally efficient method to access and analyze detailed deployment logs for troubleshooting?
options: A. Use SSH to connect to each EC2 instance that failed to update successfully. Read the logs from the CodeDeploy agent.
B. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to connect to each EC2 instance that failed to update successfully. Read the logs from the CodeDeploy agent.
C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store CodeDeploy logs. Update the appspec.yml file to copy logs to the S3 bucket. Query the S3 bucket by using Amazon Athena
D. Send CodeDeploy agent logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs by using the CloudWatch agent. Analyze the logs by using CloudWatch Logs Insights.
questions.explanation: The CloudWatch agent can send CodeDeploy agent logs from all target instances to Amazon CloudWatch Logs, providing a centralized view rather than requiring access to every failed instance. CloudWatch Logs Insights can then query and analyze those aggregated logs to identify errors in particular deployment lifecycle events. questions.questionText: An ecommerce company receives reports that its order history page is delayed in showing the processing status of orders. The order-processing system includes an AWS Lambda function that uses reserved concurrency. The Lambda function processes order messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and writes processed orders to an Amazon DynamoDB table. The DynamoDB table has auto scaling enabled for read and write capacity. Which actions should a DevOps engineer take to resolve this delay?
options: A. Check the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metric for the SQS queue. Increase the Lambda function concurrency limit.
B. Check the ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage metnc for the SQS queue Configure a redrive policy on the SQS queue.
C. Check the NumberOfMessagesSent metric for the SQS queue. Increase the SQS queue visibility timeout.
D. Check the WriteThrottleEvents metric for the DynamoDB table. Increase the maximum write capacity units (WCUs) for the table's scaling policy.
E. Check the Throttles metric for the Lambda function. Increase the Lambda function timeout.
questions.explanation: ApproximateAgeOfOldestMessage measures the age of the oldest unprocessed SQS message, so it reveals a queue-processing backlog. A reserved-concurrency setting can limit the number of simultaneous Lambda invocations available to consume that backlog. WriteThrottleEvents indicates DynamoDB writes exceeding provisioned write capacity. DynamoDB auto scaling operates only within its configured minimum and maximum WCU range, so raising the maximum WCU can allow the table to scale high enough to avoid write throttling. questions.questionText: A company runs AWS Storage Gateway in file gateway mode in front of an Amazon S3 bucket that multiple resources use. When business starts in the morning, users cannot see objects that a third party processed the previous evening. A DevOps engineer verifies that the data exists by checking the S3 bucket directly, but it does not appear in Storage Gateway. Which solution makes sure that all updated third-party files are available in the morning?
options: A. Configure a nightly Amazon EventBridge event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to run the RefreshCache command for Storage Gateway.
B. Instruct the third party to put data into the S3 bucket using AWS Transfer for SFTP.
C. Modify Storage Gateway to run in volume gateway mode.
D. Use S3 Same-Region Replication to replicate any changes made directly in the S3 bucket to Storage Gateway.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 File Gateway caches its S3 object inventory and does not automatically update that inventory for objects uploaded directly to the bucket outside the gateway workflow. Invoking RefreshCache refreshes the file share’s cached inventory to find added, removed, or replaced S3 objects; a nightly scheduled invocation therefore exposes the third-party updates before users begin work. LEARN MORE Refreshing Amazon S3 bucket object cache RefreshCache API Reference

RefreshCache API Reference

questions.questionText: A company operates application environments in multiple AWS accounts. Each environment account resides in a separate OU in AWS Organizations. A DevOps team manages the application deployment process across these environments. The process uses an AWS CodePipeline pipeline in a Shared Services account. All DevOps team members belong to the same user group and have administrative access to every account through AWS IAM Identity Center. A recent deployment issue in the development environment required the DevOps team to take manual actions. The subsequent deployment to the production environment caused an incident that made the pipeline fail, blocking new deployments for several hours. A DevOps engineer must ensure that only the pipeline can perform deployments in the production environment. The DevOps engineer must also be able to access the environment in an emergency. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Update the DevOps group to have the ReadOnlyAccess permission set for the production accounts. Configure the DevOps engineer user with a new permission set that has AdministratorAccess permissions and that allows the user to assume the pipeline role. Add an SCP that denies modification of resources by any entity other than the pipeline role.

B. Create an SCP that denies all write actions for the DevOps team members on the production OU. Configure a new user in IAM Identity Center for the DevOps engineer with a new permission set that has AdministratorAccess permissions. Add an SCP that denies modification of resources by any entity other than the pipeline role.

C. Update the DevOps group to be able to assume the pipeline role for the production accounts. Configure a new user in IAM Identity Center for the DevOps engineer with a new permission set that has AdministratorAccess permissions. Add an SCP that denies modification of resources by any entity other than the DevOps engineer.

D. Create an SCP that denies all write actions for the DevOps team members on the production OU. Use a specific tag to tag the resources that CodePipeline provisions. Add an SCP that denies modification of tagged resources by any entity other than the DevOps engineer.
questions.explanation: An SCP attached to the production OU can impose an explicit deny on resource modifications for every principal except the pipeline role. Assigning the DevOps group read-only production access prevents normal team members from making production changes. A separate emergency AdministratorAccess permission set for the designated engineer, with permission to assume the pipeline role, provides emergency access through the sole role exempted by the SCP. SCPs set the maximum permissions for principals in affected member accounts, and an explicit SCP deny overrides otherwise granted IAM permissions. LEARN MORE Service control policies (SCPs) Manage AWS accounts with permission sets

questions.questionText: AnyCompany uses AWS Organizations to create and manage multiple AWS accounts. AnyCompany recently acquired a smaller company, Example Corp. As part of the acquisition, Example Corp's single AWS account joined AnyCompany's management account through an Organizations invitation. AnyCompany moved the new member account into an OU dedicated to Example Corp. AnyCompany's DevOps engineer has an IAM user that assumes a role named OrganizationAccountAccessRole to access member accounts. This role is configured with a full-access policy. When the DevOps engineer attempts to use the AWS Management Console to assume the role in Example Corp's new member account, the DevOps engineer receives this error message: "Invalid information in one or more fields. Check your information or contact your administrator." Which solution will provide the DevOps engineer with access to the new member account?
options: A. In the management account, grant the DevOps engineer's IAM user permission to assume the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the new member account.

B. In the management account, create a new SCP. In the SCP, grant the DevOps engineer's IAM user full access to all resources in the new member account. Attach the SCP to the OU that contains the new member account.

C. In the new member account, create a new IAM role that is named OrganizationAccountAccessRole. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy to the role. In the role's trust policy, grant the management account permission to assume the role.
D. In the new member account, edit the trust policy for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role. Grant the management account permission to assume the role.
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations does not automatically create OrganizationAccountAccessRole in an existing account that joins an organization by invitation. The invited member account must have that cross-account role created manually, with the AdministratorAccess managed policy attached and a trust policy that permits the management account to assume it. Creating OrganizationAccountAccessRole for an invited account with AWS Organizations LEARN MORE Creating OrganizationAccountAccessRole for an invited account with AWS Organizations Managing account invitations with AWS Organizations

Managing account invitations with AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is evaluating the lowest-cost approach to build an image batch-processing cluster on AWS. The application cannot operate in Docker containers and must run on Amazon EC2. The batch job saves checkpoint data to an NFS volume and can tolerate interruptions. Setting up the cluster software from a generic EC2 Linux image requires 30 minutes. What is the MOST cost-effective solution?
options: A. Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. To complete the job, use an EC2 Auto Scaling group and an On-Demand pricing model to provision EC2 instances temporarily.
B. Use GlusterFS on EC2 instances for checkpoint data. To run the batch job, configure EC2 instances manually. When the job completes, shut down the instances manually.
C. Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. Use EC2 Fleet to launch EC2 Spot Instances, and utilize user data to configure the EC2 Linux instance on startup.
D. Use Amazon EFS for checkpoint data. Use EC2 Fleet to launch EC2 Spot Instances. Create a custom AMI for the cluster and use the latest AMI when creating instances.
questions.explanation: EC2 Spot Instances minimize compute cost for interruption-tolerant batch work. Amazon EFS provides managed, scalable shared file storage that EC2 Linux instances can mount through NFS, allowing checkpoint data to persist independently of interrupted instances. A custom AMI with the cluster software preconfigured eliminates the repeated 30-minute startup configuration cost, making Spot capacity launched through EC2 Fleet more cost-effective. LEARN MORE Create an EC2 Fleet Use Amazon EFS with Amazon EC2 Linux instances
