questions.questionText: A company runs sensitive workloads across AWS accounts that belong to the company’s AWS Organizations organization. The company uses an IP address range to allocate IP addresses for Amazon VPC CIDR blocks and all non-cloud hardware. The company requires a solution that prevents principals outside the company’s IP address range from taking AWS actions in the organization’s accounts. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Firewall Manager for the organization. Create an AWS Network Firewall policy that allows only source traffic from the company's IP address range. Set the policy scope to all accounts in the organization.
B. In Organizations, create an SCP that denies source IP addresses that are outside of the company’s IP address range. Attach the SCP to the organization's root.
C. Configure Amazon GuardDuty for the organization. Create a GuardDuty trusted IP address list for the company's IP range. Activate the trusted IP list for the organization.
D. In Organizations, create an SCP that allows source IP addresses that are inside of the company’s IP address range. Attach the SCP to the organization's root.
questions.explanation: A service control policy attached to the organization root can impose an explicit organization-wide guardrail on all member accounts. A Deny statement for all actions with a NotIpAddress condition on aws:SourceIp explicitly denies requests from source IP addresses outside the approved company CIDR range; explicit denies override otherwise applicable IAM permissions. SCPs attached at the root affect the accounts beneath it. LEARN MORE AWS: Denies access to AWS based on the source IP SCP evaluation
learnMore: SCP evaluation

questions.questionText: A company runs an internal application in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on Amazon EC2. The ECS cluster instances can access the public internet. The ECS tasks running on the cluster instances are configured to use images from both private Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories and a public ECR registry repository. A new security policy requires the company to eliminate the ECS cluster's direct internet access. The company must remove all NAT gateways and internet gateways from the VPC that hosts the cluster. A DevOps engineer must ensure that the ECS cluster can continue downloading images from both the public ECR registry and the private ECR repositories. Images from the public ECR registry must stay current. New image versions must be available to the ECS cluster within 24 hours after publication. Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an AWS CodeBuild project and a new private ECR repository for each image that is downloaded from the public ECR registry. Configure each project to pull the image from the public ECR repository and push the image to the new private ECR repository. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the CodeBuild project once every 24 hours. Update each task definition in the ECS cluster to refer to the new private ECR repository.

B. Create a new Amazon ECR pull through cache rule for each image that is downloaded from the public ECR registry. Create an AWS Lambda function that invokes each pull through cache rule. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes the Lambda function once every 24 hours. Update each task definition in the ECS cluster to refer to the image from the pull through cache.

C. Create a new Amazon ECR pull through cache rule for the public ECR registry. Update each task definition in the ECS cluster to refer to the image from the pull through cache. Ensure each public image has been downloaded through the pull through cache at least once before removing internet access from the VPC.
D. Create an Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoint for the public ECR repositories that are in the VPC.
E. Create an Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoint for the private ECR repositories that are in the VPC.
F. Create an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint in the VPC.
questions.explanation: An Amazon ECR pull-through cache stores public-registry images in the private ECR registry. Once an image has been pulled through the cache, later pulls are served from the cache without internet access; Amazon ECR checks the upstream registry for updates after the 24-hour cache-validation period. Downloading each needed public image before removing egress prevents the initial cache population from requiring internet access. Amazon ECS tasks on EC2 require Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints for private ECR access and an Amazon S3 gateway endpoint because ECR stores image layers in Amazon S3. LEARN MORE Sync an upstream registry with an Amazon ECR private registry Amazon ECR interface VPC endpoints (AWS PrivateLink)
learnMore: Sync an upstream registry with an Amazon ECR private registry

questions.questionText: A company operates an application with an Amazon EC2 and on-premises setup. A DevOps engineer must standardize patching across both environments. Company policy requires patching to occur only during non-business hours. Which combination of actions will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Add the physical machines into AWS Systems Manager using Systems Manager Hybrid Activations.
B. Attach an IAM role to the EC2 instances, allowing them to be managed by AWS Systems Manager.
C. Create IAM access keys for the on-premises machines to interact with AWS Systems Manager.
D. Run an AWS Systems Manager Automation document to patch the systems every hour
E. Use Amazon EventBridge scheduled events to schedule a patch window.
F. Use AWS Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to schedule a patch window.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Hybrid Activations register on-premises servers as managed nodes, while an IAM role attached to each EC2 instance grants Systems Manager the permissions required to manage it. Systems Manager Maintenance Windows define scheduled periods for potentially disruptive operations such as operating-system patching, allowing the patch task to run only during non-business hours. LEARN MORE AWS Systems Manager Hybrid Activations Managing EC2 instances with Systems Manager
learnMore: Managing EC2 instances with Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A media company runs several thousand Amazon EC2 instances in an AWS account. The company uses Slack and a shared email inbox for team communications and important updates. A DevOps engineer must send every AWS-scheduled EC2 maintenance notification to the Slack channel and the shared inbox. The solution must include each instance’s Name and Owner tags. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Integrate AWS Trusted Advisor with AWS Config. Configure a custom AWS Config rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to publish notifications to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe a Slack channel endpoint and the shared inbox to the topic.

B. Use Amazon EventBridge to monitor for AWS Health events. Configure the maintenance events to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to send notifications to the Slack channel and the shared inbox.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function that sends EC2 maintenance notifications to the Slack channel and the shared inbox. Monitor EC2 health events by using Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Configure a CloudWatch alarm that invokes the Lambda function when a maintenance notification is received.

D. Configure AWS Support integration with AWS CloudTrail. Create a CloudTrail lookup event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to pass EC2 maintenance notifications to Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). Configure Amazon SNS to target the Slack channel and the shared inbox.
questions.explanation: AWS Health sends account-specific EC2 scheduled-maintenance events to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can route those events to Amazon SNS, which can invoke a Lambda function. The function can use the affected EC2 instance identifiers to retrieve the Name and Owner tags, enrich the notification, and deliver it to Slack and the shared email inbox. Amazon EC2 scheduled events are specifically monitored through AWS Health and EventBridge, rather than CloudWatch metrics, Trusted Advisor, or CloudTrail lookups. LEARN MORE Scheduled events for Amazon EC2 instances AWS Health events
learnMore: Scheduled events for Amazon EC2 instances

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application writes a log file that captures the username, date, time, and source IP address for each login. The log is published to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The company is conducting a root cause analysis for an event that took place on the previous day. The company needs to determine the number of logins for a particular user during the past 7 days. Which solution will provide this information?
options: A. Create a CloudWatch Logs metric filter on the log group. Use a filter pattern that matches the username. Publish a CloudWatch metric that sums the number of logins over the past 7 days.
B. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription on the log group. Use a filter pattern that matches the username. Publish a CloudWatch metric that sums the number of logins over the past 7 days.
C. Create a CloudWatch Logs Insights query that uses an aggregation function to count the number of logins for the username over the past 7 days. Run the query against the log group.
D. Create a CloudWatch dashboard. Add a number widget that has a filter pattern that counts the number of logins for the username over the past 7 days directly from the log group.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Logs Insights can run a query against the log group for the past 7 days, filter events for the specified username, and use an aggregation such as stats count(*) to return the number of matching login events. AWS documents that the stats command calculates aggregate statistics and that count() counts log events returned by a query. LEARN MORE stats - Amazon CloudWatch Logs CloudWatch Logs Insights language query syntax
learnMore: stats - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
CloudWatch Logs Insights language query syntax

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer finds that every Amazon EC2 instance running behind an Application Load Balancer in an Auto Scaling group is not responding to user requests. The EC2 instances are also failing the target group's HTTP health checks. After investigating, the engineer finds that the application process is not running on any EC2 instance. The system logs contain a significant number of out-of-memory messages. The engineer must improve application resilience to handle a potential application memory leak. Monitoring and notifications must be enabled to provide alerts when an issue occurs. Which combination of actions meets these requirements?
options: A. Change the Auto Scaling configuration to replace the instances when they fail the load balancer's health checks.
B. Change the target group health check HealthCheckIntervalSeconds parameter to reduce the interval between health checks.
C. Change the target group health checks from HTTP to TCP to check if the port where the application is listening is reachable.

D. Enable the available memory consumption metric within the Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for the entire Auto Scaling group. Create an alarm when the memory utilization is high. Associate an Amazon SNS topic to the alarm to receive notifications when the alarm goes off.

E. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to collect the memory utilization of the EC2 instances in the Auto Scaling group. Create an alarm when the memory utilization is high and associate an Amazon SNS topic to receive a notification.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling can be configured to use Elastic Load Balancing health checks; when the load balancer reports a registered instance as unhealthy, Auto Scaling marks it unhealthy and replaces it. Memory utilization is not an EC2 default metric, but the CloudWatch agent collects host memory metrics from each EC2 instance. A CloudWatch alarm on that metric can send notifications through an Amazon SNS topic. LEARN MORE About the health checks for your Auto Scaling group Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent
learnMore: About the health checks for your Auto Scaling group
Metrics collected by the CloudWatch agent

questions.questionText: A company has enabled Amazon RDS storage autoscaling for its RDS DB instances. A DevOps team must visualize the autoscaling events on an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard. Which solution satisfies this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to RDS storage autoscaling events from RDS events. Create an AWS Lambda function that publishes a CloudWatch custom metric. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function. Visualize the custom metric by using the CloudWatch dashboard.

B. Create a trail by using AWS CloudTrail with management events configured. Configure the trail to send the management events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a metric filter in CloudWatch Logs to match the RDS storage autoscaling events. Visualize the metric filter by using the CloudWatch dashboard.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to RDS storage autoscaling events from the RDS events. Create a CloudWatch alarm. Configure the EventBridge rule to change the status of the CloudWatch alarm. Visualize the alarm status by using the CloudWatch dashboard.

D. Create a trail by using AWS CloudTrail with data events configured. Configure the trail to send the data events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Create a metric filter in CloudWatch Logs to match the RDS storage autoscaling events. Visualize the metric filter by using the CloudWatch dashboard.
questions.explanation: Amazon RDS delivers its events to Amazon EventBridge in near real time, and an EventBridge rule can invoke an AWS Lambda function for matching DB-instance events. The function can convert each storage-autoscaling event into a CloudWatch custom metric; custom metrics can be displayed on a CloudWatch dashboard. CloudTrail is intended to record API calls and related account activity, rather than serve as the source of RDS-generated autoscaling event notifications. LEARN MORE Creating a rule that triggers on an Amazon RDS event Monitoring Amazon RDS events
learnMore: Creating a rule that triggers on an Amazon RDS event
Monitoring Amazon RDS events

questions.questionText: A global company hosts its product catalog website in an Amazon S3 bucket in the us-east-1 Region. The company needs to improve website performance for users in different geographical Regions and reduce load on the origin server. The company must deploy a highly available cross-Region solution that uses Amazon CloudFront. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Set up multiple CloudFront distributions. Point each distribution to another S3 bucket in a different Region. Use Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing to direct users to the nearest distribution. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and the S3 bucket in the different Region.

B. Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in us-east-1. Configure global edge locations. Set up cache behaviors with optimal TTLs for static content and dynamic content. Configure origin failover to an S3 bucket in a different Region. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and the S3 bucket in the different Region.

C. Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in us-east-1. Configure Amazon ElastiCache clusters in multiple Regions to serve as a distributed caching layer between CloudFront and the S3 origin. Set up a replication script to synchronize the S3 bucket in us-east-1 to an S3 bucket in a different Region. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule the script to run once a day.

D. Enable CloudFront with Origin Shield in the eu-west-1 Region. Configure Regional edge caches. Implement AWS Global Accelerator to route requests to the nearest Regional edge location. Enable S3 replication between the S3 bucket in us-east-1 and an S3 bucket in a different Region.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudFront provides global edge delivery, and Origin Shield adds a centralized caching layer that consolidates requests from CloudFront caching layers before they reach the S3 origin, thereby reducing origin load. Configuring an origin group with a replicated S3 bucket in another Region enables managed origin failover for high availability. Using one distribution, S3 replication, Origin Shield, cache behaviors, and CloudFront origin failover requires less operational management than maintaining multiple distributions, Route 53 routing, custom replication scripts, ElastiCache clusters, or Global Accelerator. LEARN MORE Use Amazon CloudFront Origin Shield Optimize high availability with CloudFront origin failover
learnMore: Use Amazon CloudFront Origin Shield
Optimize high availability with CloudFront origin failover

questions.questionText: A company operates several AWS accounts, with an Amazon Connect instance running in each account. For event handling, the company uses the Amazon EventBridge default event bus in every account. A DevOps team must receive all Amazon Connect events in one central DevOps account. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in each account to allow the DevOps account to replay events. Configure an EventBridge rule in the DevOps account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the default event bus in the other accounts.

B. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in each account to allow the DevOps account to receive events. Configure an EventBridge rule in the DevOps account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the default event bus in the other accounts.

C. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in the DevOps account. Update the policy to allow events to be received from the accounts. Configure an EventBridge rule in each account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the DevOps account's default event bus.

D. Update the resource-based policy of the default event bus in the DevOps account. Update the policy to allow events to be replayed by the accounts. Configure an EventBridge rule in each account that matches Amazon Connect events and has a target of the DevOps account's default event bus.
questions.explanation: For cross-account EventBridge event delivery, the receiving event bus must have a resource-based policy that permits the source accounts to send events. Each source account then uses an EventBridge rule that matches its Amazon Connect events and targets the default event bus in the DevOps account. Event replay is not part of cross-account event routing. Sending and receiving events between AWS accounts in Amazon EventBridge LEARN MORE Sending and receiving events between AWS accounts in Amazon EventBridge
learnMore: Sending and receiving events between AWS accounts in Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A company has a file-reading application that stores files in a database running on Amazon EC2 instances. Regulations require the company to delete files from the EC2 instances each day at a specified time. The company must delete database records that are more than 60 days old. Database-record deletion must take place after the file deletions. The company has created scripts that delete the files and database records. The company needs an email notification whenever either deletion script fails. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to automatically invoke a Systems Manager Automation document at the specified time each day. Configure the Automation document to use a run command to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send failure notifications to the company.

B. Use AWS Systems Manager State Manager to automatically invoke a Systems Manager Automation document at the specified time each day. Configure the Automation document to use a run command to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Create a conditional statement inside the Automation document as the last step to check for errors. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send failure notifications as email messages to the company.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function at the specified time. Add the necessary permissions for the invocation to the Lambda function's resource-based policy. Configure the Lambda function to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Configure the Lambda function to use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send failure notifications to the company.

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function at the specified time. Add the necessary permissions for the invocation to the Lambda function's resource-based policy. Configure the Lambda function to run the deletion scripts in sequential order. Configure the Lambda function to use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send failure notifications as email messages to the company.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager State Manager can schedule an Automation runbook, whose ordered Run Command steps run the file-deletion script before the database-record-deletion script on managed EC2 instances. Systems Manager emits failed command and Automation status events to Amazon EventBridge; an EventBridge rule can route those failures to an Amazon SNS topic, which delivers email to its subscribers. This uses the existing scripts without building a Lambda function or custom error-notification logic. LEARN MORE Reference: Amazon EventBridge event patterns and types for Systems Manager Monitoring Systems Manager status changes using Amazon SNS notifications

Monitoring Systems Manager status changes using Amazon SNS notifications

questions.questionText: A company is refactoring applications to run on AWS. It identifies an internal web application that must make Amazon S3 API calls in a particular AWS account. The company wants to use its existing identity provider (IdP), auth.company.com, for authentication. The IdP supports only OpenID Connect (OIDC). A DevOps engineer must secure the web application's access to the AWS account. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure an IdP. Upload the IdP metadata from the existing IdP.
B. Create an IAM IdP by using the provider URL, audience, and signature from the existing IP.

C. Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows the necessary S3 actions. Configure the role's trust policy to allow the OIDC IP to assume the role if the sts.amazon.com:aud context key is appid_from_idp.

D. Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows the necessary S3 actions. Configure the role's trust policy to allow the OIDC IP to assume the role if the auth.company.com:aud context key is appid_from_idp.
E. Configure the web application to use the AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API operation to retrieve temporary credentials. Use the temporary credentials to make the S3 API calls.
F. Configure the web application to use the GetFederationToken API operation to retrieve temporary credentials. Use the temporary credentials to make the S3 API calls.
questions.explanation: AWS OIDC federation requires an IAM OIDC provider, an IAM role that trusts the provider for sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity, and a role permissions policy granting the required S3 actions. The trust policy should restrict the token audience with the custom provider’s URL-based condition key, auth.company.com:aud, matching the application ID. The application uses AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity to exchange its OIDC token for temporary credentials used to call Amazon S3. LEARN MORE Create an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider in IAM Create a role for OpenID Connect federation
learnMore: Create an OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider in IAM
Create a role for OpenID Connect federation

questions.questionText: A company has an application and a CI/CD pipeline. The CI/CD pipeline includes an AWS CodePipeline pipeline and an AWS CodeBuild project. As part of its build process, the CodeBuild project runs tests against the application and produces a test report. The company must retain the test reports for 90 days. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Add a new stage in the CodePipeline pipeline after the stage that contains the CodeBuild project. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the reports. Configure an S3 deploy action type in the new CodePipeline stage with the appropriate path and format for the reports.

B. Add a report group in the CodeBuild project buildspec file with the appropriate path and format for the reports. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the reports. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to copy the reports to the S3 bucket when a build is completed. Create an S3 Lifecycle rule to expire the objects after 90 days.

C. Add a new stage in the CodePipeline pipeline. Configure a test action type with the appropriate path and format for the reports. Configure the report expiration time to be 90 days in the CodeBuild project buildspec file.

D. Add a report group in the CodeBuild project buildspec file with the appropriate path and format for the reports. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the reports. Configure the report group as an artifact in the CodeBuild project buildspec file. Configure the S3 bucket as the artifact destination. Set the object expiration to 90 days.
questions.explanation: CodeBuild test reports stored in a report group expire 30 days after creation and that retention cannot be extended, so satisfying a 90-day requirement means moving the report data into durable storage you control. Option B creates the report group, then uses an EventBridge rule to invoke a Lambda function that copies the reports to an S3 bucket on build completion, with an S3 Lifecycle rule expiring objects after 90 days, which meets the requirement. Option D is incorrect because a report group is not a build artifact; reports and artifacts are separate CodeBuild concepts, so you cannot configure the report group as an artifact with an S3 artifact destination. Options A and C also conflate reports with pipeline actions/artifacts and cannot set a 90-day report retention. LEARN MORE Test reports in CodeBuild Working with reports
learnMore: Test reports in CodeBuild
Working with reports

questions.questionText: A company operates an application that stores artifacts in an Amazon S3 bucket. The application has a large user base and writes a high volume of objects to the S3 bucket. The company has enabled event notifications for the S3 bucket. When the application writes an object to the S3 bucket, several processing tasks must run simultaneously. The company’s DevOps team must create an AWS Step Functions workflow to orchestrate the processing tasks. Which combination of steps should the DevOps team take to meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create a Standard workflow that contains a parallel state that defines the processing tasks. Create an Asynchronous Express workflow that contains a parallel state that defines the processing tasks.
B. Create a Synchronous Express workflow that contains a map state that defines the processing tasks.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match when a new S3 object is created. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to start the processing workflow.
D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match when a new S3 object is created. Configure the EventBridge rule to start the processing workflow.
questions.explanation: Asynchronous Express Workflows are intended for event-driven processing where an immediate completion response is unnecessary, and a Parallel state runs independent processing branches concurrently. An Amazon EventBridge rule can match S3 object-created events and directly start a Step Functions state machine, eliminating the additional Lambda function and its operational management. LEARN MORE Choosing workflow type in Step Functions Starting a Step Functions workflow in response to events

Starting a Step Functions workflow in response to events

questions.questionText: A company operates a web application that emits logs containing transaction metadata, including a success or failure status for every log. The logs use JSON format. The application sends the logs to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. The company needs to create a dashboard that shows the number of successful transactions. Which solution satisfies this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster and an OpenSearch Service subscription filter to send the log group data to the cluster. Create a dashboard within the Dashboards feature in the OpenSearch Service cluster by using a search query for transactions that have a status of success.

B. Create a CloudWatch subscription filter for the log group that uses an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to parse the JSON logs and publish a custom metric to CloudWatch for transactions that have a status of success. Create a CloudWatch dashboard by using a metric graph that displays the custom metric.

C. Create a CloudWatch metric filter for the log groups with a filter pattern that matches the transaction status property and a value of success. Create a CloudWatch dashboard by using a metric graph that displays the new metric.

D. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream that is subscribed to the log group. Configure the data stream to filter incoming log data based on a status of success and to send the filtered logs to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to publish a custom metric to CloudWatch. Create a CloudWatch dashboard by using a metric graph that displays the custom metric.
questions.explanation: A CloudWatch Logs metric filter can match the JSON transaction status when it equals success and transform each matching log event into a CloudWatch metric value, such as an increment of 1. That metric can be displayed in a CloudWatch dashboard graph without running or maintaining downstream compute, streaming infrastructure, or an OpenSearch cluster. LEARN MORE Creating metrics from log events using filters Filter pattern syntax for metric filters
learnMore: Creating metrics from log events using filters
Filter pattern syntax for metric filters

questions.questionText: A company is launching an application that must use only approved AWS services. The account that runs the application was created less than 1 year ago and is assigned to an AWS Organizations OU. The company needs to create a new Organizations account structure. The structure must include an appropriate SCP that supports using only services currently active in the AWS account. The company will use AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) Access Analyzer as part of the solution. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an SCP that allows the services that IAM Access Analyzer identifies. Create an OU for the account. Move the account into the new OU. Attach the new SCP to the new OU. Detach the default FullAWSAccess SCP from the new OU.
B. Create an SCP that denies the services that IAM Access Analyzer identifies. Create an OU for the account. Move the account into the new OU. Attach the new SCP to the new OU.
C. Create an SCP that allows the services that IAM Access Analyzer identifies. Attach the new SCP to the organization's root.

D. Create an SCP that allows the services that IAM Access Analyzer identifies. Create an OU for the account. Move the account into the new OU. Attach the new SCP to the management account. Detach the default FullAWSAccess SCP from the new OU.
questions.explanation: IAM Access Analyzer can analyze access activity to identify services used by IAM entities. An SCP allow list containing those services, attached to a dedicated OU that contains the application account, restricts the account to the approved active services. For an SCP allow-list strategy, the replacement allow-list SCP must be attached before detaching the default FullAWSAccess SCP; otherwise, FullAWSAccess would continue to allow all AWS services. SCPs also do not restrict the management account. LEARN MORE IAM Access Analyzer policy generation DetachPolicy — AWS Organizations API Reference
learnMore: IAM Access Analyzer policy generation
DetachPolicy — AWS Organizations API Reference

questions.questionText: A company stores proprietary data in Amazon S3. The development team creates buckets for new projects every day. The security team wants to make sure that every current and future bucket has encryption, logging, and versioning enabled. In addition, no bucket must ever allow public read or write access. What should a DevOps engineer do to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Enable AWS CloudTrail and configure automatic remediation using AWS Lambda.
B. Enable AWS Config rules and configure automatic remediation using AWS Systems Manager documents.
C. Enable AWS Trusted Advisor and configure automatic remediation using Amazon EventBridge.
D. Enable AWS Systems Manager and configure automatic remediation using Systems Manager documents.
questions.explanation: AWS Config rules continuously evaluate S3 bucket configurations, including buckets created in the future, and identify buckets that do not meet required encryption, logging, versioning, or public-access controls. AWS Config can automatically remediate noncompliant resources by running AWS Systems Manager Automation documents. LEARN MORE Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config

Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config

questions.questionText: A development team plans to use AWS CloudFormation stacks to deploy an application. However, the developer IAM role lacks the required permissions to provision the resources specified in the AWS CloudFormation template. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that enables the developers to deploy the stacks while following the principle of least privilege. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM policy that allows the developers to provision the required resources. Attach the policy to the developer IAM role.
B. Create an IAM policy that allows full access to AWS CloudFormation. Attach the policy to the developer IAM role.
C. Create an AWS CloudFormation service role that has the required permissions. Grant the developer IAM role a cloudformation:* action. Use the new service role during stack deployments.
D. Create an AWS CloudFormation service role that has the required permissions. Grant the developer IAM role the iam:PassRole permission. Use the new service role during stack deployments.
questions.explanation: An AWS CloudFormation service role can be granted only the permissions required to create and manage the template’s resources, and CloudFormation uses that role’s credentials for stack operations. The developer IAM role needs iam:PassRole, scoped to that approved service role, to specify it during deployment; this avoids granting developers direct resource-provisioning permissions or unrestricted CloudFormation access. LEARN MORE CloudFormation service role Service roles for CloudFormation

Service roles for CloudFormation

questions.questionText: A company operates a data-ingestion application across multiple AWS accounts. The accounts belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. The company must monitor the application and centralize access to it. At present, the company runs the application on Amazon EC2 instances in several Auto Scaling groups. The EC2 instances cannot access the internet because the data is sensitive. Engineers have deployed the required VPC endpoints. The EC2 instances use a custom AMI built specifically for the application. To maintain and troubleshoot the application, system administrators require the ability to log in to the EC2 instances. This access must be automated and centrally controlled. The company’s security team must be notified whenever the instances are accessed. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to send notifications to the security team whenever a user logs in to an EC2 instance. Use EC2 Instance Connect to log in to the instances. Deploy Auto Scaling groups by using AWS CloudFormation. Use the cfn-init helper script to deploy appropriate VPC routes for external access. Rebuild the custom AMI so that the custom AMI includes AWS Systems Manager Agent.

B. Deploy a NAT gateway and a bastion host that has internet access. Create a security group that allows incoming traffic on all the EC2 instances from the bastion host. Install AWS Systems Manager Agent on all the EC2 instances. Use Auto Scaling group lifecycle hooks for monitoring and auditing access. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to log in to the instances. Send logs to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Export data to Amazon S3 for auditing. Send notifications to the security team by using S3 event notifications.

C. Use EC2 Image Builder to rebuild the custom AMI. Include the most recent version of AWS Systems Manager Agent in the image. Configure the Auto Scaling group to attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore role to all the EC2 instances. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to log in to the instances. Enable logging of session details to Amazon S3. Create an S3 event notification for new file uploads to send a message to the security team through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

D. Use AWS Systems Manager Automation to build Systems Manager Agent into the custom AMI. Configure AWS Config to attach an SCP to the root organization account to allow the EC2 instances to connect to Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to log in to the instances. Enable logging of session details to Amazon S3. Create an S3 event notification for new file uploads to send a message to the security team through an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager provides centrally controlled access to managed EC2 instances without requiring internet access or a bastion host when the required Systems Manager VPC endpoints are available. The instances need SSM Agent and an instance profile with Systems Manager permissions, which the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore managed policy provides. Building the custom AMI with the agent ensures that every Auto Scaling instance is ready to register with Systems Manager. Session Manager can log session details to Amazon S3, and S3 event notifications can publish an Amazon SNS message to notify the security team. LEARN MORE AWS Systems Manager Session Manager Configure instance permissions required for Systems Manager
learnMore: Configure instance permissions required for Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A company has deployed a landing zone with a well-defined AWS Organizations structure and an SCP. The company's development team can create AWS resources only by using AWS CloudFormation and the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). A DevOps engineer finds that Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues deployed in different CloudFormation stacks have differing configurations. The DevOps engineer also finds that the application cost allocation tag is not consistently set. The DevOps engineer needs a solution that enforces tagging and encourages code reuse. The DevOps engineer must avoid differing configurations for the deployed SQS queues. What should the DevOps engineer do to meet these requirements?
options: A. Create an Organizations tag policy to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation stacks. Instruct the development team to use CloudFormation to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CloudFormation StackSets.

B. Update the SCP to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation stacks. Instruct the development team to use CloudFormation modules to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CloudFormation stacks.

C. Use AWS CDK tagging to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation StackSets. Instruct the development team to use the AWS CDK to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CDK stacks.

D. Use AWS CDK tagging to enforce the cost allocation tag in CloudFormation stacks. Instruct the development team to use the AWS CDK to define SQS queues. Instruct the development team to deploy the SQS queues by using CDK feature flags.
questions.explanation: An SCP can enforce a required cost-allocation tag by denying the relevant resource-creation requests when the required request tag is absent. CloudFormation modules encapsulate a standardized SQS queue definition as a reusable building block, ensuring that stacks use the same queue configuration. LEARN MORE CloudFormation modules Example SCPs for tagging resources
learnMore: CloudFormation modules
Example SCPs for tagging resources

questions.questionText: A DevOps team administers a company's AWS account. The company needs to ensure that changes to specified AWS resource configurations are automatically reversed. Which solution satisfies this requirement?
options: A. Use AWS Config rules to detect changes in resource configurations. Configure remediation action that uses AWS Systems Manager Automation documents to revert the configuration changes.

B. Use Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor resource metrics. When an alarm is activated, use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify an administrator to manually reverts the configuration changes.
C. Use AWS CloudFormation to create a stack that deploys the necessary configuration changes. Update the stack when configuration changes need to be reverted.
D. Use AWS Trusted Advisor to check for noncompliant configurations. Manually apply necessary changes based on Trusted Advisor recommendations.
questions.explanation: AWS Config rules can identify noncompliant resource configurations, and AWS Config can automatically invoke a remediation action implemented by an AWS Systems Manager Automation document. The Automation runbook performs the corrective configuration change, returning the resource to the required compliant state. LEARN MORE Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config

Remediating Noncompliant Resources with AWS Config

questions.questionText: A company operates an application that stores data, including personally identifiable information (PII), in an Amazon S3 bucket. All data is encrypted using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed keys. All AWS resources are deployed from an AWS CloudFormation template. A DevOps engineer must establish a development environment for the application in a separate AWS account. Data in the development environment's S3 bucket must be refreshed weekly from the production environment's S3 bucket. The company must anonymize PII before moving it from the production environment. Data in each environment must be encrypted with distinct KMS customer managed keys. Which combination of steps should the DevOps engineer take to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Activate Amazon Macie on the S3 bucket in the production account. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to initiate a discovery job and redact all PII before copying files to the S3 bucket in the development account. Give the state machine tasks decrypt permissions on the KMS key in the production account. Give the state machine tasks encrypt permissions on the KMS key in the development account.

B. Set up S3 replication between the production S3 bucket and the development S3 bucket. Activate Amazon Macie on the development S3 bucket. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to initiate a discovery job and redact all PII as the files are copied to the development S3 bucket. Give the state machine tasks encrypt and decrypt permissions on the KMS key in the development account.

C. Set up an S3 Batch Operations job to copy files from the production S3 bucket to the development S3 bucket. In the development account, configure an AWS Lambda function to redact ail PII. Configure S3 Object Lambda to use the Lambda function for S3 GET requests. Give the Lambda function's IAM role encrypt and decrypt permissions on the KMS key in the development account.
D. Create a development environment from the CloudFormation template in the development account. Schedule an Amazon EventBridge rule to start the AWS Step Functions state machine once a week.
E. Create a development environment from the CloudFormation template in the development account. Schedule a cron job on an Amazon EC2 instance to run once a week to start the S3 Batch Operations job.
questions.explanation: PII must be discovered and redacted in the production-side workflow before any object is written to the development bucket. That workflow requires permission to decrypt the production objects with the production customer managed KMS key and to encrypt the sanitized output with the separate development customer managed key. Amazon Macie sensitive data discovery jobs detect and report sensitive data in S3 objects, and EventBridge Scheduler can start a Step Functions state machine on a recurring cron or rate schedule. Deploying the development stack from the CloudFormation template creates the required environment in the separate account. LEARN MORE Running sensitive data discovery jobs - Amazon Macie Using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to start a Step Functions state machine execution
learnMore: Running sensitive data discovery jobs - Amazon Macie
Using Amazon EventBridge Scheduler to start a Step Functions state machine execution

questions.questionText: A development team uses AWS CodeCommit, AWS CodePipeline, and AWS CodeBuild to build and deploy an application. Code changes are submitted through pull requests. The development team reviews and merges the pull requests, after which the pipeline builds and tests the application. Over time, the number of pull requests has grown. The pipeline is often blocked by failing tests. To avoid this blockage, the development team wants to run unit and integration tests for each pull request before it is merged. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a CodeBuild project to run the unit and integration tests. Create a CodeCommit approval rule template. Configure the template to require the successful invocation of the CodeBuild project. Attach the approval rule to the project's CodeCommit repository.

B. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match pullRequestCreated events from CodeCommit Create a CodeBuild project to run the unit and integration tests. Configure the CodeBuild project as a target of the EventBridge rule that includes a custom event payload with the CodeCommit repository and branch information from the event.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match pullRequestCreated events from CodeCommit. Modify the existing CodePipeline pipeline to not run the deploy steps if the build is started from a pull request. Configure the EventBridge rule to run the pipeline with a custom payload that contains the CodeCommit repository and branch information from the event.

D. Create a CodeBuild project to run the unit and integration tests. Create a CodeCommit notification rule that matches when a pull request is created or updated. Configure the notification rule to invoke the CodeBuild project.
questions.explanation: Amazon EventBridge can match AWS CodeCommit pull-request events and invoke a CodeBuild project as its target. An input transformation can pass the repository and branch information to the CodeBuild StartBuild request, so the unit and integration tests run for each pull request before merge while the existing pipeline remains dedicated to merged code. LEARN MORE AWS CodeCommit events - Amazon EventBridge Event bus targets in Amazon EventBridge
learnMore: Event bus targets in Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A company must encrypt every AMI it shares between accounts. A DevOps engineer can access a source account in which an unencrypted custom AMI was built. The DevOps engineer also can access a target account, where an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group will launch EC2 instances using that AMI. The DevOps engineer must share the AMI with the target account. The company has created an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key in the source account. Which additional actions must the DevOps engineer take to meet the requirements?
options: A. In the source account, copy the unencrypted AMI to an encrypted AMI. Specify the KMS key in the copy action.
B. In the source account, copy the unencrypted AMI to an encrypted AMI. Specify the default Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) encryption key in the copy action.
C. In the source account, create a KMS grant that delegates permissions to the Auto Scaling group service-linked role in the target account.

D. In the source account, modify the key policy to give the target account permissions to create a grant. In the target account, create a KMS grant that delegates permissions to the Auto Scaling group service-linked role.
E. In the source account, share the unencrypted AMI with the target account.
F. In the source account, share the encrypted AMI with the target account.
questions.explanation: A custom KMS key must be specified when copying the unencrypted AMI to create an encrypted AMI, because AMIs backed by snapshots encrypted with the default AWS managed key cannot be shared. For an Auto Scaling group in another account to use a customer managed key, the source key policy must permit the target account to create a grant, and the target account must grant the Auto Scaling service-linked role access to the key. The encrypted AMI is then shared with the target account. LEARN MORE Required AWS KMS key policy for use with encrypted volumes Share an AMI with specific AWS accounts
learnMore: Required AWS KMS key policy for use with encrypted volumes
Share an AMI with specific AWS accounts

questions.questionText: A company has several development teams in distinct business units that operate in one shared AWS account. Every Amazon EC2 resource that users create in the account must have tags identifying the user who created the resource. Tagging must take place within the first hour after resource creation. A DevOps engineer must tag new resources with the ID of the creating user and the applicable cost center ID. The engineer configures an AWS Lambda function to use cost center mappings to tag the resources. The engineer also configures AWS CloudTrail in the shared AWS account, with an Amazon S3 bucket storing the CloudTrail event logs. Which solution meets the tagging requirements?
options: A. Create an S3 event notification on the S3 bucket to invoke the Lambda function for s3:ObjectTagging:Put events. Enable bucket versioning on the S3 bucket.
B. Enable server access logging on the S3 bucket. Create an S3 event notification on the S3 bucket for s3:ObjectTagging:* events.
C. Enable AWS Config in the account. Configure the required-tags AWS managed rule to check and update the required tags.
D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses Amazon EC2 as the event source. Configure the rule to match events that CloudTrail delivers. Configure the rule to target the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 API activity recorded by AWS CloudTrail can be matched by an Amazon EventBridge rule using source aws.ec2, detail type AWS API Call via CloudTrail, and event source ec2.amazonaws.com. The matching event can invoke Lambda asynchronously and includes the API-call identity information needed to identify the creator; Lambda can map that identity to a cost center and tag the new resource promptly. The AWS Config required-tags managed rule only evaluates whether specified tags are present and does not update them. LEARN MORE Amazon EC2 events — Amazon EventBridge required-tags — AWS Config
learnMore: required-tags — AWS Config

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage multiple AWS accounts in a hierarchy. An SCP associated with the organization root permits the creation of IAM users. A DevOps team must be able to create IAM users with any permission level. Developers must also be able to create IAM users, but they must not be able to give new IAM users excessive permissions. The developers hold the CreateAndManageUsers role in every account. The DevOps team must be able to stop other users from creating IAM users. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an SCP in the organization to deny users the ability to create and modify IAM users. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization. Attach the CreateAndManageUsers role to developers.

B. Create an SCP in the organization to grant users that have the DeveloperBoundary policy attached the ability to create new IAM users and to modify IAM users. Configure the SCP to require users to attach the PermissionBoundaries policy to any new IAM user. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.

C. Create an IAM permissions policy named PermissionBoundaries within each account. Configure the PermissionBoundaries policy to specify the maximum permissions that a developer can grant to a new IAM user.
D. Create an IAM permissions policy named PermissionBoundaries within each account. Configure PermissionsBoundaries to allow users who have the PermissionBoundaries policy to create new IAM users.

E. Create an IAM permissions policy named DeveloperBoundary within each account. Configure the DeveloperBoundary policy to allow developers to create IAM users and to assign policies to IAM users of only if the developer includes the PermissionBoundaries policy as the permissions boundary. Attach the DeveloperBoundary policy to the CreateAndManageUsers role within each account.
questions.explanation: A permissions boundary is a managed policy that establishes the maximum permissions an identity-based policy can grant to an IAM user; it does not itself grant access. A PermissionBoundaries policy can therefore limit the permissions developers can delegate. An identity policy attached to CreateAndManageUsers can grant developers IAM-user creation and policy-management actions only when the required PermissionBoundaries policy is supplied as the permissions boundary. SCPs limit permissions but cannot grant them, and a root-level deny would also block the DevOps team. LEARN MORE Permissions boundaries for IAM entities Policies and permissions in AWS Identity and Access Management
learnMore: Permissions boundaries for IAM entities
Policies and permissions in AWS Identity and Access Management

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) private registries to store container images. A DevOps team must ensure that container images are scanned regularly for software package vulnerabilities. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Enable enhanced scanning for private registries in Amazon ECR.
B. Enable basic continuous scanning for private registries in Amazon ECR.
C. Create an AWS System Manager Automation document to scan images by using the AWS SDK. Configure the Automation document to run when a new image is pushed to an ECR registry.
D. Create an AWS Lambda function that scans all images in Amazon ECR by using the AWS SDK. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function each day.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR enhanced scanning integrates with Amazon Inspector to automatically and continuously scan container images for operating-system and programming-language package vulnerabilities. Basic scanning supports manual scans or scans on image push, not continuous scanning. LEARN MORE Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR Scan images for OS and programming language package vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR
learnMore: Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR
Scan images for OS and programming language package vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer plans to deploy a Ruby-based application to production. The application must interact with an Amazon RDS for MySQL database and requires automatic scaling and high availability. The data stored in the database is critical and must persist regardless of the application stack’s state. The DevOps engineer must establish an automated application-deployment strategy with automatic rollbacks. The solution must also alert the application team if a deployment fails. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Deploy the application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Deploy an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance as part of the Elastic Beanstalk configuration.
B. Deploy the application on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Deploy a separate Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance outside of Elastic Beanstalk.
C. Configure a notification email address that alerts the application team in the AWS Elastic Beanstalk configuration.
D. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to monitor AWS Health events. Use an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as a target to alert the application team.
E. Use the immutable deployment method to deploy new application versions.
F. Use the rolling deployment method to deploy new application versions.
questions.explanation: An Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance deployed separately from Elastic Beanstalk remains independent of the application environment lifecycle, protecting critical data if that environment is rebuilt or terminated. Elastic Beanstalk environment email notifications use Amazon SNS to notify recipients about errors and environment-health changes. Immutable deployments run the new application version in a separate Auto Scaling group; if the new instances fail health checks, Elastic Beanstalk terminates that group and retains the original instances, providing an automatic rollback. LEARN MORE Adding a database to your Elastic Beanstalk environment Elastic Beanstalk environment notifications with Amazon SNS
learnMore: Adding a database to your Elastic Beanstalk environment
Elastic Beanstalk environment notifications with Amazon SNS

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Redshift as its data warehouse solution. The company wants to build a dashboard to view changes to Redshift users and the queries those users run. Which combination of steps meets this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudWatch log group. Create an AWS CloudTrail trail that writes to the CloudWatch log group.
B. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket. Configure default audit logging on the Redshift cluster. Configure the S3 bucket as the target.
C. Configure the Redshift cluster database audit logging to include user activity logs. Configure Amazon CloudWatch as the target.
D. Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that has a log widget. Configure the widget to display user details from the Redshift logs.
E. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses Amazon Athena to query the Redshift logs. Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard that has a custom widget type that uses the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: Amazon Redshift database audit logging sends user-log events, which record database-user definition changes, and user-activity-log events, which record queries, to Amazon CloudWatch Logs when user activity logging is enabled. A CloudWatch dashboard log widget can run a CloudWatch Logs Insights query over those log groups to display the relevant user and query details. LEARN MORE Amazon Redshift database audit logging CloudWatch dashboard body structure and syntax
learnMore: CloudWatch dashboard body structure and syntax

questions.questionText: A space-exploration company receives telemetry data from multiple satellites. Small data packets arrive through Amazon API Gateway and are placed directly into an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue. A custom application subscribes to the queue and transforms the data into a standardized format. Because the satellite data is inconsistent, the application occasionally cannot transform it. In those situations, the messages stay in the SQS queue. A DevOps engineer must develop a solution that retains the failed messages and makes them available to scientists for review and later processing. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Lambda to poll the SQS queue and invoke a Lambda function to check whether the queue messages are valid. If validation fails, send a copy of the data that is not valid to an Amazon S3 bucket so that the scientists can review and correct the data. When the data is corrected, amend the message in the SQS queue by using a replay Lambda function with the corrected data.

B. Convert the SQS standard queue to an SQS FIFO queue. Configure AWS Lambda to poll the SQS queue every 10 minutes by using an Amazon EventBridge schedule. Invoke the Lambda function to identify any messages with a SentTimestamp value that is older than 5 minutes, push the data to the same location as the application's output location, and remove the messages from the queue.

C. Create an SQS dead-letter queue. Modify the existing queue by including a redrive policy that sets the Maximum Receives setting to 1 and sets the dead-letter queue ARN to the ARN of the newly created queue. Instruct the scientists to use the dead-letter queue to review the data that is not valid. Reprocess this data at a later time.

D. Configure API Gateway to send messages to different SQS virtual queues that are named for each of the satellites. Update the application to use a new virtual queue for any data that it cannot transform, and send the message to the new virtual queue. Instruct the scientists to use the virtual queue to review the data that is not valid. Reprocess this data at a later time.
questions.explanation: An Amazon SQS dead-letter queue (DLQ) captures messages that a consumer does not process successfully. A redrive policy on the source queue specifies the DLQ ARN and the maximum receive count; after that threshold is exceeded, SQS moves the failed message to the DLQ. This retains failed telemetry separately for scientists to inspect and reprocess without leaving poison messages in the source queue. LEARN MORE Capturing problematic messages in Amazon SQS Configure a dead-letter queue using the Amazon SQS console
learnMore: Capturing problematic messages in Amazon SQS
Configure a dead-letter queue using the Amazon SQS console

questions.questionText: A company runs a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances that host critical applications and process sensitive data. The EC2 instances must receive current security patches to guard against vulnerabilities and maintain compliance with industry standards and regulations. The company requires an automated solution to monitor and enforce security-patch compliance throughout the EC2 fleet. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager and AWS Config with defined patch baselines and compliance rules that run Systems Manager Automation documents.
B. Access each EC2 instance by using SSH keys. Check for and apply security updates by using package managers. Verify the installations.

C. Configure Auto Scaling groups that have scaling policies based on Amazon CloudWatch metrics. Configure Auto Scaling launch templates that launch new instances by using the latest AMIs that contain new security patches.

D. Use AWS CloudFormation to recreate EC2 instances with the latest AMI every time a new patch becomes available. Use AWS CloudTrail logs to monitor patch compliance and to send alerts for non-compliant instances.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager automates scanning for and installing missing security updates on managed nodes. Patch baselines define the patches required for compliance, and AWS Config rules with Systems Manager Automation documents can evaluate and remediate noncompliant resources, providing fleet-wide monitoring and enforcement. LEARN MORE AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager Patching noncompliant managed nodes
learnMore: Patching noncompliant managed nodes

questions.questionText: A company administers 500 AWS accounts within an AWS Organizations organization. The company finds many unattached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes across all accounts and wants to automatically tag those unattached EBS volumes for investigation. A DevOps engineer must deploy an AWS Lambda function to every AWS account. The Lambda function must execute every 30 minutes and tag all EBS volumes that have remained unattached for 7 days or longer. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?
options: A. Configure a delegated administrator account for the organization. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that contains the Lambda function. Use CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the CloudFormation template from the delegated administrator account to all the member accounts in the organization. Create an Amazon EventBridge event bus in the delegated administrator account to invoke the Lambda function in each member account every 30 minutes.

B. Create a cross-account IAM role in the organization's member accounts. Attach the AWSLambda_FullAccess policy and the AWSCloudFormationFullAccess policy to the role. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that contains the Lambda function and an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the Lambda function every 30 minutes. Create a custom script in the organization’s management account that assumes the role and deploys the CloudFormation template to the member accounts.

C. Configure a delegated administrator account for the organization. Create an AWS CloudFormation template that contains the Lambda function and an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke the Lambda function every 30 minutes. Use CloudFormation StackSets to deploy the CloudFormation template from the delegated administrator account to all the member accounts in the organization

D. Create a cross-account IAM role in the organization's member accounts. Attach the AmazonS3FullAccess policy and the AWSCodeDeployDeployerAccess policy to the role. Use AWS CodeDeploy to assume the role to deploy the Lambda function from the organization's management account. Configure an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule in the member accounts to invoke the Lambda function every 30 minutes.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions can deploy the same CloudFormation resources across AWS Organizations accounts from a delegated administrator without requiring manually managed cross-account IAM roles. A template that contains both the Lambda function and an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule creates a local 30-minute invocation schedule in each member account, so each function can inspect and tag that account’s EBS volumes. LEARN MORE Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions Register a delegated administrator member account
learnMore: Create CloudFormation StackSets with service-managed permissions
Register a delegated administrator member account

questions.questionText: A company is creating a new pipeline with AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild in a build account. The pipeline has two stages. The first stage is a CodeBuild job that builds and packages an AWS Lambda function. The second stage contains deployment actions that run in two separate AWS accounts: a development environment account and a production environment account. The deployment stages use the AWS CloudFormation action that CodePipeline calls to deploy the infrastructure required by the Lambda function. A DevOps engineer creates the CodePipeline pipeline and configures it to encrypt build artifacts by using the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) AWS managed key for Amazon S3 (the aws/s3 key). The artifacts are kept in an S3 bucket. When the pipeline runs, the CloudFormation actions fail with an access denied error. Which combination of actions must the DevOps engineer take to resolve this error?
options: A. Create an S3 bucket in each AWS account for the artifacts. Allow the pipeline to write to the S3 buckets. Create a CodePipeline S3 action to copy the artifacts to the S3 bucket in each AWS account. Update the CloudFormation actions to reference the artifacts S3 bucket in the production account.

B. Create a customer managed KMS key. Configure the KMS key policy to allow the IAM roles used by the CloudFormation action to perform decrypt operations. Modify the pipeline to use the customer managed KMS key to encrypt artifacts.

C. Create an AWS managed KMS key. Configure the KMS key policy to allow the development account and the production account to perform decrypt operations. Modify the pipeline to use the KMS key to encrypt artifacts.

D. In the development account and in the production account, create an IAM role for CodePipeline. Configure the roles with permissions to perform CloudFormation operations and with permissions to retrieve and decrypt objects from the artifacts S3 bucket. In the CodePipeline account, configure the CodePipeline CloudFormation action to use the roles.

E. In the development account and in the production account, create an IAM role for CodePipeline. Configure the roles with permissions to perform CloudFormation operations and with permissions to retrieve and decrypt objects from the artifacts S3 bucket. In the CodePipeline account, modify the artifacts S3 bucket policy to allow the roles access. Configure the CodePipeline CloudFormation action to use the roles.
questions.explanation: Cross-account CodePipeline actions require a customer-managed KMS key so its key policy can grant the target-account deployment action roles permission to decrypt artifacts. Those roles must also be able to perform the CloudFormation deployment and read the artifact objects, and the artifact S3 bucket policy must grant them cross-account access. AWS-managed KMS keys cannot be configured with the required cross-account key-policy permissions. LEARN MORE Create a pipeline in CodePipeline that uses resources from another AWS account General integrations with CodePipeline
learnMore: Create a pipeline in CodePipeline that uses resources from another AWS account
General integrations with CodePipeline

questions.questionText: A company is assessing its disaster recovery capabilities and requires the ability to fail over its daily operations to a secondary AWS Region. The company uses AWS CodeCommit as a source-control tool in the primary Region. A DevOps engineer must enable the company to develop code in the secondary Region. If the company must use that Region, developers can add another remote URL to their local Git configuration. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a CodeCommit repository in the secondary Region. Create an AWS CodeBuild project to perform a Git mirror operation of the primary Region's CodeCommit repository to the secondary Region's CodeCommit repository. Create an AWS Lambda function that invokes the CodeBuild project. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to merge events in the primary Region's CodeCommit repository. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function.

B. Create an Amazon S3 bucket in the secondary Region. Create an AWS Fargate task to perform a Git mirror operation of the primary Region's CodeCommit repository and copy the result to the S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that initiates the Fargate task. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to merge events in the CodeCommit repository. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function.

C. Create an AWS CodeArtifact repository in the secondary Region. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses the primary Region’s CodeCommit repository for the source action. Create a cross-Region stage in the pipeline that packages the CodeCommit repository contents and stores the contents in the CodeArtifact repository when a pull request is merged into the CodeCommit repository.

D. Create an AWS Cloud9 environment and a CodeCommit repository in the secondary Region. Configure the primary Region's CodeCommit repository as a remote repository in the AWS Cloud9 environment. Connect the secondary Region's CodeCommit repository to the AWS Cloud9 environment.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeCommit repositories are scoped to an AWS Region, so a secondary Region needs its own CodeCommit repository to serve as a writable Git remote during failover. A Git mirror operation replicates the repository history and refs to that repository. CodeCommit sends repository and pull-request state-change events to Amazon EventBridge, allowing a merge event to trigger Lambda and a CodeBuild project that performs the mirror. AWS CodeCommit events in Amazon EventBridge Monitoring CodeCommit events LEARN MORE AWS CodeCommit events - Amazon EventBridge Monitoring CodeCommit events in Amazon EventBridge and Amazon CloudWatch Events
learnMore: Monitoring CodeCommit events in Amazon EventBridge and Amazon CloudWatch Events

questions.questionText: A company is developing a web and mobile application that uses a serverless architecture powered by AWS Lambda and Amazon API Gateway. The company wants to fully automate backend Lambda deployment when code is pushed to the appropriate environment branch in an AWS CodeCommit repository. The deployment must provide: Separate environment pipelines for testing and production Automatic deployment for test environments only Which steps should be taken to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Configure a new AWS CodePipeline service. Create a CodeCommit repository for each environment. Set up CodePipeline to retrieve the source code from the appropriate repository. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions with AWS CloudFormation.

B. Create two AWS CodePipeline configurations for test and production environments. Configure the production pipeline to have a manual approval step. Create a CodeCommit repository for each environment. Set up each CodePipeline to retrieve the source code from the appropriate repository. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions with AWS CloudFormation.

C. Create two AWS CodePipeline configurations for test and production environments. Configure the production pipeline to have a manual approval step. Create one CodeCommit repository with a branch for each environment. Set up each CodePipeline to retrieve the source code from the appropriate branch in the repository. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions with AWS CloudFormation.

D. Create an AWS CodeBuild configuration for test and production environments. Configure the production pipeline to have a manual approval step. Create one CodeCommit repository with a branch for each environment. Push the Lambda function code to an Amazon S3 bucket. Set up the deployment step to deploy the Lambda functions from the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: AWS CodePipeline can use a specified branch in an AWS CodeCommit repository as its source and start when commits are pushed to that branch. Two pipelines can therefore use separate test and production branches from one repository. A manual approval action in the production pipeline stops it until approved, while the test pipeline can proceed automatically. AWS CloudFormation is a supported CodePipeline deploy action and can deploy the Lambda resources. LEARN MORE CodeCommit source action reference — AWS CodePipeline Add a manual approval action to a pipeline in CodePipeline
