questions.questionText: A company wants to use a grid system for a proprietary enterprise in-memory data store running on AWS. The system can operate across multiple server nodes on any Linux-based distribution. It must be able to reconfigure the entire cluster whenever a node is added or removed. When nodes are added or removed, an /etc/cluster/nodes.config file must be updated to list the IP addresses of the cluster’s current node members. The company wants to automate the process of adding new nodes to a cluster. What can a DevOps engineer do to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS OpsWorks Stacks to layer the server nodes of that cluster. Create a Chef recipe that populates the content of the /etc/cluster/nodes.config file and restarts the service by using the current members of the layer. Assign that recipe to the Configure lifecycle event.

B. Put the file nodes.config in version control. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment configuration and deployment group based on an Amazon EC2 tag value for the cluster nodes. When adding a new node to the cluster, update the file with all tagged instances, and make a commit in version control. Deploy the new file and restart the services.

C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket and upload a version of the /etc/cluster/nodes.config file. Create a crontab script that will poll for that S3 file and download it frequently. Use a process manager, such as Monit or systemd, to restart the cluster services when it detects that the new file was modified. When adding a node to the cluster, edit the file’s most recent members. Upload the new file to the S3 bucket.

D. Create a user data script that lists all members of the current security group of the cluster and automatically updates the /etc/cluster/nodes.config file whenever a new instance is added to the cluster.
questions.explanation: AWS OpsWorks Stacks layers expose the current layer members to Chef recipes. A custom recipe assigned to the Configure lifecycle event runs when an instance enters or leaves the online state and can regenerate /etc/cluster/nodes.config with the current member IP addresses and restart the data-store service throughout the cluster. LEARN MORE AWS OpsWorks Stacks Lifecycle Events

questions.questionText: A company is deploying an application that stores raw data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Three applications must access the data to produce reports. Before the applications access it, the data must be redacted differently for each application. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an S3 bucket for each application. Configure S3 Same-Region Replication (SRR) from the raw data's S3 bucket to each application's S3 bucket. Configure each application to consume data from its own S3 bucket.

B. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by object creation events in the raw data’s S3 bucket. Program the Lambda function to redact data for each application. Publish the data on the Kinesis data stream. Configure each application to consume data from the Kinesis data stream.

C. For each application, create an S3 access point that uses the raw data's S3 bucket as the destination. Create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by object creation events in the raw data's S3 bucket. Program the Lambda function to redact data for each application. Store the data in each application's S3 access point. Configure each application to consume data from its own S3 access point.

D. Create an S3 access point that uses the raw data’s S3 bucket as the destination. For each application, create an S3 Object Lambda access point that uses the S3 access point. Configure the AWS Lambda function for each S3 Object Lambda access point to redact data when objects are retrieved. Configure each application to consume data from its own S3 Object Lambda access point
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 Object Lambda applies a Lambda-based transformation when an object is retrieved through an Object Lambda access point. Using one supporting S3 access point for the raw bucket and a separate Object Lambda access point with a redaction function for each application returns an application-specific redacted view while retaining one raw data source. LEARN MORE Transforming objects with S3 Object Lambda Tutorial: Detecting and redacting PII data with S3 Object Lambda and Amazon Comprehend

questions.questionText: A company wants to strengthen its security practices by enforcing least privilege across all projects. Developers must be able to access Amazon EC2 resources, but not Amazon RDS resources. Database administrators must have access only to Amazon RDS resources. Every employee has a unique IAM user. Pre-existing IAM policies already exist for developer and database administrator job functions. All AWS resources are already tagged with the appropriate project tags. All IAM users are tagged with the applicable project and job function. The company must ensure that each employee can access only the project on which the employee is working. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. For each project, create one IAM role for developers and one IAM role for database administrators. Tag the IAM roles with the corresponding projects and job functions.

B. Modify the pre-existing IAM policies to include a StringEquals ResourceTag condition for projects that match the PrincipalTag value. Attach the modified policies to the IAM roles for each job function.
C. Create an IAM policy that allows users to assume a role when the ResourceTag value matches the PrincipalTag value for project tags and job title tags. Attach the new policy to all IAM users.

D. Create an IAM policy that allows users to assume a role when the ResourceTag value matches the PrincipalTag value for project tags and job title tags. Attach the new policy to the IAM roles for each job function.
E. Tag the pre-existing IAM policies with the appropriate projects and job functions. Attach the modified policies to IAM roles for each job function.
F. For each project, create one IAM group for developers and one IAM group for database administrators. Add the appropriate users to each group so the users can assume their respective IAM roles.
questions.explanation: IAM ABAC can compare a resource's project tag with ${aws:PrincipalTag/project} in the job-function permission policies, restricting the EC2 or RDS permissions to resources in the principal’s project. Roles tagged with the project and job function provide the matching principal attributes after assumption. An IAM-user policy can allow sts:AssumeRole only when the target role’s iam:ResourceTag values for project and job title match the user’s principal tags. Tags on managed policies do not control their permissions, and IAM groups alone do not implement the tag-matched role-assumption restriction. LEARN MORE IAM tutorial: Define permissions to access AWS resources based on tags Controlling access to AWS resources using tags
learnMore: IAM tutorial: Define permissions to access AWS resources based on tags
Controlling access to AWS resources using tags

questions.questionText: A company must implement failover for its application. The application includes an Amazon CloudFront distribution and a public Application Load Balancer (ALB) in an AWS Region. The company has configured the ALB as the distribution’s default origin. Following recent application outages, the company requires a zero-second RTO. The company deploys the application to a secondary Region in a warm standby configuration. A DevOps engineer must automate application failover to the secondary Region so that HTTP GET requests satisfy the required RTO. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a second CloudFront distribution that has the secondary ALB as the default origin. Create Amazon Route 53 alias records that have a failover policy and Evaluate Target Health set to Yes for both CloudFront distributions. Update the application to use the new record set.

B. Create a new origin on the distribution for the secondary ALCreate a new origin group. Set the original ALB as the primary origin. Configure the origin group to fail over for HTTP 5xx status codes. Update the default behavior to use the origin group.

C. Create Amazon Route 53 alias records that have a failover policy and Evaluate Target Health set to Yes for both ALBs. Set the TTL of both records to 0. Update the distribution's origin to use the new record set.

D. Create a CloudFront function that detects HTTP 5xx status codes. Configure the function to return a 307 Temporary Redirect error response to the secondary ALB if the function detects 5xx status codes. Update the distribution's default behavior to send origin responses to the function.
questions.explanation: A CloudFront origin group can contain the original ALB as the primary origin and the warm-standby ALB as the secondary origin. When configured 5xx failover criteria are returned by the primary origin, CloudFront automatically sends an eligible GET request to the secondary origin. This request-level failover avoids DNS TTL and resolver-cache delay, supporting an immediate recovery path for HTTP GET requests. LEARN MORE Optimize high availability with CloudFront origin failover Request and response behavior for origin groups
learnMore: Optimize high availability with CloudFront origin failover
Request and response behavior for origin groups

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS CodeArtifact repository to store internally developed Python packages. A DevOps engineer must use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy an application to an Amazon EC2 instance. The application depends on a Python package stored in the CodeArtifact repository. A BeforeInstall lifecycle event hook will install the package. The DevOps engineer must grant the EC2 instance access to the CodeArtifact repository. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Create a service-linked role for CodeArtifact. Associate the role with the EC2 instance. Use the aws codeartifact get-authorization-token CLI command on the instance.
B. Configure a resource-based policy for the CodeArtifact repository that allows the ReadFromRepository action for the EC2 instance principal.
C. Configure ACLs on the CodeArtifact repository to allow the EC2 instance to access the Python package.

D. Create an instance profile that contains an IAM role that has access to CodeArtifact. Associate the instance profile with the EC2 instance. Use the aws codeartifact login CLI command on the instance.
questions.explanation: An EC2 instance profile provides the instance with IAM role credentials that can authorize CodeArtifact access. The role can grant codeartifact:GetAuthorizationToken, sts:GetServiceBearerToken, and codeartifact:ReadFromRepository; aws codeartifact login retrieves the authorization token and configures pip to use the repository. ReadFromRepository alone is insufficient because fetching packages also requires an authorization token. LEARN MORE AWS CodeArtifact authentication and tokens AWS CodeArtifact permissions reference

questions.questionText: A company operates an application that uses an Amazon S3 bucket for image storage. A DevOps engineer must implement a multi-Region disaster recovery (DR) strategy for the S3 objects. The DevOps engineer enables two-way replication between the S3 buckets. The company must be able to fail over to a second S3 bucket in a second AWS Region. When an image is added to either S3 bucket, it must replicate to the other S3 bucket within 15 minutes. Which combination of steps meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Enable S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) for each replication rule used in the configuration.
B. Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point in an active-passive configuration.
C. Call the SubmitMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes operation in the Amazon S3 API when the company needs to fail over to the S3 bucket in the second Region.
D. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on both S3 buckets.
E. Configure a routing control in Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller. Add both S3 buckets in an active-passive configuration.
F. Use an Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to shift traffic from the primary bucket to the failover bucket in the second Region.
questions.explanation: S3 Replication Time Control provides the replication-time objective for new objects, with a 15-minute replication SLA. An S3 Multi-Region Access Point configured active-passive routes normal requests only to the active bucket and retains the other bucket for disaster-recovery failover. SubmitMultiRegionAccessPointRoutes updates the Multi-Region Access Point route states between active and passive, shifting S3 request traffic to the bucket in the second Region. Two-way replication ensures that objects written after failover replicate back to the other bucket. LEARN MORE Replicating objects within and across Regions Meeting compliance requirements with S3 Replication Time Control

Meeting compliance requirements with S3 Replication Time Control

questions.questionText: A company uses one AWS account to test applications on Amazon EC2 instances. The company has enabled AWS Config in the AWS account and activated the restricted-ssh AWS Config managed rule. The company requires an automated monitoring solution that provides a customized, real-time notification whenever any security group in the account is noncompliant with the restricted-ssh rule. The customized notification must include the name and ID of the noncompliant security group. A DevOps engineer creates an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in the account and subscribes the appropriate personnel to the topic. What should the DevOps engineer do next to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches an AWS Config evaluation result of NON_COMPLIANT for the restricted-ssh rule. Configure an input transformer for the EventBridge rule. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish a notification to the SNS topic.

B. Configure AWS Config to send all evaluation results for the restricted-ssh rule to the SNS topic. Configure a filter policy on the SNS topic to send only notifications that contain the text of NON_COMPLIANT in the notification to subscribers.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches an AWS Config evaluation result of NON_COMPLIANT for the restricted-ssh rule. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke AWS Systems Manager Run Command on the SNS topic to customize a notification and to publish the notification to the SNS topic.

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches all AWS Config evaluation results of NON_COMPLIANT. Configure an input transformer for the restricted-ssh rule. Configure the EventBridge rule to publish a notification to the SNS topic.
questions.explanation: AWS Config sends rule-compliance change events to Amazon EventBridge. An EventBridge rule can filter those events to the restricted-ssh rule and the NON_COMPLIANT compliance state, then publish to Amazon SNS. An EventBridge input transformer extracts fields from the matching event, such as the security group resource name and ID, and formats them as the customized notification payload. LEARN MORE Monitoring AWS Config with Amazon EventBridge Amazon EventBridge input transformation
learnMore: Monitoring AWS Config with Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A company needs to improve the security of container images that run in its production environment. The company wants to integrate operating-system scanning and programming-language package vulnerability scanning for the containers into its CI/CD pipeline. The CI/CD pipeline is an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that includes an AWS CodeBuild build project, AWS CodeDeploy actions, and an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. A DevOps engineer must add an image scan to the CI/CD pipeline. The CI/CD pipeline must deploy to production only images that have no CRITICAL or HIGH findings. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon ECR basic scanning.
B. Use Amazon ECR enhanced scanning.
C. Configure Amazon ECR to submit a Rejected status to the CI/CD pipeline when the image scan returns CRITICAL or HIGH findings.

D. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the image scan is completed. Configure the Lambda function to consume the Amazon Inspector scan status and to submit an Approved or Rejected status to the CI/CD pipeline.

E. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function when the image scan is completed. Configure the Lambda function to consume the Clair scan status and to submit an Approved or Rejected status to the CI/CD pipeline.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR enhanced scanning integrates with Amazon Inspector and detects vulnerabilities in both operating-system and programming-language packages. When an enhanced scan completes, Amazon Inspector emits an EventBridge event that includes severity counts. A Lambda function invoked by that event can inspect the CRITICAL and HIGH counts and submit an Approved or Rejected result to the pipeline, so images with either severity cannot proceed to production. LEARN MORE Scan images for software vulnerabilities in Amazon ECR EventBridge events sent for enhanced scanning in Amazon ECR

EventBridge events sent for enhanced scanning in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Systems Manager to manage a fleet of Amazon Linux EC2 instances with SSM Agent installed. All EC2 instances are configured to use Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2) and run in the same AWS account and AWS Region. Company policy requires developers to use only Amazon Linux. The company needs to ensure that every new EC2 instance is automatically managed by Systems Manager after it is created. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create an IAM role that has a trust policy that allows Systems Manager to assume the role. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedEC2InstanceDefaultPolicy policy to the role. Configure the default-ec2-instance-management-role SSM service setting to use the role.

B. Ensure that AWS Config is set up. Create an AWS Config rule that validates if an EC2 instance has SSM Agent installed. Configure the rule to run on EC2 configuration changes. Configure automatic remediation for the rule to run the AWS-InstallSSMAgent SSM document to install SSM Agent.

C. Configure Systems Manager Patch Manager. Create a patch baseline that automatically installs SSM Agent on all new EC2 instances. Create a patch group for all EC2 instances. Attach the patch baseline to the patch group. Create a maintenance window and maintenance window task to start installing SSM Agent daily.

D. Create an EC2 instance role that has a trust policy that allows Amazon EC2 to assume the role. Attach the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore policy to the role. Ensure that AWS Config is set up. Use the ec2-instance-profile-attached managed AWS Config rule to validate if an EC2 instance has the role attached. Configure the rule to run on EC2 configuration changes. Configure automatic remediation for the rule to run the AWS-SetupManagedRoleOnEc2Instance SSM document to attach the role to the EC2 instance.
questions.explanation: Systems Manager Default Host Management Configuration automatically manages EC2 instances in the configured AWS account and Region when they use IMDSv2 and have a qualifying SSM Agent version installed. It uses the default-ec2-instance-management-role service setting and a role granted AmazonSSMManagedEC2InstanceDefaultPolicy, eliminating the need to attach and remediate instance profiles individually. LEARN MORE Configure instance permissions required for Systems Manager AWS managed policies for AWS Systems Manager
learnMore: Configure instance permissions required for Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A company operates an application that stores logs in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The company wants to archive these logs in an Amazon S3 bucket. Logs are seldom accessed after 90 days and must be retained for 10 years. Which combination of steps should a DevOps engineer perform to meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to use AWS Glue to transfer all logs to an S3 bucket.
B. Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream all logs to an S3 bucket.
C. Configure a CloudWatch Logs subscription filter to stream all logs to an S3 bucket.
D. Configure the S3 bucket lifecycle policy to transition logs to S3 Glacier after 90 days and to expire logs after 3.650 days.
E. Configure the S3 bucket lifecycle policy to transition logs to Reduced Redundancy after 90 days and to expire logs after 3.650 days.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs can send matching log events through a subscription filter to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream, which can deliver the data to Amazon S3. An S3 Lifecycle configuration can transition the archived objects to S3 Glacier after 90 days and expire them after 3,650 days, satisfying the 10-year retention period. LEARN MORE Log group-level subscription filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs Examples of S3 Lifecycle configurations - Amazon S3

Examples of S3 Lifecycle configurations - Amazon S3

questions.questionText: A DevOps team is deploying application microservices to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that uses managed node groups. The team needs to enable automatic scaling of the microservice Pods according to a specified CPU utilization percentage. The Kubernetes Metrics Server has already been installed on the cluster. Which solution satisfies these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Edit the Auto Scaling group that is associated with the worker nodes of the EKS cluster. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use a target tracking scaling policy to scale when the average CPU utilization of the Auto Scaling group reaches a specific percentage.

B. Deploy the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) and the Kubernetes Vertical Pod Autoscaler (VPA) in the cluster. Configure the HPA to scale based on the target CPU utilization percentage. Configure the VPA to use the recommender mode setting.

C. Run the AWS Systems Manager AWS-UpdateEKSManagedNodeGroup Automation document. Modify the values for NodeGroupDesiredSize, NodeGroupMaxSize, and NodeGroupMinSize to be based on an estimate for the required node size.

D. Deploy the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) and the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler in the cluster. Configure the HPA to scale based on the target CPU utilization percentage. Configure the Cluster Autoscaler to use the auto-discovery setting.
questions.explanation: A Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) scales a workload’s Pod replica count to maintain a specified average CPU-utilization target, using resource metrics supplied by Metrics Server. Cluster Autoscaler complements HPA by adjusting managed node-group capacity when newly requested Pods are unschedulable; auto-discovery minimizes node-group configuration management. VPA is not required for replica scaling and can conflict with HPA when both act on CPU resource requests. LEARN MORE Scale pod deployments with Horizontal Pod Autoscaler - Amazon EKS Cluster Autoscaler - Amazon EKS Best Practices Guide

questions.questionText: A company administers multiple AWS accounts by using AWS Organizations, with OUs for different business divisions. The company is updating its corporate network to use new IP address ranges. The company has 10 Amazon S3 buckets across different AWS accounts. The S3 buckets store reports for the various divisions. The S3 bucket configurations permit access only from private corporate network IP addresses. A DevOps engineer must update the IP address range that is permitted to access the contents of the S3 buckets. The DevOps engineer must also revoke permissions for two OUs in the company. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a new SCP that has two statements, one that allows access to the new range of IP addresses for all the S3 buckets and one that denies access to the old range of IP addresses for all the S3 buckets. Set a permissions boundary for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole role in the two OUs to deny access to the S3 buckets.

B. Create a new SCP that has a statement that allows only the new range of IP addresses to access the S3 buckets. Create another SCP that denies access to the S3 buckets. Attach the second SCP to the two OUs.

C. On all the S3 buckets, configure resource-based policies that allow only the new range of IP addresses to access the S3 buckets. Create a new SCP that denies access to the S3 buckets. Attach the SCP to the two OUs.

D. On all the S3 buckets, configure resource-based policies that allow only the new range of IP addresses to access the S3 buckets. Set a permissions boundary for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole role in the two OUs to deny access to the S3 buckets.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 bucket policies are resource-based policies that can allow or deny requests based on the request source IP address, making them the appropriate control for replacing the corporate IP ranges on every bucket. A service control policy does not grant permissions, but an explicit SCP deny attached to an OU limits all IAM users and roles in accounts beneath that OU and overrides otherwise applicable permissions. This provides an OU-wide S3 access revocation. LEARN MORE Bucket policies for Amazon S3 Service control policies (SCPs)
learnMore: Bucket policies for Amazon S3
Service control policies (SCPs)

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer used an AWS CloudFormation custom resource to configure AD Connector. The AWS Lambda function executed and created AD Connector, but CloudFormation is not moving from CREATE_IN_PROGRESS to CREATE_COMPLETE. Which action should the engineer take to resolve the issue?
options: A. Ensure the Lambda function code has exited successfully.
B. Ensure the Lambda function code returns a response to the pre-signed URL.
C. Ensure the Lambda function IAM role has cloudformation:UpdateStack permissions for the stack ARN.
D. Ensure the Lambda function IAM role has ds:ConnectDirectory permissions for the AWS account.
questions.explanation: A CloudFormation custom-resource provider must send a JSON SUCCESS or FAILED response to the request’s ResponseURL, a pre-signed Amazon S3 URL. CloudFormation waits for that response before it can proceed with and complete the stack operation. LEARN MORE CloudFormation custom resource request and response reference
learnMore: CloudFormation custom resource request and response reference

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is designing an application that integrates with a legacy REST API. The application includes an AWS Lambda function that reads records from an Amazon Kinesis data stream. The Lambda function sends those records to the legacy REST API. About 10% of the records the Lambda function sends from the Kinesis data stream contain data errors and require manual processing. The Lambda function event source configuration uses an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) dead-letter queue as an on-failure destination. The DevOps engineer has configured the Lambda function to process records in batches and has implemented retries for failures. During testing, the DevOps engineer observes that the dead-letter queue contains many records with no data errors that have already been processed by the legacy REST API. The DevOps engineer needs to configure the Lambda function's event source options to reduce the number of error-free records sent to the dead-letter queue. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Increase the retry attempts.
B. Configure the setting to split the batch when an error occurs.
C. Increase the concurrent batches per shard.
D. Decrease the maximum age of record.
questions.explanation: For a Kinesis event source mapping, BisectBatchOnFunctionError splits a failed batch into smaller batches and retries them, isolating the bad records. This prevents healthy records from remaining grouped with failing records and being unnecessarily retried or discarded to the on-failure SQS destination. LEARN MORE Retain discarded batch records for a Kinesis Data Streams event source in Lambda Lambda parameters for Amazon Kinesis Data Streams event source mappings
learnMore: Retain discarded batch records for a Kinesis Data Streams event source in Lambda
Lambda parameters for Amazon Kinesis Data Streams event source mappings

questions.questionText: A global company uses AWS Control Tower to manage multiple AWS accounts. The company hosts both internal and public applications. Each application team has its own AWS account for hosting applications. The accounts are consolidated into an organization in AWS Organizations. One AWS Control Tower member account acts as a centralized DevOps account with CI/CD pipelines that application teams use to deploy applications to their respective target AWS accounts. A deployment IAM role exists in the centralized DevOps account. An application team is trying to deploy its application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster in an application AWS account. A deployment IAM role exists in the application AWS account. The deployment occurs through an AWS CodeBuild project configured in the centralized DevOps account. The CodeBuild project uses an IAM service role for CodeBuild. The deployment fails with an Unauthorized error when CodeBuild attempts to connect to the cross-account EKS cluster. Which solution resolves this error?
options: A. Configure the application account’s deployment IAM role to have a trust relationship with the centralized DevOps account. Configure the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action. Configure the application account’s deployment IAM role to have the required access to the EKS cluster. Configure the EKS cluster aws-auth ConfigMap to map the role to the appropriate system permissions.

B. Configure the centralized DevOps account’s deployment IAM role to have a trust relationship with the application account. Configure the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action. Configure the centralized DevOps account’s deployment IAM role to allow the required access to CodeBuild.

C. Configure the centralized DevOps account’s deployment IAM role to have a trust relationship with the application account. Configure the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRoleWithSAML action. Configure the centralized DevOps account’s deployment IAM role to allow the required access to CodeBuild.

D. Configure the application account’s deployment IAM role to have a trust relationship with the AWS Control Tower management account. Configure the trust relationship to allow the sts:AssumeRole action. Configure the application account’s deployment IAM role to have the required access to the EKS cluster. Configure the EKS cluster aws-auth ConfigMap to map the role to the appropriate system permissions.
questions.explanation: Cross-account access from the CodeBuild workload requires a deployment role in the application account that trusts the DevOps-side principal to call sts:AssumeRole and that grants the required EKS permissions. For clusters using the legacy ConfigMap authentication mode, the assumed IAM role must also be mapped in the aws-auth ConfigMap to Kubernetes groups with the required RBAC permissions. AWS documents cross-account role access through a target role that trusts the source account or principal, and documents mapping IAM roles to Kubernetes permissions through aws-auth. LEARN MORE Authenticate to another account with IRSA - Amazon EKS Grant IAM users access to Kubernetes with a ConfigMap - Amazon EKS

Grant IAM users access to Kubernetes with a ConfigMap - Amazon EKS

questions.questionText: A company deploys its corporate infrastructure on AWS in multiple AWS Regions and Availability Zones. The infrastructure runs on Amazon EC2 instances and connects to AWS IoT Greengrass devices. The company also deploys additional resources on on-premises servers located at its corporate headquarters. The company wants to reduce the overhead of maintaining and updating its resources. Its DevOps team plans to use AWS Systems Manager to automate management and patch application. The team confirms that Systems Manager is available in the Regions where the resources are deployed. Systems Manager is also available in a Region near the corporate headquarters. Which combination of steps must the DevOps team take to implement automated patch and configuration management across the company’s EC2 instances, IoT devices, and on-premises infrastructure?
options: A. Apply tags to all the EC2 instances, AWS IoT Greengrass devices, and on-premises servers. Use Systems Manager Session Manager to push patches to all the tagged devices.
B. Use Systems Manager Run Command to schedule patching for the EC2 instances, AWS IoT Greengrass devices, and on-premises servers.
C. Use Systems Manager Patch Manager to schedule patching for the EC2 instances, AWS IoT Greengrass devices, and on-premises servers as a Systems Manager maintenance window task.

D. Configure Amazon EventBridge to monitor Systems Manager Patch Manager for updates to patch baselines. Associate Systems Manager Run Command with the event to initiate a patch action for all EC2 instances, AWS IoT Greengrass devices, and on-premises servers.

E. Create an IAM instance profile for Systems Manager. Attach the instance profile to all the EC2 instances in the AWS account. For the AWS IoT Greengrass devices and on-premises servers, create an IAM service role for Systems Manager.

F. Generate a managed-instance activation. Use the Activation Code and Activation ID to install Systems Manager Agent (SSM Agent) on each server in the on-premises environment. Update the AWS IoT Greengrass IAM token exchange role. Use the role to deploy SSM Agent on all the IoT devices.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager can automatically patch EC2 instances, edge devices, and on-premises servers after they are registered as Systems Manager managed nodes. A maintenance window schedules Patch Manager scan or install tasks. EC2 instances need an IAM instance profile for Systems Manager; Greengrass core devices use an SSM service role and require permissions added to the Greengrass token exchange role before deploying the Systems Manager Agent component. On-premises servers must be registered through a managed-instance activation, using its Activation Code and Activation ID when installing SSM Agent. questions.questionText: A company's DevOps team uses open-source Node Package Manager (NPM) libraries to build applications. The team runs its application build process in an AWS CodeBuild project that downloads the NPM libraries from public NPM repositories. The company wants to host the NPM libraries in private NPM repositories. The company must also be able to run checks on new library versions before the DevOps team uses those libraries. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Create an AWS CodeArtifact repository with an upstream repository named npm-store. Configure the application build process to use the CodeArtifact repository as the default source for NPM. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline to perform the required checks on package versions in the CodeArtifact repository. Set the package status to unlisted if a failure occurs.
B. Enable Amazon S3 caching in the CodeBuild project configuration. Add a step in the buildspec.yaml config file to perform the required checks on the package versions in the cache.

C. Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each library. Clone the required NPM libraries to the appropriate CodeCommit repository. Modify the CodeBuild appspec.yaml config file to use the private CodeCommit repositories. Add a step to perform the required checks on the package versions.

D. Create an AWS CodeCommit repository for each library. Clone the required NPM libraries to the appropriate CodeCommit repository. Modify the CodeBuild buildspec.yaml config file so that NPM uses the private CodeCommit repositories. Add an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that performs the required checks on the package versions for each new commit to the repositories. Configure the pipeline to revert to the most recent commit in the event of a failure.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeArtifact provides managed private npm repositories and can make packages from upstream repositories available to npm clients configured to use CodeArtifact. Package-version status can be changed to Unlisted; such versions are omitted from npm version listings, so npm dependency resolution does not select them. A CodePipeline validation workflow combined with CodeArtifact therefore centralizes package hosting and prevents failed new versions from normal selection without maintaining copied libraries and repositories manually. LEARN MORE Working with upstream repositories in CodeArtifact Packages overview - CodeArtifact

questions.questionText: A company has deployed a microservices-based application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application is encountering performance problems. The company needs to determine which microservices are responsible for those problems. Which solution will provide this information?
options: A. Configure AWS X-Ray for each ECS task. Create an X-Ray group for each microservice. Implement custom X-Ray subsegments in each microservice to capture detailed timing information. Use an X-Ray service map to visualize and identify slow microservices and requests.

B. Configure AWS X-Ray for each ECS task. Use an X-Ray service map to visualize the application's architecture and request flow. Filter the X-Ray traces by response time and error rate. Identify the microservices that have high latency or high error rates. Analyze individual traces to identify slow microservices and requests.

C. Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights for each ECS task. Analyze Container Insights metrics to identify slow microservices. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to filter the Container Insights log data by response time and error rate. Analyze the log data to identify slow requests.

D. Configure Amazon CloudWatch Container Insights for each ECS task. Use the CloudWatch automatic dashboard for Amazon ECS to identify slow microservices. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to analyze the Container Insights performance logs for each ECS task to identify slow requests.
questions.explanation: AWS X-Ray traces requests end to end across instrumented services. Its trace map visualizes service dependencies and highlights services or connections with high latency and errors; response-time and error filters, followed by individual trace analysis, identify the affected microservices and slow requests. LEARN MORE Using the X-Ray trace map - AWS X-Ray What is AWS X-Ray? - AWS X-Ray

What is AWS X-Ray? - AWS X-Ray

questions.questionText: A company runs its ecommerce website on AWS. The website is presently hosted on a single Amazon EC2 instance in one Availability Zone, with a MySQL database running on that same EC2 instance. The company must remove single points of failure from the architecture to improve the website’s availability and resilience. Which solution satisfies these requirements with the LEAST website configuration changes?
options: A. Deploy the application by using AWS Fargate containers. Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB. Use Amazon API Gateway to route requests.

B. Deploy the application on EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones. Put the EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora Multi-AZ. Use Amazon CloudFront for content delivery.
C. Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to deploy the application across multiple AWS Regions. Migrate the database to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon ElastiCache for session management.
D. Migrate the application to AWS Lambda functions. Use Amazon S3 for static content hosting. Migrate the database to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility).
questions.explanation: Deploying EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer removes the application-server single point of failure and routes traffic only to healthy capacity. Aurora provides MySQL-compatible, multi-Availability-Zone storage and can fail over to a replica in another Availability Zone, removing the database-host single point of failure. Retaining EC2 and a MySQL-compatible relational database requires less application change than migrating to containers, Lambda, or nonrelational databases. questions.questionText: A company is building a microservices-based application on AWS. The application includes AWS Lambda functions and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) services that require frequent deployments. A DevOps engineer must implement a consistent deployment solution for every application component. The solution must automate deployments, minimize downtime during updates, and manage the application's configuration data. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Use AWS CloudFormation to define and provision the Lambda functions and ECS services. Implement stack updates with resource replacement for all components. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage the configuration data.

B. Use AWS CodeDeploy to manage deployments for the Lambda functions and ECS services. Implement canary deployments for the Lambda functions. Implement blue/green deployments for the ECS services. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to manage the configuration data.

C. Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate deployments for the Lambda functions and ECS services. Use canary deployments for the Lambda functions and ECS services in a different AWS Region. Use AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to manage the configuration data.

D. Use AWS Systems Manager to manage deployments for the Lambda functions and ECS services. Implement all-at-once deployments for the Lambda functions. Implement rolling updates for the ECS services. Use AWS Secrets Manager to manage the configuration data.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy supports canary traffic shifting for AWS Lambda and blue/green deployments for Amazon ECS, providing automated releases with reduced service interruption. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store centrally stores, organizes, and retrieves application configuration data, including configuration values used at runtime. questions.questionText: A company that uses electronic patient health records operates a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances running the Amazon Linux operating system. The company must continuously ensure that the EC2 instances have operating system patches and application patches that comply with current privacy regulations. The company stores application patches in a custom repository. A DevOps engineer must automate deployment of the operating system and application patches. The DevOps engineer wants to use both the default operating system patch repository and the custom patch repository. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST effort?
options: A. Use AWS Systems Manager to create a new custom patch baseline that includes the default operating system repository and the custom repository. Run the AWS-RunPatchBaseline document by using the Run command to verify and install patches. Use the BaselineOverride API to configure the new custom patch baseline.
B. Use AWS Direct Connect to integrate the custom repository with the EC2 instances. Use Amazon EventBridge events to deploy the patches.
C. Use the yum-config-manager command to add the custom repository to the /etc/yum.repos.d configuration. Run the yum-config-manager-enable command to activate the new repository.

D. Use AWS Systems Manager to create a patch baseline for the default operating system repository and a second patch baseline for the custom repository. Run the AWS-RunPatchBaseline document by using the Run command to verify and install patches. Use the BaselineOverride API to configure the default patch baseline and the custom patch baseline.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager can use a custom Linux patch baseline with alternative repositories. Because specifying alternative repositories replaces the node’s default repositories for that operation, the baseline must explicitly include both the default Amazon Linux repository and the custom repository. AWS-RunPatchBaseline can scan and install patches while reporting patch compliance, and BaselineOverride can provide the selected baseline at runtime. questions.questionText: A company must adopt a multi-account strategy to deploy its applications and the related CI/CD infrastructure. The company has created an organization in AWS Organizations with all features enabled. The company has configured AWS Control Tower and set up a landing zone. The company must use AWS Control Tower controls (guardrails) across every AWS account in the organization. The company must create the accounts for a multi-environment application and ensure that every account receives an initial baseline configuration. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an AWS Control Tower Account Factory Customization (AFC) blueprint that uses the baseline configuration. Use AWS Control Tower Account Factory to provision a dedicated AWS account for each environment and a CI/CD account by using the blueprint.

B. Use AWS Control Tower Account Factory to provision a dedicated AWS account for each environment and a CI/CD account. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to apply the baseline configuration to the new accounts.

C. Use Organizations to provision a multi-environment AWS account and a CI/CD account. In the Organizations management account, create an AWS Lambda function that assumes the Organizations access role to apply the baseline configuration to the new accounts.

D. Use Organizations to provision a dedicated AWS account for each environment, an audit account, and a CI/CD account. Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to apply the baseline configuration to the new accounts.
questions.explanation: AWS Control Tower Account Factory provisions member accounts within the Control Tower landing zone, where Control Tower governance applies. Account Factory Customization (AFC) can associate a Service Catalog blueprint with account provisioning so that the baseline configuration is deployed as each account is created. AFC automates customized account deployment after its one-time setup and avoids maintaining separate StackSets, pipelines, or custom Lambda automation. questions.questionText: A company’s DevOps engineer uses AWS Systems Manager to carry out maintenance tasks. The company has several Amazon EC2 instances that need to be restarted after AWS Health notifications. The DevOps engineer must create an automated solution that uses Amazon EventBridge to remediate these notifications within the company’s scheduled maintenance windows. How should the DevOps engineer configure an EventBridge rule to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Configure an event source of AWS Health. Configure event types that indicate scheduled instance termination and retirement. Target the AWS-RestartEC2Instance Systems Manager Automation runbook to restart the EC2 instances.

B. Configure an event source of Systems Manager. Configure an event type that indicates a maintenance window. Target the AWS-RestartEC2Instance Systems Manager Automation runbook to restart the EC2 instances.

C. Configure an event source of AWS Health. Configure event types that indicate scheduled instance termination and retirement. Target a newly created AWS Lambda function that registers a Systems Manager maintenance window task to restart the EC2 instances.

D. Configure an event source of EC2. Configure an event type that indicates instance state notification. Target a newly created AWS Lambda function that registers a Systems Manager maintenance window task to restart the EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: AWS Health emits scheduled EC2 retirement and termination events to EventBridge. To ensure restart remediation occurs only during a Systems Manager maintenance window, the AWS Health event should invoke logic that registers the restart as a Systems Manager maintenance-window task. Directly targeting the AWS-RestartEC2Instance Automation runbook would execute when the EventBridge event is received rather than waiting for the maintenance window. questions.questionText: A company operates an AWS Control Tower landing zone. The company’s DevOps team creates a workload OU, with a development OU and a production OU nested beneath it. The company gives users full access to its AWS accounts for application deployments. The DevOps team must permit only a specified management IAM role to manage IAM roles and policies in AWS accounts that are in the production OU only. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an SCP that denies full access with a condition to exclude the management IAM role for the organization root.
B. Ensure that the FullAWSAccess SCP is applied at the organization root.
C. Create an SCP that allows IAM related actions. Attach the SCP to the development OU.
D. Create an SCP that denies IAM related actions with a condition to exclude the management IAM role. Attach the SCP to the workload OU.
E. Create an SCP that denies IAM related actions with a condition to exclude the management IAM role. Attach the SCP to the production OU.
questions.explanation: A Deny-based SCP attached to the production OU applies to accounts in that OU and its descendants. Denying IAM-related actions while excluding the specified management IAM role prevents all other principals in production accounts from managing IAM, despite their otherwise broad permissions. FullAWSAccess at the organization root provides the necessary SCP-level Allow path; SCPs set maximum permissions and do not grant permissions on their own. An explicit Deny in an SCP overrides identity-policy Allows. LEARN MORE SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: An AWS CodePipeline pipeline has implemented a code-release process. The pipeline is integrated with AWS CodeDeploy to deploy application versions to multiple Amazon EC2 instances for each CodePipeline stage. During a recent deployment, the pipeline failed because of a CodeDeploy issue. The DevOps team wants to improve deployment monitoring and notifications to reduce resolution times. What should the DevOps engineer do to create notifications when issues are detected?
options: A. Implement Amazon CloudWatch Logs for CodePipeline and CodeDeploy, create an AWS Config rule to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.

B. Implement Amazon EventBridge for CodePipeline and CodeDeploy, create an AWS Lambda function to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.

C. Implement AWS CloudTrail to record CodePipeline and CodeDeploy API call information, create an AWS Lambda function to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.

D. Implement Amazon EventBridge for CodePipeline and CodeDeploy, create an Amazon Inspector assessment target to evaluate code deployment issues, and create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify stakeholders of deployment issues.
questions.explanation: AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeDeploy publish execution and deployment state-change events directly to Amazon EventBridge. EventBridge rules can route failure events to AWS Lambda for issue-specific evaluation, and the function can publish notification messages to an Amazon SNS topic for stakeholders. AWS Config and Amazon Inspector do not evaluate CodeDeploy deployment failures, while CloudTrail API records are not the direct state-change event mechanism for this notification workflow. LEARN MORE Monitoring CodePipeline events AWS CodeDeploy events - Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A company has 20 service teams. Each team owns its own microservice. Every service team uses a separate AWS account for its microservice and a VPC using the 192.168.0.0/22 CIDR block. The company manages its AWS accounts through AWS Organizations. Each service team runs its microservice on multiple Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The microservices communicate with one another over the public internet. The company’s security team has issued a new requirement that all microservice communication use HTTPS over private network connections and must not traverse the public internet. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that meets these requirements while minimizing the number of changes required for each service team. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a new AWS account in AWS Organizations. Create a VPC in this account, and use AWS Resource Access Manager to share the private subnets of this VPC with the organization. Instruct the service teams to launch a new Network Load Balancer (NLB) and EC2 instances that use the shared private subnets. Use the NLB DNS names for communication between microservices.

B. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the microservice VPCs. Use AWS PrivateLink to create VPC endpoints in each AWS account for the NLBs. Create subscriptions to each VPC endpoint in each of the other AWS accounts. Use the VPC endpoint DNS names for communication between microservices.

C. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the microservice VPCs. Create VPC peering connections between each of the microservice VPCs. Update the route tables for each VPC to use the peering links. Use the NLB DNS names for communication between microservices.

D. Create a new AWS account in AWS Organizations. Create a transit gateway in this account, and use AWS Resource Access Manager to share the transit gateway with the organization. In each of the microservice VPCs, create a transit gateway attachment to the shared transit gateway. Update the route tables of each VPC to use the transit gateway. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each of the microservice VPCs. Use the NLB DNS names for communication between microservices.
questions.explanation: AWS PrivateLink provides private, cross-account connectivity to services exposed through Network Load Balancers and supports overlapping VPC CIDR ranges. Interface endpoint DNS names provide private access to each microservice without public-internet traversal. VPC peering and Transit Gateway are unsuitable because the VPCs all have the same overlapping 192.168.0.0/22 CIDR block. LEARN MORE AWS PrivateLink architecture VPC peering limitations
learnMore: VPC peering limitations

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer deploys an application to a fleet of Amazon Linux EC2 instances. The engineer must monitor system metrics across the fleet and monitor the relationship between network traffic and memory utilization for the application code. The engineer wants to track the data at 60-second intervals. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon CloudWatch basic monitoring to collect the NetworkIn metric and the MemoryBytesUsed metric. Graph the metrics in CloudWatch.
B. Use Amazon CloudWatch detailed monitoring to collect the NetworkIn metric and the MemoryBytesUsed metric. Graph the metrics in CloudWatch.
C. Use Amazon CloudWatch detailed monitoring to collect the NetworkIn metric. Install the CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to collect the mem_used metric. Graph the metrics in CloudWatch.
D. Use Amazon CloudWatch basic monitoring to collect the built-in NetworkIn metric. Install the CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to collect the mem_used metric. Graph the metrics in CloudWatch.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 detailed monitoring publishes built-in instance metrics such as NetworkIn at one-minute intervals, whereas basic monitoring publishes non-status metrics every five minutes. Memory utilization is an in-guest operating-system metric and must be collected with the CloudWatch agent; on Linux, the agent can publish mem_used. questions.questionText: A company uses an Amazon API Gateway Regional REST API to host its application API. The REST API uses a custom domain, and its default endpoint is disabled. The company’s internal teams consume the API. The company wants to use mutual TLS between the API and the internal teams as an additional authentication layer. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to create a private certificate authority (CA). Provision a client certificate that is signed by the private CA.
B. Provision a client certificate that is signed by a public certificate authority (CA). Import the certificate into AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).
C. Upload the provisioned client certificate to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the API Gateway mutual TLS to use the client certificate that is stored in the S3 bucket as the trust store.
D. Upload the provisioned client certificate private key to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the API Gateway mutual TLS to use the private key that is stored in the S3 bucket as the trust store.

E. Upload the root private certificate authority (CA) certificate to an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the API Gateway mutual TLS to use the private CA certificate that is stored in the S3 bucket as the trust store.
questions.explanation: API Gateway mutual TLS requires each client to present a certificate issued by a trusted certificate authority (CA). The custom domain’s truststore is an Amazon S3-hosted PEM bundle containing the issuing CA certificate chain through the root CA; it does not contain client private keys or individual client certificates. A private CA can issue the internal teams’ client certificates, and its root CA certificate can serve as the trust anchor when those certificates are directly issued by that root. LEARN MORE How to turn on mutual TLS authentication for your REST APIs in API Gateway MutualTlsAuthenticationInput - Amazon API Gateway

questions.questionText: A company’s application is presently deployed in a single AWS Region. The company recently opened a new office on another continent, and users in that office are encountering high latency. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and uses Amazon DynamoDB for its database layer. The instances run in an EC2 Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. A DevOps engineer must minimize application response times and improve availability for users in both Regions. Which combination of actions should be taken to resolve the latency issues?
options: A. Create a new DynamoDB table in the new Region with cross-Region replication enabled.
B. Create new ALB and Auto Scaling group global resources and configure the new ALB to direct traffic to the new Auto Scaling group.
C. Create new ALB and Auto Scaling group resources in the new Region and configure the new ALB to direct traffic to the new Auto Scaling group.
D. Create Amazon Route 53 records, health checks, and latency-based routing policies to route to the ALB.
E. Create Amazon Route 53 aliases, health checks, and failover routing policies to route to the ALB.
F. Convert the DynamoDB table to a global table.
questions.explanation: A multi-Region application deployment places an ALB and EC2 Auto Scaling group in the new Region because these resources are Regional. Route 53 latency-based routing directs users to the endpoint that provides the lowest latency and can use health checks to avoid unhealthy endpoints. DynamoDB global tables automatically replicate data among Regional replicas, enabling local reads and writes and improving multi-Region availability. questions.questionText: A company must ensure that flow logs stay configured for every existing and newly created VPC in its AWS account. The company uses an AWS CloudFormation stack to manage its VPCs. The solution must work for any VPC that any IAM user creates. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Add the AWS::EC2::FlowLog resource to the CloudFormation stack that creates the VPCs.
B. Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Add the company's AWS account to the organization. Create an SCP to prevent users from modifying VPC flow logs.
C. Turn on AWS Config. Create an AWS Config rule to check whether VPC flow logs are turned on. Configure automatic remediation to turn on VPC flow logs.
D. Create an IAM policy to deny the use of API calls for VPC flow logs. Attach the IAM policy to all IAM users.
questions.explanation: AWS Config’s managed VPC_FLOW_LOGS_ENABLED rule evaluates all AWS::EC2::VPC resources and marks a VPC noncompliant when flow logs are not enabled. Associating automatic remediation with that rule enables flow logs for noncompliant VPCs, covering both existing VPCs and VPCs created outside the CloudFormation stack. questions.questionText: A company wants to establish a continuous delivery pipeline. The company keeps application code in a private GitHub repository. It must deploy application components to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS), Amazon EC2, and AWS Lambda. The pipeline must support manual approval actions. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Use AWS CodePipeline with Amazon ECS. Amazon EC2, and Lambda as deploy providers.
B. Use AWS CodePipeline with AWS CodeDeploy as the deploy provider.
C. Use AWS CodePipeline with AWS Elastic Beanstalk as the deploy provider.
D. Use AWS CodeDeploy with GitHub integration to deploy the application.

AWS CodeDeploy supports application deployments for Amazon EC2, AWS Lambda, and Amazon ECS, enabling one CodePipeline deployment workflow to target all the required compute platforms. questions.questionText: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group manages EC2 instances created from an AMI. The AMI includes the AWS Systems Manager Agent. When an EC2 instance is launched into the Auto Scaling group, tags are applied to that instance. EC2 instances launched by the Auto Scaling group must receive the correct operating system configuration. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a Systems Manager Run Command document that configures the desired instance configuration. Set up Systems Manager Compliance to invoke the Run Command document when the EC2 instances are not in compliance with the most recent patches.
B. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association that links to the Systems Manager command document. Create a tag query that runs immediately.

C. Create a Systems Manager Run Command task that specifies the desired instance configuration. Create a maintenance window in Systems Manager Maintenance Windows that runs daily. Register the Run Command task against the maintenance window. Designate the targets.

D. Create a Systems Manager Patch Manager patch baseline and a patch group that use the same tags that the Auto Scaling group applies. Register the patch group with the patch baseline. Define a Systems Manager command document to patch the instances Invoke the document by using Systems Manager Run Command.
questions.explanation: A Systems Manager State Manager association that uses a command document can enforce an instance configuration. When the association targets instances by the tags applied by the Auto Scaling group, newly launched instances that receive those tags are automatically targeted and the association runs immediately, applying the required configuration. questions.questionText: A company runs a web application hosted on an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. The EKS cluster runs on AWS Fargate and is accessible through an internet-facing Application Load Balancer. The application is experiencing stability issues that result in longer response times. A DevOps engineer needs to configure observability in Amazon CloudWatch to troubleshoot the issue. The solution must provide only the minimum necessary permissions. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Deploy the CloudWatch agent as a Kubernetes StatefulSet to the EKS cluster.
B. Deploy the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry Collector as a Kubernetes DaemonSet to the EKS cluster.
C. Associate a Kubernetes service account with an IAM role by using IAM roles for service accounts in Amazon EKS. Use the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy AWS managed policy.
D. Associate a Kubernetes service account with an IAM role by using IAM roles for service accounts in Amazon EKS. Use the CloudWatchAgentAdminPolicy AWS managed policy.
E. Configure an IAM OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for the EKS cluster.
F. Enable EKS control plane logging for the EKS cluster.
questions.explanation: For Amazon EKS on AWS Fargate, the Container Insights collector must use a Fargate-compatible StatefulSet deployment because DaemonSets are not supported. The collector sends telemetry to CloudWatch by using an IAM role associated with its Kubernetes service account and the CloudWatchAgentServerPolicy, which grants the required agent permissions without the broader administrative access of CloudWatchAgentAdminPolicy. IAM roles for service accounts require an IAM OIDC provider for the EKS cluster. questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer needs a solution to migrate an application from on premises to AWS. The application runs on Linux and must use particular versions of Apache Tomcat, HAProxy, and Varnish Cache to operate correctly. Its operating-system-level parameters need tuning. The solution must provide a way to automate deployment of new application versions. The infrastructure must be scalable, and faulty servers must be automatically replaced. Which solution should the DevOps engineer use?
options: A. Upload the application as a Docker image that contains all the necessary software to Amazon ECR. Create an Amazon ECS cluster using an AWS Fargate launch type and an Auto Scaling group. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses Amazon ECR as a source and Amazon ECS as a deployment provider.

B. Upload the application code to an AWS CodeCommit repository with a saved configuration file to configure and install the software. Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk web server tier and a load balanced-type environment that uses the Tomcat solution stack. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses CodeCommit as a source and Elastic Beanstalk as a deployment provider.

C. Upload the application code to an AWS CodeCommit repository with a set of .ebextensions files to configure and install the software. Create an AWS Elastic Beanstalk worker tier environment that uses the Tomcat solution stack. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses CodeCommit as a source and Elastic Beanstalk as a deployment provider.

D. Upload the application code to an AWS CodeCommit repository with an appspec.yml file to configure and install the necessary software. Create an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group associated with an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. Create an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that uses CodeCommit as a source and CodeDeploy as a deployment provider.
questions.explanation: An Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group provides scalable capacity and replaces instances that are determined to be unhealthy. AWS CodeDeploy deployments to EC2 use an appspec.yml file and lifecycle-hook scripts, allowing the deployment to install and configure exact Linux software versions, apply operating-system tuning, and deploy application revisions. CodePipeline automates the release flow from CodeCommit through CodeDeploy. LEARN MORE CodeDeploy application specification (AppSpec) files Health checks for instances in an Auto Scaling group

Health checks for instances in an Auto Scaling group

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage multiple AWS accounts. The company has enabled all features for the organization. It uses AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy configurations to the accounts, and it uses AWS Config to monitor an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must ensure that every object uploaded to the S3 bucket uses AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) encryption. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS Config conformance pack that includes the s3-bucket-server-side-encryption-enabled rule. Deploy the conformance pack to the accounts. Configure the rule to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

B. Create an SCP that includes a deny statement for the s3:createBucket action and a condition statement where s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not aws:kms. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.

C. Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set to enable an AWS CloudTrail trail to capture S3 data events for the organization. In the stack set, create an Amazon EventBridge rule to match S3 PutObject events that do not use AWS KMS encryption. Configure the rule to target an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
D. Create an SCP that includes a deny statement for the s3:putObject action and a condition where s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not aws:kms. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
questions.explanation: An SCP attached to the organization root applies a preventive guardrail to member accounts. Denying s3:PutObject when s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption is not aws:kms prevents uploads that do not request SSE-KMS. The S3 encryption condition key is evaluated for object-write requests; aws:kms is the request value for SSE-KMS. AWS Config and CloudTrail-based rules detect or notify after configuration or upload activity rather than blocking a noncompliant upload. LEARN MORE Bucket policy examples using condition keys Specifying server-side encryption with AWS KMS (SSE-KMS)
learnMore: Bucket policy examples using condition keys
Specifying server-side encryption with AWS KMS (SSE-KMS)

questions.questionText: A company operates applications on Amazon EC2 instances in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. The EC2 instances sit behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Users have recently started to encounter errors when traffic is routed to certain EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer finds that the Auto Scaling group considers the affected instances healthy despite the application errors. The user experience returns to normal after the DevOps engineer fixes the application errors on the affected instances. The company needs to ensure that traffic is routed only to healthy instances that are not experiencing application errors. The company also requires a support team to receive a notification if the traffic-routing configuration changes. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks. Enable AWS Config. Create an AWS Config rule to ensure that any new Auto Scaling group will use ELB health checks. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify the support team if the traffic routing configuration changes. Configure the AWS Config rule to send a notification to the topic.

B. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 health checks. Enable AWS Config. Create an AWS Config rule to ensure that any new Auto Scaling group will use EC2 health checks. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify the support team if the traffic routing configuration changes. Configure the AWS Config rule to send a notification to the topic.

C. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use EC2 health checks. Create an Amazon CloudWatch synthetic canary to monitor the application. Create a CloudWatch alarm that is triggered when the CloudWatch canary fails. Configure the alarm to notify the support team when the alarm state is in alarm.

D. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use ELB health checks. Create an Amazon CloudWatch synthetic canary to monitor the application. Create a CloudWatch alarm that is triggered when the CloudWatch canary fails. Configure the alarm to notify the support team when the alarm state is in alarm.
questions.explanation: Elastic Load Balancing health checks allow an Auto Scaling group to use the load balancer’s target-health result. When the ALB reports a registered target as unhealthy, Auto Scaling marks the instance unhealthy and replaces it, unlike the default EC2 health checks, which do not assess application availability. AWS Config can evaluate Auto Scaling group configuration for ELB health checks and send Amazon SNS notifications for configuration or compliance changes. LEARN MORE About the health checks for your Auto Scaling group Notifications that AWS Config Sends to an Amazon SNS topic

Notifications that AWS Config Sends to an Amazon SNS topic

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy its application environment. A deployment failed during a recent update to the existing CloudFormation stack. A DevOps engineer found that some stack resources had been modified manually. The DevOps engineer needs a solution that detects manual resource modifications and sends an alert to the DevOps lead. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational effort?
options: A. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the DevOps lead to the topic by using an email address. Create an AWS Config managed rule that has the CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK identifier. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the NON_COMPLIANT resources status. Set the SNS topic as the rule target.

B. Tag all CloudFormation resources with a specific tag. Create an AWS Config custom rule by using the AWS Config Rules Development Kit Library (RDKlib) that checks all resource changes that have the specific tag. Configure the custom rule to mark all the tagged resource changes as NON_COMPLIANT when the change is not performed by CloudFormation. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the NON_COMPUANT resources status. Create an AWS Lambda function that sends an email message to the DevOps lead. Set the Lambda function as the rule target.

C. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Subscribe the DevOps lead to the topic by using an email address. Create an AWS Config managed rule that has the CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK identifier. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the COMPLIANT resources status. Set the SNS topic as the rule target.

D. Create an AWS Config managed rule that has the CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK identifier. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that is invoked on the NON_COMPLIANT resources status. Create an AWS Lambda function that sends an email message to the DevOps lead. Set the Lambda function as the rule target.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule CLOUDFORMATION_STACK_DRIFT_DETECTION_CHECK detects CloudFormation stack drift caused by changes outside CloudFormation management and marks a drifted stack as NON_COMPLIANT. An EventBridge rule can route that noncompliance event directly to an SNS topic, which notifies the email subscriber. This avoids maintaining a custom AWS Config rule or Lambda function. LEARN MORE cloudformation-stack-drift-detection-check - AWS Config Detect unmanaged configuration changes to stacks and resources with drift detection - AWS CloudFormation

Detect unmanaged configuration changes to stacks and resources with drift detection - AWS CloudFormation

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodeCommit for source-code control. Developers make their changes in various feature branches and open pull requests to move those changes to the main branch when they are ready for production. Developers must not be able to push changes directly to the main branch. The company assigned the AWSCodeCommitPowerUser managed policy to the developers’ IAM role, and the developers can now push directly to the main branch in every repository in the AWS account. What should the company do to prevent developers from directly pushing changes to the main branch?
options: A. Create an additional policy to include a Deny rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions. Include a restriction for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the main branch.

B. Remove the IAM policy, and add an AWSCodeCommitReadOnly managed policy. Add an Allow rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the main branch.
C. Modify the IAM policy. Include a Deny rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the main branch.

D. Create an additional policy to include an Allow rule for the GitPush and PutFile actions. Include a restriction for the specific repositories in the policy statement with a condition that references the feature branches.
questions.explanation: An additional customer-managed IAM policy with an explicit Deny overrides the permissions granted by AWSCodeCommitPowerUser. It can deny codecommit:GitPush and codecommit:PutFile for the selected repository resources when codecommit:References matches refs/heads/main, while preserving permitted work on feature branches. AWS-managed policies cannot be modified. AWS CodeCommit: Limit pushes and merges to branches LEARN MORE AWS CodeCommit: Limit pushes and merges to branches AWS CodeCommit customer managed policy examples

questions.questionText: An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A DevOps engineer uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy a new version. The deployment fails during the AllowTraffic lifecycle event, but the deployment logs do not identify the cause of the failure. What could cause this?
options: A. The appspec.yml file contains an invalid script that runs in the AllowTraffic lifecycle hook.
B. The user who initiated the deployment does not have the necessary permissions to interact with the ALB.
C. The health checks specified for the ALB target group are misconfigured.
D. The CodeDeploy agent was not installed in the EC2 instances that are part of the ALB target group.
questions.explanation: A misconfigured ALB target-group health check can prevent the newly deployed instances from becoming healthy when CodeDeploy allows traffic. AWS identifies incorrectly configured Elastic Load Balancing health checks as the typical cause of an AllowTraffic failure that has no reported cause in the deployment logs. The AllowTraffic event is reserved for CodeDeploy and cannot run AppSpec scripts. LEARN MORE Troubleshoot EC2/On-Premises deployment issues — AWS CodeDeploy AppSpec 'hooks' section — AWS CodeDeploy
