questions.questionText: A company is encountering failed AWS CodeDeploy deployments for a critical application. The application is deployed to Amazon EC2 instances. A DevOps engineer needs to analyze the failed deployments to determine the root cause of the failures. Which solution provides the appropriate information for troubleshooting the deployment issues?
options: A. Configure VPC Flow Logs to monitor network traffic. Use Amazon Inspector to detect non-network deployment issues. Use Amazon Detective to analyze the findings.

B. Enable detailed monitoring on the EC2 instances. Use AWS Systems Manager Run Command to run troubleshooting scripts on all the EC2 instances simultaneously. Analyze the results in AWS CloudTrail logs.

C. Use Amazon CloudWatch Logs to review application logs. Analyze CodeDeploy deployment logs in the /opt/codedeploy-agent/deployment-root/ directory on the EC2 instances. Use AWS X-Ray to trace requests through the application components.
D. Examine AWS Trusted Advisor checks for the CodeDeploy deployments. Use the AWS Health Dashboard to monitor application health. Analyze performance metrics in Amazon CloudWatch dashboards.
questions.explanation: For Amazon EC2 deployments, AWS CodeDeploy records deployment, agent, and script information on the instances under /opt/codedeploy-agent/deployment-root/; these logs contain deployment errors and lifecycle-event details needed to diagnose failures. Amazon CloudWatch Logs supports centralized review of application and CodeDeploy logs, and AWS X-Ray supplies request traces across application components. View log data for CodeDeploy EC2/On-Premises deployments LEARN MORE View log data for CodeDeploy EC2/On-Premises deployments Send CodeDeploy agent logs to CloudWatch

Send CodeDeploy agent logs to CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A company is moving its product development teams from an on-premises data center to a hybrid environment. The new environment will add four AWS Regions and will allow developers to use the geographically nearest Region. All development teams use a shared set of Linux applications. The on-premises data center stores the applications on a NetApp ONTAP storage device. The storage volume is mounted as read-only on the development on-premises VMs. The company updates the applications on the shared volume once per week. A DevOps engineer must replicate the data to all new Regions. The DevOps engineer must ensure that the data is always current with deduplication. The data must also be independent of the availability of the on-premises storage device. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon S3 File Gateway in the on-premises data center. Create S3 buckets in each Region. Set up a cron job to copy the data from the storage device to the S3 File Gateway. Set up S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to the S3 buckets in each Region.

B. Create an Amazon FSx File Gateway in one Region. Create file servers in Amazon FSx for Windows File Server in each Region. Set up a cron job to copy the data from the storage device to the FSx File Gateway.

C. Create Multi-AZ Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP instances and volumes in each Region. Configure a scheduled SnapMirror relationship between the on-premises storage device and the FSx for ONTAP instances.

D. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system in each Region. Deploy an AWS DataSync agent in the on-premises data center. Configure a schedule for DataSync to copy the data to Amazon EFS daily.
questions.explanation: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP supports NetApp SnapMirror volume replication from on-premises ONTAP to FSx for ONTAP and can schedule updates as frequently as every 5 minutes. SnapMirror preserves deduplicated and compressed data during replication, while each regional FSx for ONTAP destination holds an independent, read-only data-protection copy. Multi-AZ deployments provide availability across Availability Zones within each Region. LEARN MORE Replicating your data using NetApp SnapMirror - FSx for ONTAP Migrating to FSx for ONTAP using NetApp SnapMirror

questions.questionText: A large company has recently acquired a small company. The large company invited the small company to join the large company's existing organization in AWS Organizations as a new OU. A DevOps engineer determines that the small company must launch t3.small Amazon EC2 instance types for the company's application workloads. The small company must deploy the instances only in US-based AWS Regions. The DevOps engineer must use an SCP in the small company's new OU to ensure that the small company can launch only the required instance types. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure a statement to deny the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the ec2:InstanceType condition is not equal to t3.small.Configure another statement to deny the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the aws:RequestedRegion condition is not equal to us-*.

B. Configure a statement to allow the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the ec2:InstanceType condition is not equal to t3.small.Configure another statement to allow the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the aws:RequestedRegion condition is not equal to us-*.

C. Configure a statement to deny the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the ec2:InstanceType condition is equal to t3.small.Configure another statement to deny the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the aws:RequestedRegion condition is equal to us-*.

D. Configure a statement to allow the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the ec2:InstanceType condition is equal to t3.small.Configure another statement to allow the ec2:RunInstances action for all EC2 instance resources when the aws:RequestedRegion condition is equal to us-*.
questions.explanation: An SCP explicit Deny on ec2:RunInstances when ec2:InstanceType is not t3.small prevents every other instance type from being launched. A separate explicit deny for requests outside US Regions enforces the geographic restriction. SCPs set maximum permissions for attached OUs and accounts, so these denies override any IAM permissions that would otherwise allow the launches. questions.questionText: A company operates on AWS and has a VPC containing critical compute infrastructure with predictable traffic patterns. The company configured VPC Flow Logs to publish to a log group in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. The company’s DevOps team must configure a monitoring solution for the VPC Flow Logs that identifies anomalies in network traffic to the VPC over time. When the monitoring solution identifies an anomaly, the company must be able to initiate a response to it. How should the DevOps team configure the monitoring solution to satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Subscribe the log group to the data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics to detect log anomalies in the data stream. Create an AWS Lambda function to use as the output of the data stream. Configure the Lambda function to write to the default Amazon EventBridge event bus in the event of an anomaly finding.

B. Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream that delivers events to an Amazon S3 bucket. Subscribe the log group to the delivery stream. Configure Amazon Lookout for Metrics to monitor the data in the S3 bucket for anomalies. Create an AWS Lambda function to run in response to Lookout for Metrics anomaly findings. Configure the Lambda function to publish to the default Amazon EventBridge event bus.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function to detect anomalies. Configure the Lambda function to publish an event to the default Amazon EventBridge event bus if the Lambda function detects an anomaly. Subscribe the Lambda function to the log group.

D. Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Subscribe the log group to the data stream. Create an AWS Lambda function to detect log anomalies. Configure the Lambda function to write to the default Amazon EventBridge event bus if the Lambda function detects an anomaly. Set the Lambda function as the processor for the data stream.
questions.explanation: Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics can apply Random Cut Forest anomaly detection to a streaming data source, assigning anomaly scores based on recently observed patterns. CloudWatch Logs subscription filters can deliver log events to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams, and Kinesis Data Analytics can invoke an AWS Lambda function as an output destination. The Lambda function can publish a custom event to the default Amazon EventBridge event bus, where rules can invoke automated response targets. LEARN MORE Example: Detecting Data Anomalies on a Stream (RANDOM_CUT_FOREST Function) Using a Lambda Function as Output

Using a Lambda Function as Output

questions.questionText: A company operates an application that uses an Amazon API Gateway REST API, AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon DynamoDB table. The application currently operates in one AWS Region. The company needs to make the application highly available in two Regions. User traffic must route to the Region with the lowest latency. Which combination of steps satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Create a replica of the DynamoDB table in a second Region.
B. Create a global secondary index for the DynamoDB table.
C. Create copies of the REST API and the Lambda functions in a second Region.
D. Create health checks in Amazon Route 53. Create DNS records that include a failover routing policy.
E. Create health checks in Amazon Route 53. Create DNS records that include a latency routing policy.
F. Create DNS records in Amazon Route 53 that include a multivalue answer routing policy.
questions.explanation: A DynamoDB global table requires a replica table in each participating Region so that each regional application stack can use a local copy of the data. The REST API and Lambda functions must also be deployed in the second Region to provide a complete regional application endpoint. Route 53 latency-based routing selects the Region with the best latency, and associated health checks ensure that Route 53 routes only to healthy endpoints. LEARN MORE DynamoDB global tables core concepts Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53

Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53

questions.questionText: A company operates a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The application stores data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company has configured Amazon Route 53 with an alias record pointing to the ALB. A new company guideline mandates a geographically isolated disaster recovery (DR) site with an RTO of 4 hours and an RPO of 15 minutes. Which DR strategy satisfies these requirements with the LEAST change to the application stack?
options: A. Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different Availability Zone. Create an RDS read replica in the new Availability Zone, and configure the new stack to point to the local RDS DB instance. Add the new stack to the Route 53 record set by using a health check to configure a failover routing policy.

B. Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different AWS Region. Create an RDS read replica in the new Region, and configure the new stack to point to the local RDS DB instance. Add the new stack to the Route 53 record set by using a health check to configure a latency routing policy.

C. Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different AWS Region. In the event of an outage, copy and restore the latest RDS snapshot from the primary Region to the DR Region. Adjust the Route 53 record set to point to the ALB in the DR Region.

D. Launch a replica environment of everything except Amazon RDS in a different AWS Region. Create an RDS read replica in the new Region, and configure the new environment to point to the local RDS DB instance. Add the new stack to the Route 53 record set by using a health check to configure a failover routing policy. In the event of an outage, promote the read replica to primary.
questions.explanation: A prepared, cross-Region replica environment provides geographic isolation. Amazon RDS supports cross-Region read replicas for RDS for MySQL, and a read replica can be promoted to a standalone writable DB instance for disaster recovery. Route 53 failover routing with health checks supports an active/passive endpoint switch to the secondary ALB. Replication lag must be monitored so that the asynchronous replica remains within the 15-minute RPO; promotion and DNS failover can meet a 4-hour RTO. LEARN MORE Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance

Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodePipeline to automate its release pipeline. The pipeline uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy an application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the blue/green deployment model. The company needs to implement scripts that test the green version of the application before traffic is shifted. The scripts finish in 5 minutes or less. If these tests discover errors, the application must be rolled back. Which strategy meets these requirements?
options: A. Add a stage to the CodePipeline pipeline between the source and deploy stages. Use AWS CodeBuild to create a runtime environment and build commands in the buildspec file to invoke test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment command to stop the deployment.

B. Add a stage to the CodePipeline pipeline between the source and deploy stages. Use this stage to invoke an AWS Lambda function that will run the test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment command to stop the deployment.

C. Add a hooks section to the CodeDeploy AppSpec file. Use the AfterAllowTestTraffic lifecycle event to invoke an AWS Lambda function to run the test scripts. If errors are found, exit the Lambda function with an error to initiate rollback.

D. Add a hooks section to the CodeDeploy AppSpec file. Use the AfterAllowTraffic lifecycle event to invoke the test scripts. If errors are found, use the aws deploy stop-deployment CLI command to stop the deployment.
questions.explanation: For an Amazon ECS blue/green deployment, the AfterAllowTestTraffic AppSpec lifecycle event runs validation after the test listener sends traffic to the replacement task set and before production traffic is shifted. A Lambda validation hook can report failure, which causes CodeDeploy to stop the deployment and roll it back. Lambda can run a five-minute test. LEARN MORE AWS CodeDeploy: AppSpec hooks section AWS CodeDeploy: Deploy an Amazon ECS service with a validation test

questions.questionText: A company is rolling out a new application that uses Amazon EC2 instances. The company requires a solution to query application logs and AWS account API activity. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to Amazon S3. Use CloudWatch to query both sets of logs.

B. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to CloudWatch Logs. Use CloudWatch Logs Insights to query both sets of logs.

C. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon Kinesis. Configure AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to Kinesis. Use Kinesis to load the data into Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift to query both sets of logs.

D. Use the Amazon CloudWatch agent to send logs from the EC2 instances to Amazon S3. Use AWS CloudTrail to deliver the API logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena to query both sets of logs in Amazon S3.
questions.explanation: The CloudWatch agent can collect application log files from Amazon EC2 instances and send them to CloudWatch Logs. AWS CloudTrail can deliver AWS account API activity to a CloudWatch Logs log group. CloudWatch Logs Insights can search and analyze the resulting log data across selected log groups, providing a common query solution for both sources. questions.questionText: A DevOps team uses AWS CodePipeline, AWS CodeBuild, and AWS CodeDeploy to deploy an application. The application is a REST API that uses AWS Lambda functions and Amazon API Gateway. Recent deployments have introduced errors that affected many customers. The DevOps team requires a solution that reverts to the most recent stable application version when an error is detected. The solution must impact as few customers as possible. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Set the deployment configuration in CodeDeploy to LambdaAllAtOnce. Configure automatic rollbacks on the deployment group. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that detects HTTP Bad Gateway errors on API Gateway. Configure the deployment group to roll back when the number of alarms meets the alarm threshold.

B. Set the deployment configuration in CodeDeploy to LambdaCanary10Percent10Minutes. Configure automatic rollbacks on the deployment group. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that detects HTTP Bad Gateway errors on API Gateway. Configure the deployment group to roll back when the number of alarms meets the alarm threshold.

C. Set the deployment configuration in CodeDeploy to LambdaAllAtOnce. Configure manual rollbacks on the deployment group. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to send notifications every time a deployment fails. Configure the SNS topic to invoke a new Lambda function that stops the current deployment and starts the most recent successful deployment.

D. Set the deployment configuration in CodeDeploy to LambdaCanary10Percent10Minutes. Configure manual rollbacks on the deployment group. Create a metric filter on an Amazon CloudWatch log group for API Gateway to monitor HTTP Bad Gateway errors. Configure the metric filter to invoke a new Lambda function that stops the current deployment and starts the most recent successful deployment.
questions.explanation: A Lambda canary deployment that shifts 10% of traffic first limits the initial impact of a faulty release. CodeDeploy can monitor an associated CloudWatch alarm and automatically redeploy the last known good revision when the alarm threshold is met, avoiding custom rollback automation. The LambdaCanary10Percent10Minutes configuration leaves 90% of traffic on the stable version for 10 minutes before the remaining traffic shift. LEARN MORE Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy Configure advanced options for a deployment group

Configure advanced options for a deployment group

questions.questionText: A company has created an AWS Lambda function that processes orders received through an API. The company uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the Lambda function as the last stage of a CI/CD pipeline. A DevOps engineer has observed intermittent failures in the ordering API for a few seconds following deployment. After investigating, the DevOps engineer believes the failures occur because database changes have not fully propagated before the Lambda function is invoked. How should the DevOps engineer resolve this?
options: A. Add a BeforeAllowTraffic hook to the AppSpec file that tests and waits for any necessary database changes before traffic can flow to the new version of the Lambda function.
B. Add an AfterAllowTraffic hook to the AppSpec file that forces traffic to wait for any pending database changes before allowing the new version of the Lambda function to respond.
C. Add a BeforeInstall hook to the AppSpec file that tests and waits for any necessary database changes before deploying the new version of the Lambda function.
D. Add a ValidateService hook to the AppSpec file that inspects incoming traffic and rejects the payload if dependent services, such as the database, are not yet ready.
questions.explanation: For AWS Lambda deployments, CodeDeploy provides BeforeAllowTraffic and AfterAllowTraffic validation hooks. A BeforeAllowTraffic hook runs before production traffic is shifted to the new Lambda version, allowing it to wait for and verify required database changes before the new version receives requests. AfterAllowTraffic runs only after traffic has been enabled, while BeforeInstall and ValidateService are not Lambda deployment lifecycle hooks. LEARN MORE AppSpec 'hooks' section - AWS CodeDeploy PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus - AWS CodeDeploy API Reference

PutLifecycleEventHookExecutionStatus - AWS CodeDeploy API Reference

questions.questionText: A company is building a web application's infrastructure with AWS CloudFormation. The database engineering team manages the database resources in one CloudFormation template, while the software development team manages the web application resources in a separate CloudFormation template. As the application scope expands, the software development team needs to use resources that the database engineering team maintains. However, both teams want to retain their own review and lifecycle-management processes. Both teams also require resource-level change-set reviews. The software development team wants to deploy changes to this template through their CI/CD pipeline. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a stack export from the database CloudFormation template and import those references into the web application CloudFormation template.
B. Create a CloudFormation nested stack to make cross-stack resource references and parameters available in both stacks.
C. Create a CloudFormation stack set to make cross-stack resource references and parameters available in both stacks.
D. Create input parameters in the web application CloudFormation template and pass resource names and IDs from the database stack.
questions.explanation: CloudFormation exports let the database stack publish selected resource outputs, and the web application stack can consume them with Fn::ImportValue. This creates a supported cross-stack reference while keeping the stacks independently managed, reviewed through their own change sets, and deployed through separate lifecycle processes and CI/CD pipelines. LEARN MORE Get exported outputs from a deployed CloudFormation stack Fn::ImportValue

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. It uses an AWS CodePipeline pipeline to deploy the application across multiple AWS Regions. The pipeline has one stage per Region, and each stage includes an AWS CloudFormation action for that Region. When the pipeline deploys the application to a Region, the company wants to verify that the application is healthy before the pipeline proceeds to the next Region. Amazon Route 53 record sets are configured for the application in every Region. A DevOps engineer creates a Route 53 health check based on an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for each Region in which the application is deployed. What should the DevOps engineer do next to fulfill the requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS Step Functions workflow to check the state of the CloudWatch alarm. Configure the Step Functions workflow to exit with an error if the alarm is in the ALARM state. Create a new stage in the pipeline between each Region deployment stage. In each new stage, include an action to invoke the Step Functions workflow.

B. Configure an AWS CodeDeploy application to deploy a CloudFormation template with automatic rollback. Configure the CloudWatch alarm as the instance health check for the CodeDeploy application. Remove the CloudFormation actions from the pipeline. Create a CodeDeploy action in the pipeline stage for each Region.

C. Create a new pipeline stage for each Region where the application is deployed. Configure a CloudWatch alarm action for the new stage to check the state of the CloudWatch alarm and to exit with an error if the alarm is in the ALARM state

D. Configure the CloudWatch agent on the EC2 instances to report the application status to the Route 53 health check. Create a new pipeline stage for each Region where the application is deployed. Configure a CloudWatch alarm action to exit with an error if the CloudWatch alarm is in the ALARM state.
questions.explanation: A Standard AWS Step Functions workflow can query the applicable regional CloudWatch alarm and fail its execution when the alarm state is ALARM. Invoking that workflow in a validation stage after each regional deployment causes CodePipeline to wait for the health check and stop before advancing to the next Region if the application is unhealthy. AWS CodePipeline supports invoking Step Functions workflows and marks the action failed when a Standard workflow ends in a failed terminal state. LEARN MORE AWS Step Functions invoke action reference - AWS CodePipeline Use DescribeAlarms with an AWS SDK or CLI - Amazon CloudWatch
learnMore: Use DescribeAlarms with an AWS SDK or CLI - Amazon CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A company needs its internal web application to be highly available. Its architecture consists of one Amazon EC2 web server instance and one NAT instance that supplies outbound internet access for updates and access to public data. Which combination of architectural changes should the company make to provide high availability?
options: A. Add the NAT instance to an EC2 Auto Scaling group that spans multiple Availability Zones. Update the route tables.
B. Create additional EC2 instances spanning multiple Availability Zones. Add an Application Load Balancer to split the load between them.
C. Configure an Application Load Balancer in front of the EC2 instance. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms to recover the EC2 instance upon host failure.
D. Replace the NAT instance with a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone. Update the route tables.
E. Replace the NAT instance with a NAT gateway that spans multiple Availability Zones. Update the route tables.
questions.explanation: High availability for the web tier requires EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones behind an Application Load Balancer so traffic can be sent to healthy instances. For zonal NAT gateway architectures, egress resilience requires a NAT gateway in each Availability Zone and route tables that direct each subnet to the NAT gateway in the same Availability Zone; otherwise, failure of the NAT gateway’s Availability Zone removes internet access for workloads in other zones. LEARN MORE NAT gateway basics Example: VPC with servers in private subnets and NAT

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer has successfully created an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster with managed node groups. When the engineer attempts to add node groups to the cluster, the cluster returns the following error: "NodeCreationFailure: Instances failed to join the Kubernetes cluster." The DevOps engineer verifies that the EC2 worker nodes are running and that the EKS cluster is in an active state. How should the DevOps engineer troubleshoot this problem?
options: A. Ensure that the EKS cluster's VPC subnets do not overlap with the 172.17.0.0/16 CIDR range.
B. Use kubectl to update the kubeconfig file to use the credentials that created the cluster.
C. Run the AWSSupport-TroubleshootEKSWorkerNode runbook.
D. Create an AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) OpenID Connect (OIDC) provider for the cluster.
questions.explanation: The AWSSupport-TroubleshootEKSWorkerNode Systems Manager Automation runbook is designed to analyze an EC2 worker node and an EKS cluster for common conditions that prevent worker nodes from joining the cluster. Its required operating conditions are a running worker node and an ACTIVE EKS cluster. LEARN MORE AWSSupport-TroubleshootEKSWorkerNode - AWS Systems Manager Automation Runbook Reference Troubleshoot problems with Amazon EKS clusters and nodes
learnMore: Troubleshoot problems with Amazon EKS clusters and nodes

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer uses AWS CodeBuild to build software packages frequently. The CodeBuild project creates large Docker images that the DevOps engineer can reuse across multiple builds. The DevOps engineer wants to improve build performance while minimizing costs. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Store the Docker images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Implement a local Docker layer cache for CodeBuild.
B. Cache the Docker images in an Amazon S3 bucket that is available across multiple build hosts. Expire the cache by using an S3 Lifecycle policy.
C. Store the Docker images in an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Modify the CodeBuild project runtime configuration to always use the most recent image version.
D. Create custom AMIs that contain the cached Docker images. In the CodeBuild build, launch Amazon EC2 instances from the custom AMIs.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR is the appropriate registry for storing Docker images, and CodeBuild's local Docker layer cache caches existing Docker layers. This cache mode is intended for builds that create or pull large Docker images and reduces network transfer and rebuild work, improving build speed without the overhead of managing EC2 instances. LEARN MORE Local caching - AWS CodeBuild Cache builds to improve performance - AWS CodeBuild

questions.questionText: A company has an AWS Organizations organization with many OUs that contain many AWS accounts. The organization has a dedicated delegated administrator AWS account. The company requires the accounts in one OU to enforce server-side encryption for every Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume and Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue that is created or updated by an AWS CloudFormation stack. Which solution will enforce this policy before a CloudFormation stack operation in the accounts in this OU?
options: A. Activate trusted access to CloudFormation StackSets. Create a CloudFormation Hook that enforces server-side encryption on EBS volumes and SQS queues. Deploy the Hook across the accounts in the OU by using StackSets.

B. Set up AWS Config in all the accounts in the OU. Use AWS Systems Manager to deploy AWS Config rules that enforce server-side encryption for EBS volumes and SQS queues across the accounts in the OU.
C. Write an SCP to deny the creation of EBS volumes and SQS queues unless the EBS volumes and SQS queues have server-side encryption. Attach the SCP to the OU.

D. Create an AWS Lambda function in the delegated administrator account that checks whether server-side encryption is enforced for EBS volumes and SQS queues. Create an IAM role to provide the Lambda function access to the accounts in the OU.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation Hooks proactively inspect targeted resource configurations before CloudFormation creates or updates resources. A Hook can require the applicable encryption settings for EBS volumes and SQS queues and fail a noncompliant stack operation. Deploying the Hook to every account in the OU through StackSets provides the required organization-wide scope. LEARN MORE CloudFormation Hooks concepts Creating and managing CloudFormation Hooks

Creating and managing CloudFormation Hooks

questions.questionText: A company has begun using AWS across several teams. Each team has multiple accounts and distinct security profiles. The company manages these accounts in an organization through AWS Organizations. Every account has its own configuration and security controls. The company's DevOps team wants to use preventive and detective controls to govern all accounts. The DevOps team must ensure account security both now and as the company creates future accounts in the organization. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use Organizations to create OUs that have appropriate SCPs attached for each team. Place team accounts in the appropriate OUs to apply security controls. Create any new team accounts in the appropriate OUs.

B. Create an AWS Control Tower landing zone. Configure OUs and appropriate controls in AWS Control Tower for the existing teams. Configure trusted access for AWS Control Tower. Enroll the existing accounts in the appropriate OUs that match the appropriate security policies for each team. Use AWS Control Tower to provision any new accounts.

C. Create AWS CloudFormation stack sets in the organization's management account. Configure a stack set that deploys AWS Config with configuration rules and remediation actions for all controls to each account in the organization. Update the stack sets to deploy to new accounts as the accounts are created.

D. Configure AWS Config to manage the AWS Config rules across all AWS accounts in the organization. Deploy conformance packs that provide AWS Config rules and remediation actions across the organization.
questions.explanation: AWS Control Tower provides ongoing governance across AWS Organizations accounts by applying preventive controls to OUs and detective controls that monitor for noncompliance. Existing accounts can be enrolled in the OUs whose controls match their security policies, and Account Factory provisions new accounts into the governed landing zone. Preventive controls are implemented through SCPs or RCPs, while detective controls are implemented through AWS Config rules. LEARN MORE About controls in AWS Control Tower Preventive controls - AWS Control Tower
learnMore: About controls in AWS Control Tower
Preventive controls - AWS Control Tower

questions.questionText: A development team uses AWS CodeCommit for application-code version control and AWS CodePipeline to coordinate software deployments. The team has chosen a remote main branch as the pipeline trigger for integrating code changes. A developer pushed code changes to the CodeCommit repository but observed no pipeline activity, even after 10 minutes. Which action should be taken to troubleshoot this issue?
options: A. Check that an Amazon EventBridge rule has been created for the main branch to trigger the pipeline.
B. Check that the CodePipeline service role has permission to access the CodeCommit repository.
C. Check that the developer’s IAM role has permission to push to the CodeCommit repository.
D. Check to see if the pipeline failed to start because of CodeCommit errors in Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeCommit source actions require change detection through polling or an Amazon EventBridge rule. An EventBridge rule can match CodeCommit repository state-change events for the main branch and invoke the target pipeline; if that rule is absent or incorrectly configured, a push will not start the pipeline. LEARN MORE CodeCommit source actions and EventBridge Create an EventBridge rule for a CodeCommit source

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is building a CI/CD pipeline to create container images. The engineer must store container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) and scan the images for common vulnerabilities. The CI/CD pipeline must remain resilient to outages in upstream source container image repositories. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an ECR private repository in the private registry to store the container images and scan images when images are pushed to the repository. Configure a replication rule in the private registry to replicate images from upstream repositories.

B. Create an ECR public repository in the public registry to cache images from upstream source repositories. Create an ECR private repository to store images. Configure the private repository to scan images when images are pushed to the repository.

C. Create an ECR public repository in the public registry. Configure a pull through cache rule for the repository. Create an ECR private repository to store images. Configure the ECR private registry to perform basic scanning.
D. Create an ECR private repository in the private registry to store the container images. Enable basic scanning for the private registry, and create a pull through cache rule.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR pull-through cache rules synchronize and cache upstream images in an ECR private registry. If Amazon ECR cannot update an image from the upstream registry, it can still pull the last cached image, providing resilience to upstream outages. Basic scanning is configured at the ECR private-registry level and scans images for CVEs. LEARN MORE Sync an upstream registry with an Amazon ECR private registry Configuring basic scanning for images in Amazon ECR

Configuring basic scanning for images in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A company administers AWS accounts through AWS Organizations. It requires a solution that sends Amazon CloudWatch Logs data to an Amazon S3 bucket in a dedicated AWS account. The solution must support every existing and future CloudWatch Logs log group. Which solution will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Enable Organizations backup policies to back up all log groups to a dedicated S3 bucket. Add an S3 bucket policy that allows access from all accounts that belong to the company.

B. Create a backup plan in AWS Backup. Specify a dedicated S3 bucket as a backup vault. Assign all CloudWatch Logs log group resources to the backup plan. Create resource assignments in the backup plan for all accounts that belong to the company.

C. Create a backup plan in AWS Backup. Specify a dedicated S3 bucket as a backup vault. Assign all existing log groups to the backup plan. Create resource assignments in the backup plan for all accounts that belong to the company. Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to assign log groups to a backup plan. Create an AWS Config rule that has an automatic remediation action for all noncompliant log groups. Specify the runbook as the rule's target.

D. Create a CloudWatch Logs destination and an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream in the dedicated AWS account. Specify the S3 bucket as the destination of the delivery stream. Create subscription filters for all existing log groups in all accounts. Create an AWS Lambda function to call the CloudWatch Logs PutSubscriptionFilter API operation. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function when a CreateLogGroup event occurs.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription filters can send log events to an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream, and a CloudWatch Logs destination supports cross-account subscription delivery. Configuring Firehose to deliver to the central Amazon S3 bucket provides centralized storage. Subscription filters on existing log groups cover current data sources, while automation that calls PutSubscriptionFilter for each CreateLogGroup event extends the delivery configuration to newly created log groups. LEARN MORE Step 1: Create a destination - Amazon CloudWatch Logs Log group-level subscription filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
learnMore: Step 1: Create a destination - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
Log group-level subscription filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs

questions.questionText: A company operates a website using an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service connected to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The service was in a steady state, with tasks successfully responding to requests. A DevOps engineer updated the task definition with a new container image and deployed the new task definition to the service. The DevOps engineer observes that the service is repeatedly stopping and starting new tasks because the ALB health checks are failing. What should the DevOps engineer do to troubleshoot the failed deployment?
options: A. Ensure that a security group associated with the service allows traffic from the ALB.
B. Increase the ALB health check grace period for the service.
C. Increase the service minimum healthy percent setting.
D. Decrease the ALB health check interval.
questions.explanation: An ECS service health check grace period causes the ECS service scheduler to ignore unhealthy Elastic Load Balancing health checks for a specified time after a task first starts. Increasing it allows tasks running the new image sufficient time to initialize and respond before ECS marks them unhealthy and replaces them. LEARN MORE Update Amazon ECS service parameters — Health check grace period

questions.questionText: A company uses an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster to host its machine learning (ML) application. As the ML model and container image increase in size, new pods now take several minutes to start. A DevOps engineer must reduce startup time to seconds. The solution must also reduce startup time to seconds when a pod runs on nodes that have recently been added to the cluster. The DevOps engineer creates an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an automation in AWS Systems Manager. When new images are pushed to an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository, the automation prefetches the container images. The DevOps engineer also configures tags to apply to the cluster and node groups. What should the DevOps engineer do next to meet the requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows EventBridge to use Systems Manager to run commands in the EKS cluster's control plane nodes. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association that uses the control plane nodes' tags to prefetch corresponding container images.

B. Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows EventBridge to use Systems Manager to run commands in the EKS cluster's nodes. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association that uses the nodes' machine size to prefetch corresponding container images.

C. Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows EventBridge to use Systems Manager to run commands in the EKS cluster's nodes. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association that uses the nodes' tags to prefetch corresponding container images.

D. Create an IAM role that has a policy that allows EventBridge to use Systems Manager to run commands in the EKS cluster's control plane nodes. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association that uses the nodes' tags to prefetch corresponding container images.
questions.explanation: EKS worker nodes run the pods and pull their container images, whereas the EKS control plane is managed by Amazon EKS. The EventBridge role must permit Systems Manager to run commands on the EKS nodes. A State Manager association targeted by node tags applies to matching managed nodes; when newly created nodes receive those tags, Systems Manager automatically applies and immediately runs the association, allowing the required images to be prefetched before pods start. LEARN MORE EKS Control Plane - Amazon EKS Understanding targets and rate controls in State Manager associations - AWS Systems Manager
learnMore: EKS Control Plane - Amazon EKS
Understanding targets and rate controls in State Manager associations - AWS Systems Manager

questions.questionText: A company has deployed a new microservices-based application on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. After every deployment, the company wants to validate critical user journeys and API endpoints before directing traffic to the new application version. The company must implement an automated solution that detects issues in the new deployment and initiates a rollback when necessary. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Set up Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights for the ECS cluster. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to analyze the task states. Program the Lambda function to use the ECS UpdateService API call to initiate a rollback if a specific percentage of tasks fail.

B. Set up Amazon CloudWatch Application Insights for the ECS cluster. Configure Application Insights to monitor key performance indicators of the microservices in the critical user journeys and API calls. Create CloudWatch alarms based on the insights. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Step Functions workflow to evaluate the alarms. Configure the workflow to initiate a rollback if necessary by using the alarms' built-in integration with Amazon ECS.

C. Create CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that simulate critical user journeys and API calls. Implement AWS X-Ray tracing for all the microservices Configure X-Ray to send traces to CloudWatch. Create CloudWatch alarms based on error rates and latency metrics. Create an AWS Lambda function to analyze the traces and to initiate a rollback if necessary by using the alarms' built-in integration with Amazon ECS.

D. Create CloudWatch Synthetics canaries that simulate critical user journeys and API calls. Configure the canaries to run against the new deployment. Create CloudWatch alarms that are invoked when canaries fail. Use the alarms’ built-in integration with Amazon ECS to initiate a rollback if the alarms are invoked before traffic is routed to the new deployment.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Synthetics canaries can simulate customer routes and monitor application endpoints and APIs. Canary failures can trigger CloudWatch alarms, and Amazon ECS deployment alarms can mark a deployment as failed and automatically roll it back to the last successful deployment. This provides automated pre-traffic validation and rollback without maintaining custom orchestration or analysis code. LEARN MORE Synthetic monitoring (canaries) - Amazon CloudWatch How CloudWatch alarms detect Amazon ECS deployment failures - Amazon Elastic Container Service
learnMore: Synthetic monitoring (canaries) - Amazon CloudWatch
How CloudWatch alarms detect Amazon ECS deployment failures - Amazon Elastic Container Service

questions.questionText: A company operates applications in AWS accounts that belong to an AWS Organizations organization. The applications use Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon S3. The company needs to detect potentially compromised EC2 instances, suspicious network activity, and unusual API activity in its current AWS accounts and in any AWS accounts it creates in the future. When one of these events is detected, the company wants to use an existing Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to notify its operational support team for investigation and remediation. Which solution meets these requirements according to AWS best practices?
options: A. In the organization’s management account, configure an AWS account as the Amazon GuardDuty administrator account. In the GuardDuty administrator account, add the company’s existing AWS accounts to GuardDuty as members. In the GuardDuty administrator account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule with an event pattern to match GuardDuty events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic.

B. In the organization’s management account, configure Amazon GuardDuty to add newly created AWS accounts by invitation and to send invitations to the existing AWS accounts. Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set that accepts the GuardDuty invitation and creates an Amazon EventBridge rule. Configure the rule with an event pattern to match GuardDuty events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic. Configure the CloudFormation stack set to deploy into all AWS accounts in the organization.

C. In the organization’s management account, create an AWS CloudTrail organization trail. Activate the organization trail in all AWS accounts in the organization. Create an SCP that enables VPC Flow Logs in each account in the organization. Configure AWS Security Hub for the organization. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with an event pattern to match Security Hub events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic.

D. In the organization’s management account, configure an AWS account as the AWS CloudTrail administrator account. In the CloudTrail administrator account, create a CloudTrail organization trail. Add the company’s existing AWS accounts to the organization trail. Create an SCP that enables VPC Flow Logs in each account in the organization. Configure AWS Security Hub for the organization. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule with an event pattern to match Security Hub events and to forward matching events to the SNS topic.
questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty provides threat detection for potentially compromised EC2 instances, suspicious network behavior, and unusual API activity. Designating a GuardDuty delegated administrator in AWS Organizations centralizes management of member accounts; adding existing organization accounts enables GuardDuty for them, and the organization auto-enable capability covers future member accounts. GuardDuty findings are delivered to Amazon EventBridge, where a rule in the administrator account can route matching findings to the existing Amazon SNS topic. LEARN MORE Adding members to the organization - Amazon GuardDuty Processing GuardDuty findings with Amazon EventBridge

Processing GuardDuty findings with Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A company is building a mobile app that needs extensive automated testing across multiple device types. The company uses AWS CodePipeline for its CI/CD pipeline. The company must implement a scalable testing solution that can support increased test loads as the app expands. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST management overhead?
options: A. Integrate AWS Device Farm with the pipeline to run the tests and scale as needed.
B. Deploy a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances with various mobile device emulators and auto scaling to run the tests. Create a custom AWS Lambda function to invoke EC2 test runs.

C. Implement a containerized testing solution that uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with auto scaling. Configure the pipeline to invoke an AWS Lambda function to start the test runs on the ECS cluster.
D. Use AWS Lambda functions with custom runtime emulators to run the tests. Integrate the Lambda functions with the pipeline.
questions.explanation: AWS Device Farm is a managed mobile application testing service that runs tests in parallel across device pools and uses service-managed test hosts. AWS CodePipeline supports Device Farm directly as a test action, avoiding the operational work of provisioning and maintaining emulator fleets, container clusters, or custom invocation functions. LEARN MORE Integrating AWS Device Farm in a CodePipeline test stage Test frameworks and built-in tests in AWS Device Farm
