Test frameworks and built-in tests in AWS Device Farm

questions.questionText: A company must manage shared libraries for multiple projects across its development AWS account and production AWS account. The company has configured IAM roles for developers and defined an AWS CodePipeline pipeline by using the AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK). A DevOps engineer needs to implement a solution that ensures only developers can access the latest library versions. The solution must test shared packages independently before other applications consume the packages and before the packages are promoted to production. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a single AWS CodeArtifact repository for development and production in a central account. Use IAM policies for the developer roles to allow only developers to access the shared libraries. Create an Amazon EventBridge role to start an AWS CodeBuild project and to test each package before the package is copied to the production repository.

B. Create an AWS CodeArtifact repository in the development account. Create another CodeArtifact repository in the production account. For the development repository, add a repository policy that allows only developers to access the shared libraries. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to start the CodePipeline pipeline and to test each package before the package is copied to the production repository.

C. Create a single Amazon S3 bucket with versioning enabled for development and production in a central account. Use IAM policies for the developer roles to allow only the developers to access the shared libraries. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to start an AWS CodeBuild project and to test each package before the package is copied to production.

D. Create an Amazon S3 bucket with versioning enabled in the development account. Create another S3 bucket with versioning enabled in the production account. For the development S3 bucket, add a bucket policy that allows only developers to access the shared libraries. Create an Amazon EventBridge role to start the CodePipeline pipeline. Configure the role to test each package when the package is copied to production and to revert the changes if the tests fail.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeArtifact is designed to store and share software packages. Separate CodeArtifact repositories in the development and production accounts provide an explicit promotion boundary. A resource-based policy on the development repository can grant access only to the developer IAM principals, and an EventBridge rule can trigger the CodePipeline workflow so package tests run before promotion/copying into the production repository. CodeArtifact repository policies control which principals can access a repository. LEARN MORE Repository policies - CodeArtifact StartPipelineExecution - CodePipeline
learnMore: Repository policies - CodeArtifact
StartPipelineExecution - CodePipeline

questions.questionText: A company deploys a web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company keeps the application code in an AWS CodeCommit repository. When code is merged into the main branch, an AWS Lambda function invokes an AWS CodeBuild project. The CodeBuild project packages the code, stores the packaged code in AWS CodeArtifact, and invokes AWS Systems Manager Run Command to deploy the packaged code to the EC2 instances. Previous deployments have caused defects, EC2 instances that are not running the latest packaged-code version, and inconsistencies among instances. Which combination of actions should a DevOps engineer take to implement a more reliable deployment solution?
options: A. Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline that uses the CodeCommit repository as a source provider. Configure pipeline stages that run the CodeBuild project in parallel to build and test the application. In the pipeline, pass the CodeBuild project output artifact to an AWS CodeDeploy action.

B. Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline that uses the CodeCommit repository as a source provider. Create separate pipeline stages that run a CodeBuild project to build and then test the application. In the pipeline, pass the CodeBuild project output artifact to an AWS CodeDeploy action.
C. Create an AWS CodeDeploy application and a deployment group to deploy the packaged code to the EC2 instances. Configure the ALB for the deployment group.
D. Create individual Lambda functions that use AWS CodeDeploy instead of Systems Manager to run build, test, and deploy actions.

E. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Modify the CodeBuild project to store the packages in the S3 bucket instead of in CodeArtifact. Use deploy actions in CodeDeploy to deploy the artifact to the EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: AWS CodePipeline provides a controlled sequence of source, build, test, and deployment stages, and a CodeBuild output artifact can be made available to a subsequent CodeDeploy action. An EC2/On-Premises CodeDeploy application and deployment group can use an ALB target group during deployment. For in-place deployments, CodeDeploy deregisters instances while they are updated with the latest application revision and reregisters them after a successful deployment, helping prevent clients from reaching inconsistent or incomplete instances. LEARN MORE AWS CodeBuild build and test action reference AWS CodeDeploy deploy action reference

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS to operate digital workloads. Each application team has a separate AWS account for hosting its applications. The accounts are consolidated into an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to enforce security standards throughout the organization. To prevent noncompliance caused by security misconfigurations, the company has mandated AWS CloudFormation usage. A production support team can change resources in the production environment through the AWS Management Console to troubleshoot and resolve application-related issues. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that identifies, in near real time, any AWS service misconfiguration that causes noncompliance. The solution must automatically remediate the issue within 15 minutes of identification. It must also track noncompliant resources and events in a centralized dashboard with accurate timestamps. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST development overhead?
options: A. Use CloudFormation drift detection to identify noncompliant resources. Use drift detection events from CloudFormation to invoke an AWS Lambda function for remediation. Configure the Lambda function to publish logs to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Configure an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard to use the log group for tracking.

B. Turn on AWS CloudTrail in the AWS accounts. Analyze CloudTrail logs by using Amazon Athena to identify noncompliant resources. Use AWS Step Functions to track query results on Athena for drift detection and to invoke an AWS Lambda function for remediation. For tracking, set up an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that uses Athena as the data source.

C. Turn on the configuration recorder in AWS Config in all the AWS accounts to identify noncompliant resources. Enable AWS Security Hub with the --no-enable-default-standards option in all the AWS accounts. Set up AWS Config managed rules and custom rules. Set up automatic remediation by using AWS Config conformance packs. For tracking, set up a dashboard on Security Hub in a designated Security Hub administrator account.

D. Turn on AWS CloudTrail in the AWS accounts. Analyze CloudTrail logs by using Amazon CloudWatch Logs to identify noncompliant resources. Use CloudWatch Logs filters for drift detection. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function for remediation. Stream filtered CloudWatch logs to Amazon OpenSearch Service. Set up a dashboard on OpenSearch Service for tracking.
questions.explanation: AWS Config continuously records supported resource configuration changes and evaluates resources with managed or custom rules. AWS Config automatic remediation uses AWS Systems Manager Automation documents, while conformance packs package AWS Config rules and remediation actions for deployment across AWS Organizations. A delegated Security Hub administrator can use its dashboard to view findings from member accounts centrally. This supplies managed detection, remediation, and centralized tracking without building custom log-analysis and workflow components. LEARN MORE Recording AWS Resources with AWS Config Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config
learnMore: Recording AWS Resources with AWS Config
Setting Up Auto Remediation for AWS Config

questions.questionText: A development team uses AWS CodeCommit for application version control. The team uses AWS CodePipeline, AWS CodeBuild, and AWS CodeDeploy for its CI/CD infrastructure. In CodeCommit, the team recently merged pull requests that had not passed long-running tests in the code base. The team then needed to roll back codebase branches, causing lost time and wasted effort. A DevOps engineer must automate testing for CodeCommit pull requests so that reviewers can more easily view automated-test results during the pull request review. What should the DevOps engineer do to satisfy this requirement?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to the pullRequestStatusChanged event. Create an AWS Lambda function that invokes a CodePipeline pipeline with a CodeBuild action that runs the tests for the application. Program the Lambda function to post the CodeBuild badge as a comment on the pull request so that developers will see the badge in their code review.

B. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to the pullRequestCreated event. Create an AWS Lambda function that invokes a CodePipeline pipeline with a CodeBuild action that runs the tests for the application. Program the Lambda function to post the CodeBuild test results as a comment on the pull request when the test results are complete.

C. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to pullRequestCreated and pullRequestSourceBranchUpdated events. Create an AWS Lambda function that invokes a CodePipeline pipeline with a CodeBuild action that runs the tests for the application. Program the Lambda function to post the CodeBuild badge as a comment on the pull request so that developers will see the badge in their code review.

D. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to the pullRequestStatusChanged event. Create an AWS Lambda function that invokes a CodePipeline pipeline with a CodeBuild action that runs the tests for the application. Program the Lambda function to post the CodeBuild test results as a comment on the pull request when the test results are complete.
questions.explanation: Automated validation must be initiated when a pull request is created and again whenever its source branch is updated, ensuring that the displayed build status corresponds to the current proposed code. AWS CodeCommit publishes pullRequestCreated and pullRequestSourceBranchUpdated events through Amazon EventBridge; a Lambda function can use those events to start the test pipeline and add the resulting CodeBuild badge to the pull request for reviewer visibility. LEARN MORE Monitoring CodeCommit events in Amazon EventBridge and Amazon CloudWatch Events AWS CodeCommit events - Amazon EventBridge
learnMore: Monitoring CodeCommit events in Amazon EventBridge and Amazon CloudWatch Events

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to create separate AWS accounts for each department. The company must automate these tasks: Periodically update Linux AMIs with new patches and create a golden image. Install a new Chef agent version in the golden image when one is available. Make the newly generated AMIs available to the departments' accounts. Which solution fulfills these requirements with the LEAST management overhead?
options: A. Write a script to launch an Amazon EC2 instance from the previous golden image. Apply the patch updates. Install the new version of the Chef agent, generate a new golden image, and then modify the AMI permissions to share only the new image with the department's accounts.

B. Use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create an image pipeline that consists of the base Linux AMI and components to install the Chef agent. Use AWS Resource Access Manager to share EC2 Image Builder images with the department's accounts.

C. Use an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to update the Linux AMI by using the previous image. Provide the URL for the script that will update the Chef agent. Use AWS Organizations to replace the previous golden image in the department's accounts.

D. Use Amazon EC2 Image Builder to create an image pipeline that consists of the base Linux AMI and components to install the Chef agent. Create a parameter in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store to store the new AMI ID that can be referenced by the department's accounts.
questions.explanation: Amazon EC2 Image Builder provides a managed, scheduled pipeline for building patched golden AMIs and applying software-installation components, including Chef agent updates. Image Builder distribution settings can update an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter with the output AMI ID, giving consuming accounts a stable reference to the latest generated AMI. Sharing an Image Builder resource through AWS RAM does not itself provide the output EC2 AMI as a launchable golden image; AMI distribution and launch permissions are separate concerns. LEARN MORE What is EC2 Image Builder? Create and update AMI distribution configurations
learnMore: What is EC2 Image Builder?
Create and update AMI distribution configurations

questions.questionText: A company has an application that contains AWS Lambda functions. The Lambda functions execute Python code stored in an AWS CodeCommit repository. The company recently had production-environment failures due to an error in the Python code. An engineer has created unit tests for the Lambda functions to help prevent future defects from being released into the production environment. The company’s DevOps team must implement a solution that integrates the unit tests into an existing AWS CodePipeline pipeline. The solution must generate unit-test reports for the company to review. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Associate the CodeCommit repository with Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure a test stage that uses the new CodeBuild project. Create a buildspec.yml file in the CodeCommit repository. In the buildspec yml file, define the actions to run a CodeGuru review.

B. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure a test stage that uses the new CodeBuild project. Create a CodeBuild report group. Create a buildspec.yml file in the CodeCommit repository. In the buildspec.yml file, define the actions to run the unit tests with an output of JUNITXML in the build phase section. Configure the test reports to be uploaded to the new CodeBuild report group.

C. Create a new AWS CodeArtifact repository. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure a test stage that uses the new CodeBuild project. Create an appspec.yml file in the original CodeCommit repository. In the appspec.yml file, define the actions to run the unit tests with an output of CUCUMBERJSON in the build phase section. Configure the tests reports to be sent to the new CodeArtifact repository.

D. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. In the CodePipeline pipeline, configure a test stage that uses the new CodeBuild project. Create a new Amazon S3 bucket. Create a buildspec.yml file in the CodeCommit repository. In the buildspec yml file, define the actions to run the unit tests with an output of HTML in the phases section. In the reports section, upload the test reports to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild can run unit tests as a CodePipeline test stage and publish their results to a CodeBuild report group. CodeBuild supports JUnit XML test reports, and report groups retain test-run details that can be viewed in CodeBuild. LEARN MORE Test reports in AWS CodeBuild Build specification reference for CodeBuild
learnMore: Test reports in AWS CodeBuild
Build specification reference for CodeBuild

questions.questionText: A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations, with all features enabled, to manage its AWS accounts. Amazon EQ instances operate in the AWS accounts. The company requires all current EC2 instances to use Instance Metadata Service Version 2 (IMDSv2). The company must block AWS API calls that originate from EC2 instances that do not use IMDSv2. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a new SCP statement that denies the ec2:RunInstances action when the ec2:MetadataHttpTokens condition key is not equal to the value of required. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.

B. Create a new SCP statement that denies the ec2:RunInstances action when the ec2:MetadataHttpPutResponseHopLimit condition key value is greater than two. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
C. Create a new SCP statement that denies "*" when the ec2:RoleDelivery condition key value is less than two. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
D. Create a new SCP statement that denies when the ec2:MetadataHttpTokens condition key value is not equal to required. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
questions.explanation: The ec2:RoleDelivery condition key is included for requests made with an EC2 role session and indicates the IMDS version that delivered the credentials: 1.0 for IMDSv1 and 2.0 for IMDSv2. An SCP that denies "*" when ec2:RoleDelivery is less than 2.0 prevents any AWS API calls made with credentials delivered through IMDSv1, including from existing instances. The metadata-options condition keys instead restrict instance launch or metadata configuration APIs. LEARN MORE Transition to using Instance Metadata Service Version 2 AWS global condition context keys — ec2:RoleDelivery
learnMore: Transition to using Instance Metadata Service Version 2

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is creating a continuous-deployment pipeline for a serverless application that uses AWS Lambda functions. The company wants to minimize customer impact from an unsuccessful deployment and also monitor for issues. Which deployment-stage configuration meets these requirements?
options: A. Use an AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) template to define the serverless application. Use AWS CodeDeploy to deploy the Lambda functions with the Canary10Percent15Minutes Deployment Preference Type. Use Amazon CloudWatch alarms to monitor the health of the functions.

B. Use AWS CloudFormation to publish a new stack update, and include Amazon CloudWatch alarms on all resources. Set up an AWS CodePipeline approval action for a developer to verify and approve the AWS CloudFormation change set.

C. Use AWS CloudFormation to publish a new version on every stack update, and include Amazon CloudWatch alarms on all resources. Use the RoutingConfig property of the AWS::Lambda::Alias resource to update the traffic routing during the stack update.

D. Use AWS CodeBuild to add sample event payloads for testing to the Lambda functions. Publish a new version of the functions, and include Amazon CloudWatch alarms. Update the production alias to point to the new version. Configure rollbacks to occur when an alarm is in the ALARM state.
questions.explanation: AWS SAM integrates with CodeDeploy to perform gradual Lambda deployments. The Canary10Percent15Minutes deployment preference sends 10% of traffic to the new function version first and shifts the remaining traffic after 15 minutes. CloudWatch alarms can monitor function health; if an alarm is triggered, CodeDeploy automatically rolls back the deployment, limiting customer exposure to a defective version. LEARN MORE Deploying serverless applications gradually with AWS SAM DeploymentPreference - AWS Serverless Application Model
learnMore: Deploying serverless applications gradually with AWS SAM
DeploymentPreference - AWS Serverless Application Model

questions.questionText: A company recently created a new AWS Control Tower landing zone in a new AWS Organizations organization. The landing zone must demonstrate compliance with the Center for Internet Security (CIS) Benchmarks for AWS Foundations. The company’s security team wants to use AWS Security Hub to view compliance across every account. Only the security team must be permitted to view aggregated Security Hub findings. Additionally, specific users must be able to view findings from their own accounts in the organization. All accounts must be enrolled in Security Hub after account creation. Which combination of steps meets these requirements in the MOST automated way?
options: A. Turn on trusted access for Security Hub in the organization’s management account. Create a new security account by using AWS Control Tower. Configure the new security account as the delegated administrator account for Security Hub. In the new security account, provide Security Hub with the CIS Benchmarks for AWS Foundations standards.
B. Turn on trusted access for Security Hub in the organization’s management account. From the management account, provide Security Hub with the CIS Benchmarks for AWS Foundations standards.

C. Create an AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) permission set that includes the required permissions. Use the CreateAccountAssignment API operation to associate the security team users with the permission set and with the delegated security account.
D. Create an SCP that explicitly denies any user who is not on the security team from accessing Security Hub.
E. In Security Hub, turn on automatic enablement.

F. In the organization’s management account, create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to the CreateManagedAccount event. Create an AWS Lambda function that uses the Security Hub CreateMembers API operation to add new accounts to Security Hub. Configure the EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: AWS Organizations trusted access and a Security Hub delegated administrator provide centralized organization-wide Security Hub administration and aggregated findings. A dedicated Control Tower security account separates this security function from the management account, and the CIS AWS Foundations standard can be enabled from that administrator account. IAM Identity Center permission sets and account assignments provide scoped access: the security team can access the delegated administrator account, while other users can receive access only to their assigned accounts. Security Hub automatic enablement adds and enables newly created organization accounts natively, so custom EventBridge and Lambda membership automation is unnecessary. LEARN MORE AWS Security Hub CSPM and AWS Organizations Automatically enabling Security Hub CSPM in new organization accounts
learnMore: Automatically enabling Security Hub CSPM in new organization accounts

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage its AWS accounts. The organization root contains an OU named Environments. The Environments OU has two child OUs, named Development and Production, respectively. The Environments OU and its child OUs have the default FullAWSAccess policy attached. A DevOps engineer plans to remove the FullAWSAccess policy from the Development OU and replace it with a policy that allows all actions on Amazon EC2 resources. What will be the result of this policy replacement?
options: A. All users in the Development OU will be allowed all API actions on all resources.
B. All users in the Development OU will be allowed all API actions on EC2 resources. All other API actions will be denied.
C. All users in the Development OU will be denied all API actions on all resources.
D. All users in the Development OU will be denied all API actions on EC2 resources. All other API actions will be allowed.
questions.explanation: Service control policies set the maximum permissions that IAM principals can receive and use an implicit-deny model for actions not allowed by applicable SCPs. Because the root and parent OU allow all actions but the Development OU allows only Amazon EC2 actions, the effective SCP permissions for Development are limited to EC2; all other API actions are denied unless separately exempt from SCP evaluation. LEARN MORE SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations
learnMore: SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations
Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is deploying a new version of a company application through an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group associated with Amazon EC2 instances. After a period of time, the deployment fails. The engineer notices that every event associated with the particular deployment ID has a Skipped status, and that code was not deployed to the instances associated with the deployment group. What are valid causes of this failure?
options: A. The networking configuration does not allow the EC2 instances to reach the internet via a NAT gateway or internet gateway, and the CodeDeploy endpoint cannot be reached.
B. The IAM user who triggered the application deployment does not have permission to interact with the CodeDeploy endpoint.
C. The target EC2 instances were not properly registered with the CodeDeploy endpoint.
D. An instance profile with proper permissions was not attached to the target EC2 instances.
E. The appspec.yml file was not included in the application revision.
questions.explanation: When all lifecycle events in an EC2/On-Premises CodeDeploy deployment are skipped, the CodeDeploy agent may be unable to contact the CodeDeploy or Amazon S3 endpoint over HTTPS, which can result from the lack of an internet route through a NAT gateway or internet gateway. The same condition can occur when the target instance has no IAM instance profile or its profile lacks the permissions required by CodeDeploy. LEARN MORE Troubleshoot EC2/On-Premises deployment issues - AWS CodeDeploy Deployments on an EC2/On-Premises Compute Platform - AWS CodeDeploy
learnMore: Troubleshoot EC2/On-Premises deployment issues - AWS CodeDeploy
Deployments on an EC2/On-Premises Compute Platform - AWS CodeDeploy

questions.questionText: A company must update its order-processing application to improve resilience and availability. The application needs a stateful database and uses a single-node Amazon RDS DB instance to store customer orders and transaction history. A DevOps engineer must make the database highly available. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Migrate the database to Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Configure automatic failover between AWS Regions by using Amazon Route 53 health checks.
B. Migrate the database to Amazon EC2 instances in multiple Availability Zones. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach to connect all the instances to a single EBS volume.
C. Use the RDS DB instance as the source instance to create read replicas in multiple Availability Zones. Deploy an Application Load Balancer to distribute read traffic across the read replicas.
D. Modify the RDS DB instance to be a Multi-AZ deployment. Verify automatic failover to the standby instance if the primary instance becomes unavailable.
questions.explanation: An Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment automatically maintains a synchronous standby DB instance in a different Availability Zone. If the primary instance becomes unavailable, Amazon RDS automatically fails over to the standby, providing high availability and data redundancy without changing the application’s database architecture. Read replicas are asynchronous and are primarily for read scaling, not primary-instance failover. LEARN MORE Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS
learnMore: Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS
Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS

questions.questionText: A company is moving its container-based workloads to a multi-account AWS Organizations environment. The environment includes application workload accounts that the company uses to deploy and operate the containerized workloads. The company has also set up a shared services account for shared workloads in the organization. The company must comply with strict regulations. Every container image must undergo security scanning before deployment to any environment. Downstream deployment mechanisms can consume images only after they pass a scan with no critical vulnerabilities. Pre-scan and post-scan images must be isolated from each other so that a deployment can never use pre-scan images. A DevOps engineer must develop a strategy to centralize this process. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST administrative overhead?
options: A. Create Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories in the shared services account: one repository for each pre-scan image and one repository for each post-scan image. Configure Amazon ECR image scanning to run on new image pushes to the pre-scan repositories. Use resource-based policies to grant the organization write access to the pre-scan repositories and read access to the post-scan repositories.

B. Create pre-scan Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repositories in each account that publishes container images. Create repositories for post-scan images in the shared services account. Configure Amazon ECR image scanning to run on new image pushes to the pre-scan repositories. Use resource-based policies to grant the organization read access to the post-scan repositories.
C. Configure image replication for each image from the image's pre-scan repository to the image's post-scan repository.

D. Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline for each pre-scan repository. Create a source stage that runs when new images are pushed to the pre-scan repositories. Create a stage that uses AWS CodeBuild as the action provider. Write a buildspec.yaml definition that determines the image scanning status and pushes images without critical vulnerabilities to the post-scan repositories.

E. Create an AWS Lambda function. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that reacts to image scanning completed events and invokes the Lambda function. Write function code that determines the image scanning status and pushes images without critical vulnerabilities to the post-scan repositories.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR repository policies can grant cross-account push or pull access, enabling a shared services account to centralize separate pre-scan and approved-image repositories. ECR scan-completion events sent to EventBridge include scan status and severity counts, allowing a Lambda function to promote an image only when the completed scan has no CRITICAL findings. Restricting deployment accounts to read only from the approved repository prevents use of pre-scan images. Image replication does not enforce the vulnerability gate, and a separate CodePipeline for every repository creates more administrative overhead. LEARN MORE Amazon ECR events and EventBridge Private repository policies in Amazon ECR
learnMore: Private repository policies in Amazon ECR

questions.questionText: A company has several development groups operating in one shared AWS account. The groups’ senior manager needs an alert through a third-party API call when resource creation nears the account’s service limits. Which solution accomplishes this with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs periodically and targets an AWS Lambda function. Within the Lambda function, evaluate the current state of the AWS environment and compare deployed resource values to resource limits on the account. Notify the senior manager if the account is approaching a service limit.

B. Deploy an AWS Lambda function that refreshes AWS Trusted Advisor checks, and configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function periodically. Create another EventBridge rule with an event pattern matching Trusted Advisor events and a target Lambda function. In the target Lambda function, notify the senior manager.

C. Deploy an AWS Lambda function that refreshes AWS Health Dashboard checks, and configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the Lambda function periodically. Create another EventBridge rule with an event pattern matching Health Dashboard events and a target Lambda function. In the target Lambda function, notify the senior manager.

D. Add an AWS Config custom rule that runs periodically, checks the AWS service limit status, and streams notifications to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Deploy an AWS Lambda function that notifies the senior manager, and subscribe the Lambda function to the SNS topic.
questions.explanation: AWS Trusted Advisor provides Service Limits checks, and Amazon EventBridge can monitor changes in Trusted Advisor check status, including when a service quota is reached or approaching a limit. Periodically refreshing the checks and routing matching Trusted Advisor events to a Lambda function provides a low-code path for issuing the third-party API notification. LEARN MORE Monitoring AWS Trusted Advisor check results with Amazon EventBridge AWS Trusted Advisor
learnMore: Monitoring AWS Trusted Advisor check results with Amazon EventBridge

questions.questionText: A DevOps team operates an on-premises API that acts as the backend for an Amazon API Gateway endpoint. Customers have reported high response latency, which the development team confirmed by using the API Gateway latency metrics in Amazon CloudWatch. To determine the cause, the team must gather relevant data without adding latency. Which actions should they take to achieve this?
options: A. Install the CloudWatch agent server side and configure the agent to upload relevant logs to CloudWatch.
B. Enable AWS X-Ray tracing in API Gateway, modify the application to capture request segments, and upload those segments to X-Ray during each request.
C. Enable AWS X-Ray tracing in API Gateway, modify the application to capture request segments, and use the X-Ray daemon to upload segments to X-Ray.
D. Modify the on-premises application to send log information back to API Gateway with each request.
E. Modify the on-premises application to calculate and upload statistical data relevant to the API service requests to CloudWatch metrics.
questions.explanation: The CloudWatch agent can collect and upload server-side logs independently of API request processing. API Gateway active tracing samples requests, while application-generated X-Ray segments provide backend timing details. An X-Ray daemon receives segment data locally, buffers it, and uploads it to X-Ray in batches, avoiding direct AWS X-Ray API calls from each request path. LEARN MORE Amazon API Gateway active tracing support for AWS X-Ray Sending trace data to AWS X-Ray
learnMore: Sending trace data to AWS X-Ray

questions.questionText: A company maintains its AWS accounts in an AWS Organizations organization. AWS Config has been manually configured in every AWS account. The company needs to implement a solution that centrally configures AWS Config for all accounts in the organization. The solution must also record resource changes in a central account. Which combination of actions should a DevOps engineer take to meet these requirements?
options: A. Configure a delegated administrator account for AWS Config. Enable trusted access for AWS Config in the organization.
B. Configure a delegated administrator account for AWS Config. Create a service-linked role for AWS Config in the organization’s management account.
C. Create an AWS CloudFormation template to create an AWS Config aggregator. Configure a CloudFormation stack set to deploy the template to all accounts in the organization.
D. Create an AWS Config organization aggregator in the organization's management account. Configure data collection from all AWS accounts in the organization and from all AWS Regions.
E. Create an AWS Config organization aggregator in the delegated administrator account. Configure data collection from all AWS accounts in the organization and from all AWS Regions.
questions.explanation: AWS Config trusted access and a delegated administrator allow AWS Config to integrate with AWS Organizations. An organization aggregator created in the delegated administrator account can aggregate AWS Config configuration and compliance data from all organization accounts and all AWS Regions into that central account. LEARN MORE Registering a Delegated Administrator for AWS Config Creating Aggregators for AWS Config
learnMore: Registering a Delegated Administrator for AWS Config
Creating Aggregators for AWS Config

questions.questionText: A company has set up an Amazon S3 event source for an AWS Lambda function. The company requires the Lambda function to run when a new object is created or an existing object is modified in a specific S3 bucket. The Lambda function will use the S3 bucket name and S3 object key from the incoming event to read the contents of the created or modified S3 object. The Lambda function will parse those contents and store the parsed contents in an Amazon DynamoDB table. The Lambda function’s execution role has permission to read from the S3 bucket and write to the DynamoDB table. During testing, a DevOps engineer finds that the Lambda function does not run when objects are added to the S3 bucket or when existing objects are modified. Which solution will resolve the problem?
options: A. Increase the memory of the Lambda function to give the function the ability to process large files from the S3 bucket.
B. Create a resource policy on the Lambda function to grant Amazon S3 the permission to invoke the Lambda function for the S3 bucket.
C. Configure an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue as an OnFailure destination for the Lambda function.
D. Provision space in the /tmp folder of the Lambda function to give the function the ability to process large files from the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 requires permission in the Lambda function’s resource-based policy to invoke the function, typically granting the s3.amazonaws.com service principal lambda:InvokeFunction and limiting it to the source bucket (and account). The Lambda execution role governs the function’s access to S3 and DynamoDB after it starts; it does not grant S3 permission to start the function. LEARN MORE Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda Managing permissions in AWS Lambda
learnMore: Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda
Managing permissions in AWS Lambda

questions.questionText: A DevOps administrator manages the security of a company's Amazon CloudWatch Logs log groups. Company security policy requires that employee IDs not be visible in logs except to authorized personnel. Employee IDs use the pattern Emp-XXXXXX, where each X represents a digit. An audit found employee IDs in one log file. Engineers can access that log file, but they are not authorized to view employee IDs. The engineers currently have an AWS IAM Identity Center permission granting logs:* on all resources in the account. The administrator must mask employee IDs so that new log entries containing an employee ID are not visible to unauthorized personnel. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Create a new data protection policy on the log group. Add an Emp-\d{6} custom data identifier configuration. Create an IAM policy that has a Deny action for the Action":"logs:Unmask" permission on the resource. Attach the policy to the engineering accounts.

B. Create a new data protection policy on the log group. Add managed data identifiers for the personal data category. Create an IAM policy that has a Deny action for the "NotAction":"logs:Unmask" permission on the resource. Attach the policy to the engineering accounts.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function to parse a log file entry, remove the employee ID, and write the results to a new log file. Create a Lambda subscription filter on the log group and select the Lambda function. Grant the lambda:InvokeFunction permission to the log group.

D. Create an Amazon Data Firehose delivery stream that has an Amazon S3 bucket as the destination. Create a Firehose subscription filter on the log group that uses the Firehose delivery stream. Remove the "logs:*" permission on the engineering accounts. Create an Amazon Macie job on the S3 bucket that has an Emp-\d{6} custom identifier.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs data protection policies can use a custom data identifier with the Emp-\d{6} regular expression to detect and mask this company-specific employee-ID pattern in newly ingested events. Masked data is revealed only to principals with logs:Unmask; since logs:* grants that permission, an explicit Deny on logs:Unmask for engineers prevents unmasking while preserving their other required CloudWatch Logs access. LEARN MORE Custom data identifiers - Amazon CloudWatch Logs Help protect sensitive log data with masking - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
learnMore: Custom data identifiers - Amazon CloudWatch Logs
Help protect sensitive log data with masking - Amazon CloudWatch Logs

questions.questionText: A company is moving its on-premises Windows and Linux applications to AWS. It will use automation to launch Amazon EC2 instances that mirror the on-premises configurations. The migrated applications need access to shared storage that uses SMB for Windows and NFS for Linux. The company is also building a pilot-light disaster recovery (DR) environment in a separate AWS Region. It will use automation to launch and configure the EC2 instances in the DR Region. The company must replicate the storage to that DR Region. Which storage solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Use Amazon S3 for the application storage. Create an S3 bucket in the primary Region and an S3 bucket in the DR Region. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the primary Region to the DR Region.

B. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) for the application storage. Create a backup plan in AWS Backup that creates snapshots of the EBS volumes that are in the primary Region and replicates the snapshots to the DR Region.
C. Use a Volume Gateway in AWS Storage Gateway for the application storage. Configure Cross-Region Replication (CRR) of the Volume Gateway from the primary Region to the DR Region.
D. Use Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP for the application storage. Create an FSx for ONTAP instance in the DR Region. Configure NetApp SnapMirror replication from the primary Region to the DR Region.
questions.explanation: Amazon FSx for NetApp ONTAP supplies managed shared file storage that supports both SMB and NFS, including simultaneous multi-protocol access to the same volume. NetApp SnapMirror can replicate FSx for ONTAP data to a second FSx for ONTAP file system across AWS Regions, providing a current replica for the pilot-light DR environment. LEARN MORE Managing FSx for ONTAP volumes Replicating your data using NetApp SnapMirror
learnMore: Managing FSx for ONTAP volumes
Replicating your data using NetApp SnapMirror

questions.questionText: A company runs an application that uses a MySQL-compatible Amazon Aurora Multi-AZ DB cluster for its database. A cross-Region read replica was created for disaster-recovery purposes. A DevOps engineer needs to automate promotion of the replica so that it becomes the primary database instance if a failure occurs. Which solution will achieve this?
options: A. Configure a latency-based Amazon Route 53 CNAME with health checks so it points to both the primary and replica endpoints. Subscribe an Amazon SNS topic to Amazon RDS failure notifications from AWS CloudTrail and use that topic to invoke an AWS Lambda function that will promote the replica instance as the primary.

B. Create an Aurora custom endpoint to point to the primary database instance. Configure the application to use this endpoint. Configure AWS CloudTrail to run an AWS Lambda function to promote the replica instance and modify the custom endpoint to point to the newly promoted instance.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function to modify the application's AWS CloudFormation template to promote the replica, apply the template to update the stack, and point the application to the newly promoted instance. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke this Lambda function after the failure event occurs.

D. Store the Aurora endpoint in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Create an Amazon EventBridge event that detects the database failure and runs an AWS Lambda function to promote the replica instance and update the endpoint URL stored in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Code the application to reload the endpoint from Parameter Store if a database connection fails.
questions.explanation: An Aurora MySQL cross-Region read replica can be promoted to a standalone read/write DB cluster for disaster recovery. A Lambda function triggered by an EventBridge failure event can perform that promotion and update the promoted cluster endpoint in Systems Manager Parameter Store. When the application reloads the endpoint from Parameter Store after a connection failure, it reconnects to the newly promoted primary cluster. Parameter Store is intended for runtime configuration data such as database connection strings and supports updating values without application code changes or redeployment. LEARN MORE Promoting a read replica to a DB cluster for Aurora MySQL Working with Parameter Store
learnMore: Promoting a read replica to a DB cluster for Aurora MySQL
Working with Parameter Store

questions.questionText: A company stores application code in an AWS CodeConnections-compatible Git repository. The company wants to configure unit tests to run when pull requests are opened. It wants the test status to appear in pull requests after the tests complete. The company also wants to save output data files generated by the tests to an Amazon S3 bucket after the tests finish. Which combination of solutions meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an IAM service role to allow access to the resources that are required to run the tests.B Create a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline that has a test stage. Create a trigger to run the pipeline when pull requests are created or updated. Add a source action to report test results.
C. Create an AWS CodeBuild project to run the tests. Enable webhook triggers to run the tests when pull requests are created or updated. Enable build status reporting to report test results.
D. Create a buildspec.yml file that has a reports section to upload output files when the tests have finished running.
E. Create a buildspec.yml file that has an artifacts section to upload artifacts when the tests have finished running.
F. Create an appspec.yml file that has a files section to upload output files when the tests have finished running.
questions.explanation: An AWS CodeBuild project can be triggered by webhook events for pull-request creation or updates and can report build start and completion status to supported source providers. CodeBuild runs with an IAM service role that grants the permissions required by the build. The artifacts section of buildspec.yml identifies build output files for upload to the project’s Amazon S3 output location; the reports section is intended for test-report data. questions.questionText: A company uses AWS WAF to safeguard its cloud infrastructure. A DevOps engineer must enable an operations team to analyze log messages from AWS WAF. The operations team must be able to create alarms for particular patterns in the log output. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Create an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. Configure the appropriate AWS WAF web ACL to send log messages to the log group. Instruct the operations team to create CloudWatch metric filters.

B. Create an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster and appropriate indexes. Configure an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream to stream log data to the indexes. Use OpenSearch Dashboards to create filters and widgets.

C. Create an Amazon S3 bucket for the log output. Configure AWS WAF to send log outputs to the S3 bucket. Instruct the operations team to create AWS Lambda functions that detect each desired log message pattern. Configure the Lambda functions to publish to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.

D. Create an Amazon S3 bucket for the log output. Configure AWS WAF to send log outputs to the S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to create an external table definition that fits the log message pattern. Instruct the operations team to write SQL queries and to create Amazon CloudWatch metric filters for the Athena queries.
questions.explanation: AWS WAF can send web ACL logs directly to an Amazon CloudWatch Logs log group. CloudWatch Logs metric filters detect defined log-event patterns and produce CloudWatch metrics that can be used for alarms, providing log analysis and alerting without operating custom Lambda code, an OpenSearch cluster, or an S3/Athena workflow. questions.questionText: A company’s security policies mandate security-hardened AMIs for production environments. A DevOps engineer has used EC2 Image Builder to create a pipeline that builds the AMIs on a recurring schedule. The DevOps engineer must update the launch templates for the company’s Auto Scaling groups. The Auto Scaling groups must use the latest AMIs when launching Amazon EC2 instances. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to receive new AMI events from Image Builder. Target an AWS Systems Manager Run Command document that updates the launch templates of the Auto Scaling groups with the newest AMI ID.

B. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to receive new AMI events from Image Builder. Target an AWS Lambda function that updates the launch templates of the Auto Scaling groups with the newest AMI ID.

C. Configure the launch template to use a value from AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store for the AMI ID. Configure the Image Builder pipeline to update the Parameter Store value with the newest AMI ID.
D. Configure the Image Builder distribution settings to update the launch templates with the newest AMI IConfigure the Auto Scaling groups to use the newest version of the launch template.
questions.explanation: EC2 Image Builder distribution settings can update an EC2 launch template as part of AMI distribution. Image Builder creates a new launch-template version containing the new AMI ID and can set it as the default version. Auto Scaling groups configured to use the newest launch-template version will therefore launch subsequent instances from the newly built AMI without custom event-driven code or commands. questions.questionText: A company uses an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster and loads transactional data into the database every 5 hours. Data analysts use the Aurora PostgreSQL database to run short-running queries, create complex aggregated queries, and generate simple reports that use the data. The data analysts also manually update the data, including deleting and inserting data. The data analysts have reported performance problems. The database team recently identified a long-running idle transaction connection that affected performance by blocking other queries and preventing VACUUM operations. The team wants proactive notification of these possible operational issues and of the recommended actions to resolve them. The company's AWS account uses Amazon DevOps Guru to monitor all applications in the account. Which solution will meet these requirements?
options: A. Turn on Performance Insights and DevOps Guru in the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure DevOps Guru to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

B. Turn on Performance Insights in the existing Aurora PostrgreSQL DB cluster. Configure Amazon EventBridge to receive events from the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure the Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

C. Turn on Performance Insights and DevOps Guru in the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure the Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES).

D. Turn on Performance Insights in the existing Aurora PostrgreSQL DB cluster. Configure Amazon EventBridge to receive events from the existing Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster. Configure DevOps Guru to send notifications to the database team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).
questions.explanation: Amazon DevOps Guru for RDS can proactively detect long-running Aurora PostgreSQL connections in the idle in transaction state, which can hold locks and prevent VACUUM operations. Performance Insights is required for DevOps Guru to provide detailed database-specific analysis and recommendations. DevOps Guru uses Amazon SNS notification topics to notify teams when insights are created or updated. questions.questionText: A production account requires that every Amazon EC2 instance manually logged in to be terminated within 24 hours. All applications in the production account use Auto Scaling groups with the Amazon CloudWatch Logs agent configured. How can this procedure be automated?
options: A. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription to an AWS Step Functions application. Configure an AWS Lambda function to add a tag to the EC2 instance that produced the login event and mark the instance to be decommissioned. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke a second Lambda function once a day that will terminate all instances with this tag.

B. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that will be invoked by the login event. Send the notification to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic that the operations team is subscribed to, and have them terminate the EC2 instance within 24 hours.

C. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that will be invoked by the login event. Configure the alarm to send to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Use a group of worker instances to process messages from the queue, which then schedules an Amazon EventBridge rule to be invoked.

D. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription to an AWS Lambda function. Configure the function to add a tag to the EC2 instance that produced the login event and mark the instance to be decommissioned. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke a daily Lambda function that terminates all instances with this tag.
questions.explanation: Amazon CloudWatch Logs subscription filters can send matching login events directly to an AWS Lambda function. That function can identify and tag the originating EC2 instance for decommissioning. An Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule can invoke a daily Lambda function to find and terminate instances with that tag, providing an automated termination cycle within 24 hours. CloudWatch Logs subscription-filter destinations include Lambda, but not AWS Step Functions. LEARN MORE Log group-level subscription filters - Amazon CloudWatch Logs Concepts - Amazon CloudWatch Logs

Concepts - Amazon CloudWatch Logs

questions.questionText: A company has built its serverless infrastructure on AWS. The infrastructure includes an Amazon API Gateway REST API, multiple AWS Lambda functions, and Amazon EventBridge. The company wants to learn about new supply chain attacks that its CI/CD pipelines fail to catch. The company needs a solution that detects malicious activity in the deployed application. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Enable AWS WAF for the API Gateway REST API. Configure an AWS WAF ACL. Add the known bad inputs managed rule group.
B. Enable Amazon GuardDuty. Enable Lambda Protection. Use EventBridge for event notifications.
C. Deploy AWS CloudFormation Guard in the CI/CD pipelines. Write rules to catch the supply chain attacks.
D. Create a firewall in AWS Network Firewall. Configure a policy. Add the managed rule for the Emerging Threats rule group.
questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty Lambda Protection monitors Lambda network activity and generates findings when suspicious traffic indicates potentially malicious code in a Lambda function. GuardDuty sends findings to Amazon EventBridge, which can route them for event notifications. This provides runtime detection of malicious activity that was not caught before deployment. questions.questionText: A company has an AWS Control Tower landing zone that manages its organization through AWS Organizations. The company has created an OU structure based on its requirements. Its DevOps team has set up the core solution accounts and an account for all centralized AWS CloudFormation and AWS Service Catalog solutions. The company wants to provide a set of customizations that an account can request through AWS Control Tower. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Enable trusted access for CloudFormation with Organizations by using service-managed permissions.

B. Create an IAM role that is named AWSControlTowerBlueprintAccess. Configure the role with a trust policy that allows the AWSControlTowerAdmin role in the management account to assume the role. Attach the AWSServiceCatalogAdminFullAccess IAM policy to the AWSControlTowerBlueprintAccess role.
C. Create a Service Catalog product for each CloudFormation template.
D. Create a CloudFormation stack set for each CloudFormation template. Enable automatic deployment for each stack set. Create a CloudFormation stack instance that targets specific OUs.
E. Deploy the Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) CloudFormation stack.
F. Create a CloudFormation template that contains the resources for each customization.
questions.explanation: AWS Control Tower Account Factory Customization uses a CloudFormation template as a blueprint, packaged as an AWS Service Catalog product in a blueprint hub account. The hub account must contain an IAM role named AWSControlTowerBlueprintAccess that trusts the management account’s AWSControlTowerAdmin role and has the AWSServiceCatalogAdminFullAccess managed policy, allowing AWS Control Tower to administer the Service Catalog portfolio and products used for account customization. questions.questionText: A company has deployed an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that uses Amazon EC2 node groups. The company’s DevOps team uses the Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler and has recently installed a supported EKS cluster Autoscaler. The DevOps team must implement a solution to collect EKS cluster metrics and logs to establish a performance baseline. The team will create an initial set of thresholds for specific metrics and update those thresholds over time as the cluster is used. The team must receive an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) email notification if the initial thresholds are exceeded or if the EKS cluster Autoscaler is not operating properly. The solution must collect cluster, node, and pod metrics. It also must capture logs in Amazon CloudWatch. Which combination of steps should the DevOps team take to meet these requirements?
options: A. Deploy the CloudWatch agent and Fluent Bit to the cluster. Ensure that the EKS cluster has appropriate permissions to send metrics and logs to CloudWatch.
B. Deploy AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry to the cluster. Ensure that the EKS cluster has appropriate permissions to send metrics and logs to CloudWatch.
C. Create CloudWatch alarms to monitor the CPU, memory, and node failure metrics of the cluster. Configure the alarms to send an SNS email notification to the DevOps team if thresholds are exceeded.

D. Create a CloudWatch composite alarm to monitor a metric log filter of the CPU, memory, and node metrics of the cluster. Configure the alarm to send an SNS email notification to the DevOps team when anomalies are detected.
E. Create a CloudWatch alarm to monitor the logs of the Autoscaler deployments for errors. Configure the alarm to send an SNS email notification to the DevOps team if thresholds are exceeded.

F. Create a CloudWatch alarm to monitor a metric log filter of the Autoscaler deployments for errors. Configure the alarm to send an SNS email notification to the DevOps team if thresholds are exceeded.
questions.explanation: CloudWatch Container Insights uses the CloudWatch agent to collect EKS performance data at cluster, node, and pod levels, and Fluent Bit can send container logs to CloudWatch Logs. Container Insights exposes CPU, memory, and failed-node metrics that can be evaluated with CloudWatch alarms and routed to an SNS topic. To alert on Autoscaler errors written to logs, a CloudWatch Logs metric filter must create a numerical metric from matching error events; a CloudWatch alarm on that metric can send the SNS email notification. LEARN MORE Container Insights Amazon EKS and Kubernetes Container Insights metrics
learnMore: Container Insights

questions.questionText: A business has an application made up of five independent AWS Lambda functions. A DevOps engineer has created a CI/CD pipeline with AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeBuild that builds, tests, packages, and deploys each Lambda function sequentially. The pipeline uses an Amazon EventBridge rule so that it starts as soon as possible after a change is made to the application source code. After using the pipeline for several months, the DevOps engineer notices that it takes too long to finish. What should the DevOps engineer implement to BEST increase the pipeline speed?
options: A. Modify the CodeBuild projects within the pipeline to use a compute type with more available network throughput.
B. Create a custom CodeBuild execution environment that includes a symmetric multiprocessing configuration to run the builds in parallel.
C. Modify the CodePipeline configuration to run actions for each Lambda function in parallel by specifying the same runOrder.
D. Modify each CodeBuild project to run within a VPC and use dedicated instances to increase throughput.
questions.explanation: CodePipeline can run actions in parallel within the same stage when those actions use the same runOrder value. Because the five Lambda functions are independent, their build, test, package, and deployment actions can run concurrently rather than serially, reducing the overall pipeline completion time. LEARN MORE Action declaration - AWS CodePipeline

questions.questionText: A company is implementing a well-architected design for its globally accessible API stack. The design must provide both high reliability and quick response times for users in North America and Europe. The API stack includes the following three tiers: Amazon API Gateway AWS Lambda Amazon DynamoDB Which solution will satisfy the requirements?
options: A. Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway APIs in North America and Europe using health checks. Configure the APIs to forward requests to a Lambda function in that Region. Configure the Lambda functions to retrieve and update the data in a DynamoDB table in the same Region as the Lambda function.

B. Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway APIs in North America and Europe using latency-based routing and health checks. Configure the APIs to forward requests to a Lambda function in that Region. Configure the Lambda functions to retrieve and update the data in a DynamoDB global table.

C. Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway in North America, create a disaster recovery API in Europe, and configure both APIs to forward requests to the Lambda functions in that Region. Retrieve the data from a DynamoDB global table. Deploy a Lambda function to check the North America API health every 5 minutes. In the event of a failure, update Route 53 to point to the disaster recovery API.

D. Configure Amazon Route 53 to point to API Gateway API in North America using latency-based routing. Configure the API to forward requests to the Lambda function in the Region nearest to the user. Configure the Lambda function to retrieve and update the data in a DynamoDB table.
questions.explanation: Route 53 latency-based routing directs users to the regional endpoint with the lowest latency, while health checks prevent routing to an unhealthy endpoint. API Gateway and Lambda can therefore process requests in the selected Region. DynamoDB global tables replicate data across Regions and allow local replicas to serve reads and writes, supporting both low-latency regional access and multi-Region resilience. questions.questionText: A company has one AWS account running hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances in a single AWS Region. The company launches and terminates EC2 instances every hour. The account also contains existing EC2 instances that have been running for more than a week. The company’s security policy requires every running EC2 instance to have an EC2 instance profile attached. The company has created a default EC2 instance profile, which must be attached to any EC2 instances that have no profile attached. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches the Amazon EC2 RunInstances API calls. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to attach the default instance profile to the EC2 instances.

B. Configure AWS Config. Deploy an AWS Config ec2-instance-profile-attached managed rule. Configure an automatic remediation action that invokes an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to attach the default instance profile to the EC2 instances.

C. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches the Amazon EC2 StartInstances API calls. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook to attach the default instance profile to the EC2 instances.

D. Configure AWS Config. Deploy an AWS Config iam-role-managed-policy-check managed rule. Configure an automatic remediation action that invokes an AWS Lambda function to attach the default instance profile to the EC2 instances.
questions.explanation: The AWS Config managed rule ec2-instance-profile-attached evaluates EC2 instances and marks an instance noncompliant when no IAM instance profile is attached. AWS Config automatic remediation can invoke a Systems Manager Automation runbook, such as AWS-AttachIAMToInstance, to attach the default instance profile. This approach identifies and remediates both existing noncompliant instances and instances that later become noncompliant. questions.questionText: A company plans to use AWS CloudFormation to deploy infrastructure. The company has strict tagging and resource requirements and needs to restrict deployment to two Regions. Developers must be able to deploy multiple versions of the same application. Which solution ensures that resources are deployed according to company policy?
options: A. Create AWS Trusted Advisor checks to find and remediate unapproved CloudFormation StackSets.
B. Create a Cloud Formation drift detection operation to find and remediate unapproved CloudFormation StackSets.
C. Create CloudFormation StackSets with approved CloudFormation templates.
D. Create AWS Service Catalog products with approved CloudFormation templates.
questions.explanation: AWS Service Catalog provides developers with self-service access to administrator-approved CloudFormation products while enforcing governance through portfolio and launch constraints. Administrators can manage product versions, restrict the Regions where a product can launch, and apply resource tags during provisioning, ensuring deployments comply with the required resource and tagging policies. questions.questionText: A company runs AWS Lambda functions in the primary AWS Region of its AWS account. The company created the Lambda functions manually. The company must use a Python-based AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) application to manage the Lambda functions. Which solution satisfies these requirements with the LEAST implementation effort?
options: A. Start a partial scan by using the AWS CloudFormation infrastructure as code (IaC) generator. Filter by the Lambda resource type. Create an AWS CDK application from the scanned resources. Download the AWS CDK application. For each Lambda function, set the from_asset parameter for the Lambda handler code object.

B. Start a partial scan by using the AWS CloudFormation infrastructure as code (IaC) generator. Filter by the Lambda resource type. Create a CloudFormation template from the scanned resources. Download the CloudFormation template. For each Lambda function, replace the Code/S3Bucket property and the Code/S3Key property with the Code/ZipFile property. Convert the CloudFormation template to an AWS CDK application.

C. Start a partial scan by using the AWS CloudFormation infrastructure as code (IaC) generator. Filter by the Lambda resource type. Create a CloudFormation template from the scanned resources. Download the CloudFormation template. For each Lambda function, replace the Code/S3Bucket property and the Code/S3Key property with the Code/ImageUri property. Convert the CloudFormation template to an AWS CDK application.

D. Create a resource inventory by using AWS Config. Filter by the Lambda resource type. Export the inventory to a .csv file. Write an AWS CDK application that references the Lambda functions from the .csv file. For each Lambda function, set the from_asset parameter for the Lambda handler code object.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation IaC generator can scan unmanaged resources and migrate them into a new AWS CDK application. For Lambda functions, the code location is a write-only, mutually exclusive property set, so the generated form cannot reliably recover the original code configuration. Using the CDK Lambda from_asset code definition supplies the local deployment package and lets CDK package and deploy it, making direct CDK generation from the filtered scan the lowest-effort option. Code/ZipFile and Code/ImageUri are appropriate only when the existing function specifically uses inline ZIP code or an ECR image, respectively, and AWS Config inventory does not create IaC for resource management. questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions to implement an API. It uses an AWS CodePipeline pipeline to build and deploy that API. The pipeline includes a source stage, a build stage, and a deployment stage. The company deploys the API without running smoke tests. Shortly after deployment, it identifies multiple issues with the API. A security audit also discovers security vulnerabilities in the production code. The company wants to avoid these issues in the future. Which combination of steps meets this requirement?
options: A. Create a smoke test script that returns an error code if the API code fails the test. Add an action in the deployment stage to run the smoke test script after deployment. Configure the deployment stage for automatic rollback.

B. Create a smoke test script that returns an error code if the API code fails the test. Add an action in the deployment stage to run the smoke test script after deployment. Configure the deployment stage to fail if the smoke test script returns an error code.
C. Add an action in the build stage that uses Amazon Inspector to scan the Lambda function code after the code is built. Configure the build stage to fail if the scan returns any security findings.
D. Add an action in the build stage to run an Amazon CodeGuru code scan after the code is built. Configure the build stage to fail if the scan returns any security findings.
E. Add an action in the deployment stage to run an Amazon CodeGuru code scan after deployment. Configure the deployment stage to fail if the scan returns any security findings.
questions.explanation: A post-deployment smoke test that returns a nonzero error code and fails its pipeline action provides an automated quality gate: detected API failures mark the deployment stage as failed. A CodeGuru code scan in the build stage identifies code-quality and security issues before the artifact is deployed, and failing the stage when findings occur prevents vulnerable code from progressing through the pipeline. CodeBuild phases fail when a command fails, enabling a scan or test command to enforce these gates. questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Control Tower and AWS CloudFormation to manage its AWS accounts and create AWS resources. The company requires every Amazon S3 bucket to be encrypted with AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) when the S3 buckets are created in a CloudFormation stack. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Use AWS Organizations. Attach an SCP that denies the s3:PutObject permission if the request does not include an x-amz-server-side-encryption header that requests server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS).
B. Use AWS Control Tower with a multi-account environment. Configure and enable proactive AWS Control Tower controls on all OUs with CloudFormation hooks.
C. Use AWS Control Tower with a multi-account environment. Configure and enable detective AWS Control Tower controls on all OUs with CloudFormation hooks.

D. Use AWS Organizations. Create an AWS Config organizational rule to check whether a KMS encryption key is enabled for all S3 buckets. Deploy the rule. Create and apply an SCP to prevent users from stopping and deleting AWS Config across all AWS accounts,
questions.explanation: AWS Control Tower proactive controls are implemented through CloudFormation hooks and evaluate resources before CloudFormation deploys them. The Amazon S3 proactive control CT.S3.PR.10 requires bucket default server-side encryption using AWS KMS, so enabling proactive controls on the relevant OUs prevents noncompliant S3 bucket creation. questions.questionText: A developer maintains a fleet of 50 Amazon EC2 Linux servers. The servers belong to an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group and use Elastic Load Balancing for load balancing. Occasionally, application servers are terminated after they fail ELB HTTP health checks. The developer wants to perform root-cause analysis, but the server is terminated before application logs can be accessed. How can log collection be automated?
options: A. Use Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to put instances in a Pending:Wait state. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for EC2 Instance Terminate Successful and trigger an AWS Lambda function that invokes an SSM Run Command script to collect logs, push them to Amazon S3, and complete the lifecycle action once logs are collected.

B. Use Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to put instances in a Terminating:Wait state. Create an AWS Config rule for EC2 Instance-terminate Lifecycle Action and trigger a step function that invokes a script to collect logs, push them to Amazon S3, and complete the lifecycle action once logs are collected.

C. Use Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to put instances in a Terminating:Wait state. Create an Amazon CloudWatch subscription filter for EC2 Instance Terminate Successful and trigger a CloudWatch agent that invokes a script to collect logs, push them to Amazon S3, and complete the lifecycle action once logs are collected.

D. Use Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks to put instances in a Terminating:Wait state. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule for EC2 Instance-terminate Lifecycle Action and trigger an AWS Lambda function that invokes an SSM Run Command script to collect logs, push them to Amazon S3, and complete the lifecycle action once logs are collected.
questions.explanation: A termination lifecycle hook holds an instance in the Terminating:Wait state before it is terminated. Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling sends an EC2 Instance-terminate Lifecycle Action event to Amazon EventBridge when the lifecycle action occurs, so an EventBridge rule can invoke AWS Lambda. The Lambda function can invoke Systems Manager Run Command to collect the logs and upload them to Amazon S3, then complete the lifecycle action so termination can proceed. LEARN MORE How lifecycle hooks work in Auto Scaling groups Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling events - Amazon EventBridge
learnMore: How lifecycle hooks work in Auto Scaling groups

questions.questionText: A company has built a serverless web application hosted on AWS. The application consists of Amazon S3, Amazon API Gateway, several AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company uses AWS CodeCommit to store its source code. The source code combines AWS Serverless Application Model (AWS SAM) templates with Python code. A security audit and penetration test find that user names and passwords used for database authentication are hardcoded in CodeCommit repositories. A DevOps engineer must implement a solution that automatically detects and prevents hardcoded secrets. What is the MOST secure solution that meets these requirements?
options: A. Enable Amazon CodeGuru Profiler. Decorate the handler function with @with_lambda_profiler(). Manually review the recommendation report. Write the secret to AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a secure string. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from Parameter Store.

B. Associate the CodeCommit repository with Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer. Manually check the code review for any recommendations. Choose the option to protect the secret. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from AWS Secrets Manager.

C. Enable Amazon CodeGuru Profiler. Decorate the handler function with @with_lambda_profiler(). Manually review the recommendation report. Choose the option to protect the secret. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from AWS Secrets Manager.

D. Associate the CodeCommit repository with Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer. Manually check the code review for any recommendations. Write the secret to AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store as a string. Update the SAM templates and the Python code to pull the secret from Parameter Store.
questions.explanation: Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer integrates with AWS CodeCommit and AWS Secrets Manager to detect unprotected secrets, including hardcoded usernames and passwords, during code review. Its protect-credential action stores and manages the secret in AWS Secrets Manager, after which the application can retrieve the database credentials rather than retain them in source code. AWS CodeGuru Reviewer documentation LEARN MORE What is Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer? Find unprotected secrets in your code with Amazon CodeGuru Reviewer
