questions.questionText: A company operates a web application on AWS. Its web tier uses an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) deployment with the Fargate launch type behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and Amazon Route 53. The application uses an Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra) database. The company keeps container images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). New image versions are pushed on a regular basis. The company must implement a multi-Region recovery strategy with automatic failover to a secondary Region. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure Amazon ECR private image replication to a new ECR private registry in the secondary Region. Configure Amazon Keyspaces point-in-time recovery to copy to the secondary Region. Create an ALB and a new Fargate service with the desired count set to 0 in the secondary Region. Create new Route 53 DNS records that use a weighted routing policy.

B. Configure Amazon ECR private image replication to a new ECR private registry in the secondary Region. Configure Amazon Keyspaces multi-Region replication to the secondary Region. Create an ALB and a new Fargate service with the desired count set to 1 in the secondary Region. Create new Route 53 DNS records that use a failover routing policy.

C. Copy the current Amazon ECR private images to a new ECR private registry in the secondary Region. Configure Amazon Keyspaces multi-Region replication to the secondary Region. Create an ALB and a new Fargate service with the desired count set to 1 in the secondary Region. Create new Route 53 DNS records that use a failover routing policy.

D. Configure Amazon ECR private image replication to a new ECR private registry in the secondary Region. Configure Amazon Keyspaces multi-Region replication to the secondary Region. Create an ALB and a new Fargate service with the desired count set to 0 in the secondary Region. Create new Route 53 DNS records that use a weighted routing policy.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR private image replication replicates newly pushed private images across Regions, and Amazon Keyspaces multi-Region replication provides managed cross-Region database replication. A secondary ECS Fargate service with a desired count of 1 is ready to receive traffic. Amazon Route 53 failover routing supports active-passive behavior by routing to the healthy primary resource and returning the secondary resource when the primary is unhealthy. LEARN MORE Private image replication in Amazon ECR How multi-Region replication works in Amazon Keyspaces

How multi-Region replication works in Amazon Keyspaces

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodePipeline and AWS CodeDeploy to deploy application code to Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances send application and CodeDeploy logs to Amazon CloudWatch. Recently, the company manually rolled back a deployment due to application errors. The company wants to automate the rollback process when application errors occur. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a CloudWatch metric based on the application logs. Create a CloudWatch alarm based on the metric that will activate when application errors occur. Change the deployment group settings to use the CloudWatch alarm configuration. Configure the deployment group to use an auto rollback configuration.

B. Configure a CloudWatch alarm that uses a custom metric for application errors that are recorded in the CodeDeploy agent logs. Configure the current deployment to use the CloudWatch alarm for its alarm configuration. Configure the deployment to use an auto rollback configuration.

C. Create an AWS Lambda function that will create a new deployment by using the last successful application deployment. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches events from CodeDeploy that have a deployment status of FAILURE. Configure the EventBridge rule to target the Lambda function.

D. Create an AWS Lambda function that will create a new deployment group for the application deployment. Create a CloudWatch alarm based on metrics from the application logs. Configure the alarm to activate when an application error occurs on an EC2 instance. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function.
questions.explanation: A CloudWatch metric can be created from application logs and used by an alarm to detect application errors. Associating that alarm with the CodeDeploy deployment group causes CodeDeploy to stop the deployment when the alarm enters the ALARM state. Enabling automatic rollback for a deployment stopped on an alarm redeploys the last known good application revision. LEARN MORE Monitoring deployments with CloudWatch alarms in CodeDeploy Redeploy and roll back a deployment with CodeDeploy
learnMore: Monitoring deployments with CloudWatch alarms in CodeDeploy
Redeploy and roll back a deployment with CodeDeploy

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer operates a web application deployed on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) service behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Recent service updates caused application downtime because of problems in the application code. The DevOps engineer must design a solution that tests updates with a small portion of traffic before deploying to the remainder of the service. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a new pipeline in AWS CodePipeline. Connect the pipeline to an AWS CodeConnections compatible Git repository. Configure the pipeline with an ECRBuildAndPublish action and an Amazon ECS standard deployment action. Configure the ECS service to use the rolling update deployment type.

B. Update the ECS service to use AWS CodeDeploy as the deployment controller. Create a second target group for the ALCreate a CodeDeploy application and deployment group for the application. Use CodeDeploy to deploy updates by using the CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes deployment configuration.

C. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project that uses AWS Lambda compute and that includes an IAM role that has permissions to update the ECS task definition. Update the project buildspec file to call the Amazon ECS RegisterTaskDefinition API for deployments. Configure the ECS service to use the rolling update deployment type.

D. Create a new AWS CodeBuild project. Connect the project to an AWS CodeConnections compatible Git repository. Create a buildspec.yml file in the Git repository that contains commands to call the Amazon ECS UpdateService API. Set a slow start duration of 2 minutes on the ALB target group.
questions.explanation: An Amazon ECS blue/green deployment with AWS CodeDeploy and an ALB routes traffic between the original and replacement task sets through separate target groups. The CodeDeployDefault.ECSCanary10Percent15Minutes configuration sends 10% of traffic to the updated task set initially and shifts the remaining 90% after 15 minutes, providing a canary test period before full deployment. LEARN MORE CodeDeploy blue/green deployments for Amazon ECS Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy

Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled to manage multiple AWS accounts. AWS Config is enabled in every account. The company requires developers to create AWS CloudFormation stacks in a new AWS account to test features for a new application the developers are building. The company needs to ensure that developers can use only approved Amazon EC2 instance types for the application. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS Lambda function that returns SUCCESS when the EC2 instance type property matches a value from a list of approved instance types. Activate a CloudFormation Guard Hook in the new AWS account to run the Lambda function.

B. Create an AWS config rule that uses the desired-instance-type rule in the new AWS account. Provide the list of approved instance types in the rule configuration. Create a remediation for the AWS config rule that uses the AWS-StopEC2Instance remediation action.

C. Create an SCP that includes a Deny effect for ec2:RunInstnaces when the ec2:InstanceType property does not match a value from a list of approved instance types. Attach the SCP to the root of the organization.
D. Create a CloudFormation Guard rule to ensure that the EC2 instance type matches a value from a list of approved instance types. Activate a Guard Hook in the new AWS account to run the Guard rule.
questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation Guard Hooks evaluate CloudFormation resource configurations before stack operations are allowed. A Guard rule can check an AWS::EC2::Instance resource’s instance type against an approved list, and the Guard Hook can be configured to fail noncompliant stack operations in the new account. AWS Config remediation occurs after a resource is evaluated, while a Lambda function requires a Lambda Hook rather than a Guard Hook. LEARN MORE Guard Hooks Creating and managing CloudFormation Hooks
learnMore: Guard Hooks
Creating and managing CloudFormation Hooks

questions.questionText: A company is migrating an application to Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The company wants to centralize log data in Amazon CloudWatch in the us-west-2 Region. No Amazon ECS CloudWatch log groups currently exist. The company receives the following error when an ECS task tries to launch: service my-service-name was unable to place a task because no container instance met all of its requirements. The ECS task definition contains this container log configuration: The ECS cluster uses an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to supply task capacity. The EC2 instances launch an Amazon ECS-optimized AMI. Which solution will resolve the problem?
options: A. Modify the ECS infrastructure IAM role to add the logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents permissions.
B. Modify the ECS log configuration to use blocking mode.
C. Modify the ECS container instance IAM role to add the logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents permissions.
D. Modify the ECS log configuration by setting the awslogs-create-group option to false.
questions.explanation: For Amazon ECS tasks running on EC2 with the awslogs log driver, the Amazon ECS container instances need logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents permissions on the IAM role used to launch those instances. Those permissions allow the logging driver to create CloudWatch Logs streams and publish container log events. LEARN MORE Send Amazon ECS logs to CloudWatch Amazon ECS container instance IAM role
learnMore: Send Amazon ECS logs to CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A software engineering team uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy a new application version. The team needs the deployment process to automatically roll back to the prior version if any issues occur. During deployment, a health check validates the application's stability. If that health check fails, the deployment must automatically revert. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Implement lifecycle event hooks in the deployment configuration.
B. Use AWS CloudFormation to monitor the health of the deployment.
C. Set up alarms in Amazon CloudWatch to start a rollback.
D. Configure automatic rollback settings in AWS CodeDeploy.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeDeploy automatic rollback settings can redeploy the last known good application revision when a deployment fails. A health-check failure marks the deployment as failed, so this configuration provides the required automatic reversion. questions.questionText: A video-sharing company stores its videos in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company must analyze user-access patterns, such as the number of users who access a particular video each month. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST development effort?
options: A. Enable Amazon S3 server access logging. Load the access logs into an Amazon Aurora database. Run SQL queries on the Aurora database to analyze the user access patterns.
B. Enable Amazon S3 server access logging. Use Amazon Athena to create an external table that contains the access logs. Run SQL queries on the Athena table to analyze the user access patterns.

C. Invoke an AWS Lambda function for every S3 object access event. Configure the Lambda function to write the file access information, including user ID, S3 bucket ID, and file key, to an Amazon Aurora database. Run SQL queries on the Aurora database to analyze the user access patterns.

D. Record a log message in Amazon CloudWatch Logs for every S3 object access event. Configure a log stream in CloudWatch Logs to write the file access information, including user ID, S3 bucket ID, and file key, to an Amazon Managed Service for Apache Flink application. Perform a sliding window analysis on the user access patterns.
questions.explanation: Amazon S3 server access logs provide request-level records, and Amazon Athena can query those logs in Amazon S3 through an external table using SQL. This supports aggregating access activity by object and month without building a data-loading pipeline, application code, or a database. AWS documents querying S3 access logs with Athena, including queries that filter requesters, object keys, and time periods. LEARN MORE Using Amazon S3 server access logs to identify requests Enabling Amazon S3 server access logging

questions.questionText: A company is building a web application and uses AWS CodeBuild for its CI/CD pipeline. The company must produce multiple artifacts from one build process and must be able to identify which build generated each artifact. The artifacts must be stored in an Amazon S3 bucket for subsequent processing and deployment. Builds run frequently and use a large Git repository. The company needs to optimize build times. Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Configure the buildspec.yml file to specify multiple artifacts with different file sets. Enable local caching for the build process by using source cache mode. Use environment variables to dynamically name artifacts based on the build ID.

B. Configure the buildspec.yml file to output all files as a single artifact. Enable local caching for the build process by using custom cache mode. Create an AWS Lambda function that is invoked by CodeBuild completion. Program the Lambda function to split the artifact into multiple files and to upload the files to the S3 bucket with dynamic names based on build ID.

C. Create separate CodeBuild projects for each artifact type. Enable local caching for the build process by using Docker layer cache mode. Configure each project to output a single artifact to the S3 bucket with a dynamic name based on build ID. Use AWS Step Functions to orchestrate the projects in parallel.

D. Set up CodeBuild to generate a single ZIP artifact that contains all files. Enable S3 caching for the build process. Use AWS CodePipeline with a custom action to extract the files and reorganize the files into multiple artifacts in the S3 bucket. Configure the custom action to dynamically name the files based on the time of the build.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild supports multiple secondary artifacts in a buildspec, each with its own file set. Local source caching caches Git metadata and lets later builds retrieve only changes between commits, which is suited to frequent builds of a large Git repository. A build-ID-based artifact name provides a direct association between every S3 artifact and its generating build without requiring separate projects or post-build processing. LEARN MORE Build specification reference for CodeBuild Local caching - AWS CodeBuild

Local caching - AWS CodeBuild

questions.questionText: A company in a highly regulated industry is building an artifact with AWS CodeBuild and AWS CodePipeline. During the build process, the company must connect to an external authenticated API. The company’s DevOps engineer must encrypt the build outputs using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. The external API credentials must be reset monthly. The DevOps engineer has created a new AWS KMS key. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Store the API credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Update the key policy for the CodeBuild IAM service role to have access to the KMS key. Set CODEBUILD_KMS_KEY_ID as the new key ID.
B. Store the API credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Update the key policy for the CodePipeline IAM service role to have access to the KMS key. Add the key to the pipeline.
C. Store the API credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Update the key policy for the CodeBuild IAM service role to have access to the KMS key. Set CODEBUILD_KMS_KEY_ID as the new key ID.
D. Store the API credentials in AWS Secrets Manager. Update the key policy for the CodePipeline IAM service role to have access to the KMS key. Add the key to the pipeline.
questions.explanation: AWS Secrets Manager is designed to store sensitive API credentials and supports scheduled automatic rotation, including monthly schedules. AWS CodeBuild encrypts build output artifacts with the KMS key identified by CODEBUILD_KMS_KEY_ID; its service role must be permitted by the KMS key policy to use that customer managed key. LEARN MORE AWS CodeBuild environment variables AWS Secrets Manager rotation schedules

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) for all images in the company’s containerized infrastructure. The company uses pull-through cache functionality with the /external prefix to avoid throttling when retrieving images from external image registries. The company uses AWS Organizations for its accounts. Every image in the registry must be encrypted with a specific, pre-provisioned AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. The company’s internally created images already comply with this policy. However, cached external images use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed keys (SSE-S3). The company must remove the noncompliant cache repositories. The company must also implement a secure solution so that all new pull-through cache repositories are automatically encrypted with the required KMS key. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Configure AWS Config. Add a custom rule that uses Guard syntax. Write the rule to enable KMS encryption for new repositories.
B. Configure an ECR repository creation template for the prefix. Specify the KMS key. Wait for the repositories to repopulate.
C. Configure an SCP for all AWS accounts that requires all ECR repositories to be KMS encrypted.
D. Create a new Amazon EventBridge rule that triggers on all "ECR Pull Through Cache Action" events. Set AWS KMS as the rule target.
questions.explanation: Amazon ECR repository creation templates apply encryption settings when ECR creates repositories for pull-through cache actions. A template that matches the /external prefix and specifies the pre-provisioned KMS key ensures recreated and future cache repositories use that key. The template affects only newly created repositories, so the existing SSE-S3 repositories must be removed before they can be repopulated with compliant encryption. LEARN MORE Amazon ECR repository creation templates Create an Amazon ECR repository creation template
learnMore: Create an Amazon ECR repository creation template

questions.questionText: A DevOps team adds automated load- and stress-testing capabilities to a CI/CD pipeline by using AWS CodeBuild. The team uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster in a testing environment for load testing. The team configured the testing DB cluster with a minimum capacity of 1. The team uses 10 DB clusters in a production environment. All DB clusters are configured to automatically scale up to a maximum capacity of 15 Aurora Replicas. During load testing, the configuration of the Aurora DB cluster in the testing environment does not allow the cluster to scale quickly enough to satisfy transient demand, causing the load test to fail. The DevOps team must configure the DB cluster in the testing environment to satisfy the load-testing demand. Which solution will meet this requirement MOST cost-effectively?
options: A. Set the minimum capacity to 10. Reduce the scale-in cooldown period in the PRE_BUILD phase of the CodeBuild configuration.
B. Set the minimum capacity to 10 in the PRE_BUILD phase of the CodeBuild configuration. Reset the capacity to 1 in the POST_BUILD phase.
C. Set the minimum capacity to 10 in the POST_BUILD phase of the CodeBuild configuration. Reset the capacity to 1 in the same POST_BUILD phase.
D. Add an Amazon RDS Proxy in front of the testing Aurora DB cluster. Set the RDS Proxy endpoint in the PRE_BUILD phase of the CodeBuild configuration.
questions.explanation: Aurora Auto Scaling maintains the configured minimum number of Aurora Replicas. Increasing the testing cluster’s minimum capacity to 10 before load testing ensures that reader capacity is available for the transient workload, and resetting the minimum to 1 after the build minimizes the cost outside the test window. Scale-in cooldown settings do not accelerate initial scale-out, and RDS Proxy manages connections rather than pre-provisioning Aurora Replicas. LEARN MORE Amazon Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas Adding an auto scaling policy to an Amazon Aurora DB cluster
learnMore: Adding an auto scaling policy to an Amazon Aurora DB cluster

questions.questionText: A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage multiple AWS accounts across multiple OUs. The company plans to implement a comprehensive account-management solution and needs consistent baseline configurations. A DevOps engineer is developing a solution that automatically deploys AWS CloudFormation templates to new AWS accounts. The particular CloudFormation template deployed must differ according to the organizational unit (OU) into which each new account is placed. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Enable AWS Control Tower. Use Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) to deploy each CloudFormation template from a centralized account. Create a CodeCommit repository to store the entire configuration package, including the CloudFormation templates and a manifest file that maps each CloudFormation template to its corresponding OU.

B. Enable AWS Control Tower. Build a pipeline in AWS CodePipeline to deploy the CloudFormation deployment from a centralized account. Create a CodeCommit repository to store the entire configuration package, including the CloudFormation templates and a manifest file that maps each CloudFormation template to its corresponding OU. After the code is updated in CodeCommit, initiate the pipeline and deploy the CloudFormation templates to the new AWS accounts.

C. Store the CloudFormation templates in an Amazon S3 bucket by using a separate prefix for each AWS account. Create an AWS Lambda function that deploys a specific CloudFormation template to each new AWS account based on the prefix path that indicates where each template is located in the S3 bucket.

D. Store CloudFormation templates in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function that deploys a specific CloudFormation template to the new AWS accounts based on the OU each new account is in. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that matches "eventName": "CreateAccountResult" and "state": "SUCCEEDED." Set the Lambda function as the target of the EventBridge rule.
questions.explanation: Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) provides a managed, lifecycle-integrated mechanism for deploying CloudFormation customizations to accounts in specified OUs. Its configuration package includes CloudFormation templates and a manifest that defines OU deployment targets, and it automatically deploys resources when new accounts are created through AWS Control Tower Account Factory. This avoids maintaining separate custom pipeline or Lambda/EventBridge orchestration. LEARN MORE Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) overview The resources section of the CfCT manifest file
learnMore: Customizations for AWS Control Tower (CfCT) overview
The resources section of the CfCT manifest file

questions.questionText: A company keeps a large volume of data in Amazon S3 buckets across multiple AWS Regions and multiple AWS accounts. The company uses an AWS Organizations organization with all features enabled to manage those AWS accounts. A DevOps engineer must deliver an overview of potential security risks associated with the data stored in the S3 buckets. The company must be able to review the findings from one central location. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient manner?
options: A. Enable Amazon Macie in each AWS account and Region. Enable automated discovery and configure custom data identifiers. In each account, designate a central Region and configure AWS Security Hub to perform cross-Region aggregation.

B. Configure an account as the delegated Amazon Macie administrator account in the organization. Enable Macie in each Region in the delegated administrator account. Enable automated discovery and configure AWS Security Hub to perform cross-Region aggregation.

C. Designate an account as a central Amazon Macie administrator account and enable Macie in each Region. Send and accept a Macie membership request in each account in the organization. Configure AWS Security Hub to perform cross-Region aggregation in the administrator account.

D. Activate Amazon Macie in each Region in each AWS account and enable automated discovery. Designate a Macie administrator account. Send and accept membership invitations in all other accounts. In the administrator account, activate AWS Security Hub in each Region.
questions.explanation: A delegated Amazon Macie administrator can centrally manage Macie for an AWS Organization and enable automated sensitive data discovery across member accounts’ S3 buckets. Enabling Macie in each relevant Region ensures regional S3 data is assessed. AWS Security Hub cross-Region aggregation consolidates findings from linked Regions into a single home Region, providing a central review location without manually configuring Macie memberships in every account. LEARN MORE Amazon Macie administrator and member account relationships Configuring automated sensitive data discovery

questions.questionText: A company uses a Git provider that is compatible with AMS Code services that support credential authentication as version control for application code. The company wants to package the code and make it available when it is merged. The packaged code must be available as an upstream source for future packaged code. Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements?
options: A. Create an AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the Git provider credentials. Create an AWS CodeBuild project that integrates with the Git repository by using the Secrets Manager secret and a corresponding webhook.

B. Create an AWS Parameter Store secure string parameter that holds the Git provider credentials. Create an AWS CodeBuild project that integrates with the Git repository by using the secure string parameter and a corresponding webhook.

C. Create an AWS Secrets Manager secret that holds the Git provider credentials. Create an AWS CodeBuild project that define a Secrets Manager environment variable in the buildspec. Use the environment variable to configure a mirror of the Git repository during the install phase.
D. Create an AWS CodeArtifact domain and repository. Configure the AWS CodeBuild project to package the CodeBuild project's output artifact and upload the artifact to the CodeArtifact repository.
E. Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the AWS CodeBuild project to package and upload the artifact to the S3 bucket.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild can use a Secrets Manager secret for supported Git source-provider credentials and use a webhook to start builds from repository changes. AWS CodeArtifact repositories store published software packages and can be configured as upstream repositories, allowing future package builds to consume those packages through a repository endpoint. LEARN MORE Access your source provider in CodeBuild What is AWS CodeArtifact?

What is AWS CodeArtifact?

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodePipeline to automate the release process for a container-based application. The company hosts the application on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Each time the company updates its code, the pipeline automatically builds and deploys the new version. The company uses AWS CodeDeploy for some deployments. Some deployments create issues for many users. A DevOps engineer must update the application delivery solution to add a step that validates changes with a subset of customers. The updated solution must support reverting failed deployments. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Update the CodeDeploy deployment group to use a blue/green deployment strategy. Create a custom canary deployment configuration. Turn on rollback configuration overrides when alarm thresholds are met.
B. Update the CodeDeploy deployment group to use a canary deployment strategy. Turn on rollback configuration overrides in the deployment configuration.
C. Update the CodePipeline deployment configuration to use a canary deployment strategy. Turn on rollback configuration overrides in the pipeline.
D. Update the CodeDeploy deployment group to use a linear deployment strategy. Turn on rollback configuration overrides when alarm thresholds are met.
questions.explanation: For Amazon ECS deployments, CodeDeploy uses a blue/green deployment model and can apply a custom canary configuration to shift only an initial portion of traffic to the replacement task set before routing the remaining traffic. The CodeDeploy deployment group can also use CloudWatch alarm thresholds to automatically roll back by redeploying the last known good revision. LEARN MORE CodeDeploy blue/green deployments for Amazon ECS Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy
learnMore: CodeDeploy blue/green deployments for Amazon ECS
Working with deployment configurations in CodeDeploy

questions.questionText: A company uses AWS Systems Manager to manage a large fleet of Amazon EC2 Linux instances in its production AWS account. The EC2 instances must adhere to a list of compliance requirements. The company’s DevOps engineers developed Chef cookbooks to identify and remediate configuration deviations. The company does not want to manage Chef server and agent infrastructure. The DevOps engineers must configure the Chef cookbooks to run periodically on the EC2 instances. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association. Associate the AWS-ApplyChefRecipes document with all EC2 instances. Configure the association to retrieve the Chef cookbooks from a source repository and to run every hour.

B. Store the Chef agent installation package in an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure a Systems Manager Run Command to invoke the AWS-InstallApplication command on all instances and to run the repair action. Schedule the Run Command to run every hour.
C. Create a Systems Manager State Manager association that applies the AWS-RefreshAssociation document to all EC2 instances. Configure the association to run every hour.

D. Configure a Systems Manager patch policy to run the scan and install operation every hour. Create a patch baseline for the EC2 instances. Configure the instance IAM profile with permissions for patch operations.
questions.explanation: AWS Systems Manager State Manager can create a scheduled association for the AWS-ApplyChefRecipes document on Linux managed nodes. That document retrieves Chef cookbooks from supported repositories, runs the specified recipes, and can automatically install the Chef client, so a separate Chef server and managed agent infrastructure are unnecessary. An hourly association provides the required recurring compliance detection and remediation. LEARN MORE Creating associations that run Chef recipes Understanding how State Manager works
learnMore: Creating associations that run Chef recipes
Understanding how State Manager works

questions.questionText: A company uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Amazon EC2 launch type. The company requires all log data to be centralized in Amazon CloudWatch. The company’s ECS tasks include a LogConfiguration object that specifies awslogs as the log driver name. The company’s ECS tasks failed to deploy. An error message states that a missing permission caused the failure. The company verified that the IAM role used to launch container instances includes the logs:CreateLogGroup, logs:CreateLogStream, and logs:PutLogEvents permissions. Which solution will resolve the problem?
options: A. Add an IAM trust policy to the IAM role that establishes Amazon ECS as a trusted service.
B. Add the logs:PutDestination permission to the policy applied to the IAM role.
C. Remove the logs:CreateLogStream permission from the policy applied to the IAM role.
D. Add an IAM trust policy to the IAM role that establishes CloudWatch as a trusted service.
questions.explanation: An ECS task execution role must trust the Amazon ECS service so that ECS can assume it and perform the authorized actions on the task’s behalf. CloudWatch Logs API permissions do not by themselves permit role assumption; the role trust policy must include Amazon ECS as a trusted service principal. LEARN MORE IAM roles for Amazon ECS Send Amazon ECS logs to CloudWatch

Send Amazon ECS logs to CloudWatch

questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is updating an existing service in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The service uses the rolling update deployment type. All cluster updates are deployed by using AWS CloudFormation. Currently, no automated remediation takes place when a deployment fails. The service stays in a FAILED state until the DevOps team manually resolves the identified issues. The DevOps engineer must configure an automatic solution to remediate a deployment failure caused by the service task failing to start. The service must automatically roll back to its most recently completed deployment. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
options: A. Configure Amazon CloudWatch alarms that check the service's runtime metrics. Update the service deployment configuration to reference the new alarms.

B. Set an Amazon EventBridge rule that uses the SERVICE_DEPLOYMENT_FAILED event name. Add an AWS Lambda function target that rolls the service back to the most recent deployment that is in a COMPLETED state.
C. Update the service to use the ECS deployment circuit breaker failure detection support. Configure the service to roll back on failures.

D. Use an AWS CodeDeploy deployment group for all ECS service updates. Configure automatic rollbacks on the deployment group to roll back to the most recent successful deployment when a deployment fails.
questions.explanation: The Amazon ECS deployment circuit breaker detects failed rolling deployments when tasks cannot reach a steady state, including failures to start. With rollback enabled, ECS automatically restores the service to the most recent successfully completed deployment. This native ECS capability is supported for rolling-update services and can be declared through the ECS service deployment configuration in AWS CloudFormation. LEARN MORE How the Amazon ECS deployment circuit breaker detects failures AWS::ECS::Service DeploymentCircuitBreaker
learnMore: How the Amazon ECS deployment circuit breaker detects failures

questions.questionText: A software-as-a-service (SaaS) company needs to implement customer file uploads. Industry standards require the company to provide OpenAPI specifications to customers. The company will use Amazon S3 for file storage. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?
options: A. Create an Application Load Balancer. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster for the application to process uploads to Amazon S3. Generate the OpenAPI definitions separately.

B. Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API. Set up an AWS service integration for the upload. Create mapping templates to transform the requests and responses to match AWS API requirements. Export the OpenAPI definition.

C. Create an AWS Verified Access instance. Deploy an Amazon EC2 instance with the application to process uploads. Connect the instance as a network interface endpoint. Generate the OpenAPI definitions separately.

D. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Create a Lambda@Edge function as an authorizer. Configure the S3 bucket for the uploads. Write an AWS Lambda function to periodically export the OpenAPI definition from CloudFront.
questions.explanation: Amazon API Gateway REST APIs support AWS service integrations with Amazon S3, allowing upload requests to be mapped to the required S3 API format without running application servers or containers. API Gateway can export the configured REST API as an OpenAPI definition, so it meets both the upload and specification requirements with managed, pay-per-use services. questions.questionText: A company is developing a web application on AWS. The application uses AWS CodeConnections to access a Git repository. The company configures an AWS CodePipeline pipeline that automatically builds and deploys the application to a staging environment whenever code is pushed to the main branch. Bugs and integration issues occasionally occur in the main branch because no automated testing is integrated into the pipeline. The company wants tests to run automatically when code merges occur in the Git repository and wants to stop deployments from reaching the staging environment if any test fails. Tests can run for up to 20 minutes. Which solution meets these requirements?
options: A. Add an AWS CodeBuild action to the pipeline. Add a buildspec.yml file to the Git repository to define commands to run tests. Configure the pipeline to stop the deployment if a test fails.
B. Configure Git webhooks to initiate an AWS Lambda function during each code merge. Configure the Lambda function to run tests programmatically and to stop the pipeline if a test fails.

C. Configure AWS Batch to use Docker images of test environments. Integrate AWS Batch into the pipeline. Add an AWS Lambda function to the pipeline that submits the batch jobs and reverts the code merge if a test fails.
D. Configure the Git repository to push code to an Amazon S3 bucket during each code merge. Use S3 Event Notifications to initiate tests and to revert the code merge if a test fails.
questions.explanation: AWS CodeBuild provides build and test actions for CodePipeline and runs the commands specified in a buildspec file. A failed CodeBuild test action causes the pipeline to fail before its subsequent deployment action can run. CodeBuild supports the required 20-minute test duration, whereas an AWS Lambda invocation has a maximum timeout of 15 minutes. questions.questionText: A company uses AWS CodeDeploy to deploy an application to Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. The company configures the Auto Scaling group by using an EC2 launch template that references a custom AMI with the CodeDeploy agent installed. The company updates the AMI weekly, and replaces all EC2 instances with new instances launched from the updated AMI. The company requires each EC2 instance to have an application tag that identifies the application deployed on that instance. Currently, the company tags the EC2 instances manually. To deploy the application, the company creates a CodeDeploy application and a deployment group. The company sets a custom resource tag in the deployment group and configures the deployment group to target the Auto Scaling group. The company must ensure that every instance in the Auto Scaling group is tagged with the appropriate application tag. Which solution meets this requirement?
options: A. Create a tag specification in the EC2 launch template and set the resource type to applications. Configure the tag specification to apply the custom resource tag. Update the Auto Scaling group to use the most recent version of the EC2 launch template. Perform an instance refresh in the Auto Scaling group.

B. Configure the process that creates the custom AMI to tag the AMI with the custom resource tag. Create a new version of the AMI. Update the Auto Scaling group to use the new version of the AMI. Perform an instance refresh in the Auto Scaling group.

C. Configure the CodeDeploy deployment group to include a tag specification that applies the custom resource tag. Configure the Auto Scaling group to propagate the tag when instances are launched. Create a new deployment in the deployment group that specifies the EC2 instance IDs as target instances.

D. Create a tag specification in the EC2 launch template and set the resource type to instances. Configure the tag specification to apply the custom resource tag. Update the Auto Scaling group to use the most recent version of the EC2 launch template. Perform an instance refresh in the Auto Scaling group.
questions.explanation: An EC2 launch template tag specification with resource type instance applies the application tag to every EC2 instance created by the Auto Scaling group. Updating the group to use the launch-template version and performing an instance refresh replaces the existing fleet, ensuring all instances receive the tag. Launch-template tag specifications support instance, volume, network-interface, and spot-instances-request resource types; applications is not supported. CodeDeploy deployment-group tags are used to identify deployment targets, not to tag EC2 instances. LEARN MORE AWS::EC2::LaunchTemplate TagSpecification Tagging instances for deployment groups in CodeDeploy
learnMore: Tagging instances for deployment groups in CodeDeploy

questions.questionText: A company runs an application as an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) task that processes messages from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The ECS task operates on a schedule, processing the SQS queue every 10 minutes. A large volume of messages was delivered to the SQS queue. The application required several hours to process every message. The company's new service level objective (SLO) requires the application to process messages within 10 minutes of delivery. A DevOps engineer must configure the application to meet the SLO while minimizing idle running resources. Which solution satisfies these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?
options: A. Configure a step scaling policy for the ECS task. Configure the step scaling policy to use the ECSServiceAverageMemoryUtilization metric. Set the maximum number of tasks to equal the number of messages the application receives at peak hours.

B. Configure a target tracking scaling policy for the ECS task. Calculate the number of messages for each task by using the SQS ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible metric and the ECS RunningTaskCount metric. Scale the number of tasks based on the calculated attribute.

C. Create a scheduled scaling policy to increase the number of ECS tasks available during peak volume periods. Set the schedule as a cron for the application's peak hours. Set the maximum number of tasks to equal the number of messages the application receives at peak hours.

D. Create a predictive scaling policy to increase the number of available ECS tasks during peak volume periods. Configure the predictive scaling policy to use the ECSServiceAverageCPUUtilization metric. Set the maximum number of tasks to equal the number of messages the application receives at peak hours.
questions.explanation: A target tracking policy using a custom backlog-per-task metric scales ECS tasks from the actual amount of immediately available SQS work and scales them back in as the backlog drains. The backlog-per-task calculation is ApproximateNumberOfMessagesVisible / RunningTaskCount; its target can be set from the acceptable processing time and each task's message-processing rate. This directly accommodates bursty arrivals while avoiding capacity that remains idle outside demand. LEARN MORE Create a target tracking scaling policy for Application Auto Scaling using metric math Amazon ECS service utilization metrics

questions.questionText: A company runs an application on 20 Amazon EC2 instances. The application uses the AWS CodeDeploy CodeDeployDefault.HalfAtATime deployment configuration to deploy application updates to the instances. During recent deployments, the load has exceeded the capacity of the available instances. Consequently, the application has become unstable during deployments. A DevOps engineer must ensure that at least 75% of instances remain available at all times and that deployments finish as quickly as possible. Which solution satisfies these requirements?
options: A. Modify the deployment group to use the CodeDeployDefault.OneAtATime deployment configuration.
B. Modify the CodeDeploy deployment group to use a MinimumHealthyHosts deployment configuration with a FLEET_PERCENT value of 75.
C. Modify the CodeDeploy deployment group to use a MinimumHealthyHosts deployment configuration with a FLEET_PERCENT value of 25.
D. Modify the CodeDeploy deployment group to use a TimeBasedLinear deployment configuration with a LinearInterval value of 5 minutes and a LinearPercentage value of 25.
questions.explanation: For EC2/on-premises deployments, a CodeDeploy MinimumHealthyHosts setting defines the number or percentage of instances that must remain healthy throughout a deployment. FLEET_PERCENT with a value of 75 keeps at least 75% of the fleet healthy; with 20 instances, this permits deployment to up to 5 instances concurrently, the fastest batch size that preserves the required availability. questions.questionText: A DevOps engineer is developing a photo-sharing website that lets users upload photos and view photos shared by other users. Users upload photos to an Amazon S3 bucket by using presigned URLs. The DevOps engineer must ensure that photos are scanned for malware before the website makes the photos available to other users. Which combination of steps meets these requirements?
options: A. Enable Amazon GuardDuty S3 Protection. Create an AWS Lambda function to process S3 Protection findings and block access to any referenced objects.
B. Create a bucket policy for the S3 bucket. Update the IAM role that the website uses to restrict access to uploaded photos by using tag-based access control (TBAC).
C. Create a resource-based policy for the S3 bucket. Restrict access to uploaded photos by using the aws:SecureTransport condition key.
D. Enable Amazon Macie. Create an AWS Lambda function to process Macie findings and delete any referenced objects that contain malware.
E. Enable Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 with object tagging.
questions.explanation: Amazon GuardDuty Malware Protection for S3 automatically scans newly uploaded S3 objects. When object tagging is enabled, it applies the GuardDutyMalwareScanStatus tag with the scan result. Tag-based access control in the S3 bucket policy and the website's IAM role can allow the website to return only objects whose tag indicates that no threats were found, preventing access to unscanned or malicious uploads.
